@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 2 — Night Sightings]{Scene 2 — Night Sightings} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-g-02-high-street-market-square]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 3 — Gideon Tumble’s Flat]{Scene 3 — Gideon Tumble’s Flat} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-05-gideon-tumble-flat]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 4 — The Newspaper Office]{Scene 4 — The Newspaper Office} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-06-brandmere-crier-office]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 5 — Veronique’s Offer]{Scene 5 — Veronique’s Offer} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-06-brandmere-crier-office]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-02]{Duckworth Pym}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.gideon-tumble]{Gideon Tumble}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.mascot-revenant-mortimer-pell]{The Murder King Costume}, Lettice Quayle
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S02]{Gideon Tumble’s Notebook}

Synopsis

Mortimer Pell wore the Murder King costume for twenty-two years—waving at children, posing for portraits, shouting the slogan Have It Our Way! from the drive-thru moat. Two weeks ago he died inside it. The costume was hung up in storage, and now it isn’t: every night it walks out of the Grand Throne Restaurant and wanders Coronation Square, waving at nobody.

The party is hired to restore “brand quietude” before the Coronation Day promotion. At the restaurant they meet shift lead Duckworth Pym and, unexpectedly, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}, Crown & Cleaver’s Vice President, who wants the costume “retired with dignity”—and anything found inside it returned to her, unread.

A night hunt across Coronation Square, a visit to the flat Mortimer shared with his understudy Gideon Tumble, and a midnight fight at the offices of the Brandmere Crier reveal the truth: the costume is not haunted by a ghost but animated by the brand itself—an egregore of the real King Aldric the Unkind, who was murdered four hundred years ago and whose murder was trademarked. Mortimer found out. Somebody killed him for it.

Background — DM Only

Four hundred years ago, King Aldric the Unkind ruled the land where Brandmere now stands. His own knight, Ossian Cleave, murdered him—then sold the killing, the crown and the very idea of “the King” to a small grey clerk named Tallis Vend, who registered all of it in the Grand Ledger. Crown & Cleaver Holdings was the first company Creation & Company ever owned, and “Murder King” is, legally, the trademark of a regicide.

Mortimer Pell, a career mascot performer, got curious about the history of “his” king. He spent two years in the Guild Records and found a copy of the original trademark deed, naming Baron Ossian Cleave as the vendor. He copied it, and talked about it to his flatmate and understudy, Gideon Tumble, who wrote everything down in his own notebook. Mortimer told the Crier. Two days later he died in the costume, of what the Murder King incident form calls “a sudden end-of-shift”. (Crown & Cleaver cleaners smothered him in the costume storage room. Gideon heard it from the corridor and has been hiding ever since.)

The costume walks because the brand is alive. Advertising this old—four centuries of a slogan shouted at crowds—grows an egregore, and the Murder King egregore is wearing the costume Mortimer died in. It half believes it is Aldric. It is looking for the evidence of its own murder, and for the man who copied it. It regains strength whenever anyone says its name.

Running This Mission

  • Play the first half as a comedy ghost-hunt and the second as a murder mystery. The turn is Gideon’s notebook.
  • The costume is not evil; it is a confused, proud king made of slogans. Let it be talked to. The best ending is a Persuasion win at the Crier.
  • Veronique Salt is the star of this mission. She is charming, precise and dangerous. She should leave the players unsure whether she is a villain or a patron. (She is both.)
  • Saying “Murder King” heals the costume. Tell the players once, then enjoy watching them try not to say it.

Threads In and Out

  • In: the recall memo signed by V. Salt in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S01]{S01}.
  • Out: Veronique becomes the recurring face of corporate opposition; the deed names Baron Cleave (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S15]{S15}); Mortimer resurfaces at Wight Castle (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05]{S05}); the notebook voids Clause 11 (Disclosure) in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S24]{S24}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Pip is waiting for you at the Warren with a job slip and a plate of carrot cake. “Great second job! Very visible!” he says, then lowers his voice. “Murder King’s mascot has been—er—going for walks. At night. On his own. There’s a bonus if it’s sorted before Coronation Day!”

He slides the slip across. Under the fee, in a different hand, someone has written: Please hurry. — D. Pym.

pages.name: Scene 1 — The Grand Throne Restaurant
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-04-murder-king-grand-throne]{Open battlemap}
When: Late afternoon, the day before the promotion
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-02]{Duckworth Pym}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S02|Murder King Incident Form 19-C]{Murder King Incident Form 19-C} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S02|Murder King Incident Form 19-C]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S02|Veronique Salt’s Business Card]{Veronique Salt’s Business Card} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S02|Veronique Salt’s Business Card]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Grand Throne Restaurant is a castle. A small one, made mostly of painted plywood over real stone, but a castle: corner towers with conical red roofs, crenellations, banners, and a moat full of murky water where carriages—no, boats—queue at a drive-thru window. A wooden drawbridge carries you over the water and into a great hall of flagstones, long feast tables and a red carpet that runs straight to a throne-shaped ordering counter.

A halfling in a paper crown and a fixed, enormous smile hurries over. “Contractors! Welcome to Murder King, where you can Have It Our Way!” The smile does not move. His eyes do. “Please come to the back. Please.”

DM Description

Duckworth Pym, the shift lead, takes the party to the costume storage room behind the great hall. He explains, through his mandatory smile: Mortimer died in the costume two weeks ago, during a closing shift. The costume was cleaned and hung on its rack. That night it was gone. It came back before dawn, dripping moat water. Every night since, it walks out—through locked doors—and wanders the Square.

The storage room still shows the evidence: an empty hook on the costume rack, a dark stain on the floorboards that the cleaners missed, scratches on the inside of the door (Mortimer tried to get out), and a faint golden shimmer that clings to the empty hook.

Halfway through Duckworth’s explanation, a black carriage with crimson wheels draws up on the drawbridge. @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt} steps out, walks in as if she owns the building—she does, through three subsidiaries—and introduces herself. She wants the costume “retired with dignity”. She wants anything found inside it, or in Mortimer’s belongings, “returned to me personally, unread”. She hands each character a business card and pays the Copper fee upfront, in full, without the 30% cut. (This is a test. Pip will be thrilled.)

Features of the Area

Great Hall
Long feast tables with red cloths, a kids’ party corner with balloons, banners of the crowned King, and a red carpet runner from the doors to the throne counter.
Throne Counter
A marble dais with a gilded throne behind the till where the costume used to sit for portraits. Duckworth keeps a crossbow under the register “for drive-thru disputes”.
Costume Storage
Racks of spare crowns, capes and mascot heads, two crates of Coronation Day merchandise, an empty hook, a stain and scratches inside the door.
Duckworth’s Office
Desk, safe, weapon rack. The incident form lies on the desk.
The Drive-Thru Moat
Boats queue at the window on the east side. The moat is 10 feet deep and very cold.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-02]{Duckworth Pym}. Policy requires him to smile at all times on shift. He has been smiling for two weeks straight. He liked Mortimer. He will whisper the truth if the party gets him somewhere private: “Those weren’t our cleaners. They came in a black carriage the night he died.”
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}. Never raises her voice. Uses first names immediately. Writes notes with a different pen each time. She is genuinely curious about the party—she read the courier’s grey book after S01.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Examining the storage room[[/check skill=inv dc=12]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=inv dc=12|Search the costume storage]{Request}The stain, the scratches, and the golden shimmer on the hook. On 16+: a thread of crimson fabric snagged on a nail—not costume fabric; a fine tailored wool (Crown & Cleaver cleaners’ uniforms).
Identifying the shimmer[[/check skill=arc dc=13]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=arc dc=13|What is this golden residue?]{Request}It is not necromancy. It is the residue of belief—something made by many minds thinking the same thing. An egregore.
Reading Duckworth behind the smile[[/check skill=ins dc=11]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=ins dc=11|What is Duckworth not saying?]{Request}He is frightened and grieving. He knows the “cleaners” were not his staff.
Reading Veronique[[/check skill=ins dc=18]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=ins dc=18|What does Veronique want?]{Request}She is not frightened. She already knows what happened to Mortimer, and she is more interested in the party than the costume.
Recalling history[[/check skill=his dc=14]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=his dc=14|What do you know about the Murder King?]{Request}The mascot is based on Aldric the Unkind, a tyrant who died four centuries ago. “Murder King” was originally an insult—his enemies’ name for him.

Lines to Steal

Duckworth: “Welcome to Murder King, where you can Have It Our Way. That’s—sorry—that’s a reflex.”
Veronique: “Retire him with dignity. And anything you find, bring to me. Unread. I would hate for you to be burdened with something.”
Veronique: “You’re the ones from the flagship. The forgery was very good, by the way.”

Developments

  • Veronique pays upfront. If the party accepts, note it: she now considers them “on retainer”.
  • Duckworth gives the party Mortimer’s address: the flat he shared with “Gideon, his understudy—nobody’s seen Gideon for two weeks.”
  • The costume will walk tonight at the second bell after closing.

Scaling & Pacing

If the party wants a fight early, the costume rises from the moat as they leave; it flees after one round.

pages.name: Scene 2 — Night Sightings
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-g-02-high-street-market-square]{Coronation Square (use the High Street & Market Square map)}
When: That night, after closing
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.mascot-revenant-mortimer-pell]{the Murder King costume}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.esmond-tallow-pryce]{Lord Mayor Esmond Tallow-Pryce (optional)}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S02|Coronation Day Promotion Flyer]{Coronation Day Promotion Flyer} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S02|Coronation Day Promotion Flyer]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Coronation Square is draped for tomorrow’s promotion: bunting in red and gold, a stage half-built in front of the fountain, and posters on every lamp post showing a grinning cartoon king. The stalls are shuttered. The lamps are low.

Then you see it. A tall figure in a plush red robe and a huge, foam-headed crown, its painted smile fixed and enormous, walks slowly across the empty square. It stops beside a shuttered stall, turns to face nobody at all, and waves—a slow, regal wave—at an empty street. Then it moves on, toward a house where a banner reads Happy Birthday, Tomkin! above a door with no party behind it.

DM Description

Run a night-hunt skill challenge. The costume follows a strange route: it visits the sites of children’s parties that aren’t happening (because Mortimer used to perform at them), waves at the drive-thru moat, and finally stands for a long time outside the Brandmere Crier office on the corner, staring at the darkened windows.

The party needs four successes before three failures to track it without being noticed. Each failure means it notices them and vanishes into a wall, a fountain or a shadow, reappearing elsewhere.

Witnesses: a night-watchman (“It looked at my lantern like it was looking for something”), a baker up early (“It knocked on the Crier’s door, polite as you like”), and a child at a window (“He waved at me. He looked sad.”). If the Lord Mayor’s carriage passes (optional), Esmond Tallow-Pryce leans out and shouts, “Splendid brand activation!”

Features of the Area

The half-built stage
Scaffolding, a throne prop and a stack of foam crowns for tomorrow’s giveaway.
The fountain
The costume stands in it once, up to its knees, and says, in a deep voice, “My kingdom.”
The Crier corner
The costume’s last stop. It raises a hand to knock, then lowers it.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Tracking the costume[[/check skill=sur dc=12]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=sur dc=12|Track the costume across the Square]{Request}1 success.
Staying unseen[[/check skill=ste dc=12]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=ste dc=12|Follow without being noticed]{Request}1 success; failure counts toward the 3.
Interviewing witnesses[[/check skill=per dc=11]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=per dc=11|Ask the night-folk what they saw]{Request}1 success and a clue (see above).
Predicting the route[[/check skill=inv dc=14]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=inv dc=14|Where will it go next?]{Request}1 success: it is following a performer’s booking schedule—someone’s old appointment diary.
Saying the name (accidentally)—Anyone who says “Murder King” within 30 feet heals it 5 hp and it turns to look at them.

Developments

  • Success: the party sees the costume knock at the Crier and learns it is “looking for something”. They gain advantage on the first Persuasion check in Scene 4.
  • Failure: the costume vanishes; the party still finds the Crier connection from the baker.
  • Either way, the trail points to Mortimer’s flat and the reporter.

Complications

  • Three Crown & Cleaver cleaners are also watching the Square from a carriage. A character with passive Perception 14 spots them. They leave if confronted.

Scaling & Pacing

Use 3 successes before 3 failures for a quicker scene.

pages.name: Scene 3 — Gideon Tumble’s Flat
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-05-gideon-tumble-flat]{Open battlemap}
When: The next morning (or that same night)
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.gideon-tumble]{Gideon Tumble}, Mrs Agatha Brindle, landlady
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S02|Gideon Tumble’s Notebook (extract)]{Gideon Tumble’s Notebook (extract)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S02|Gideon Tumble’s Notebook (extract)]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S02|Transcription of the Deed of Aldric]{Transcription of the Deed of Aldric} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S02|Transcription of the Deed of Aldric]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The flat is up four flights of a crooked stair above a cobbler’s on Bellwether Lane. The landlady, Mrs Brindle, a stout woman in curlers with a ring of keys like a jailer’s, sniffs at your badges. “Mortimer’s rooms. Paid up to the end of the month, so mind you don’t touch anything. And if you see that Gideon, tell him he owes me for the milk.”

She unlocks the door. The rooms smell of greasepaint and cold tea. Posters of the cartoon King cover every wall. A spare foam crown sits on the mantel. And from behind the wardrobe in the bedroom comes a very small, very frightened sniff.

DM Description

Gideon Tumble—Mortimer’s flatmate, understudy and friend—has been hiding here for two weeks, living on biscuits and terror. He saw Mortimer go into the costume storage room the night he died, heard the struggle through the door and saw three people in crimson-trimmed uniforms leave by the back. He thinks they will come for him next. He is right.

Gideon’s notebook is the treasure. In it he copied everything Mortimer found: a transcription of the four-hundred-year-old trademark deed (“The Person, Title, Crown and Death of Aldric, called the Unkind, conveyed by Ossian Cleave to Tallis Vend, Clerk, for consideration”), notes in Mortimer’s words—“The King’s not a mascot. He was real. Somebody killed him and bought the murder.”—and an appointment: Lettice Quayle, the Crier, midnight tonight. Gideon was going to keep it for Mortimer.

If the party is kind to Gideon, he gives them the notebook and begs them to go with him to the Crier. If they frighten him, he bolts down the stairs and the party must catch him (and the notebook).

Features of the Area

Living room
Fireplace, sagging sofa, a desk covered in clippings and a crown on the mantel.
Bedroom
Two narrow beds, a wardrobe (Gideon is behind it), costume racks.
Study
Mortimer’s conspiracy board—clippings, a map of the old palace site and red string joining “Aldric”, “Cleave” and a question mark labelled “C&C?”.
Balcony
Overlooks Bellwether Lane. Gideon’s escape route if he panics.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.gideon-tumble]{Gideon Tumble}. A gangly young man with a nervous laugh and an actor’s habit of quoting lines. He keeps saying “Mort would know what to do.” He will not go to the Crier alone.
Mrs Brindle. Hard, nosy and secretly fond of “her boys”. She noticed the black carriage too.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Coaxing Gideon out[[/check skill=per dc=10]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=per dc=10|Coax Gideon out from behind the wardrobe]{Request}He comes out and talks. Failure by 5+: he bolts for the balcony.
Catching a bolting Gideon[[/check skill=ath dc=13]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=ath dc=13|Catch Gideon on the balcony]{Request}Caught before he falls (or jumps) into the lane.
Reading the conspiracy board[[/check skill=inv dc=13]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=inv dc=13|Make sense of Mortimer’s board]{Request}The trail runs from the King to Baron Ossian Cleave to “the Clerk”—and the Crier appointment is circled in red.
Reading the deed copy[[/check skill=his dc=15]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=his dc=15|Study the deed transcription]{Request}It is a real legal formula of four centuries ago. The vendor is Ossian Cleave; the buyer is “Tallis Vend, Clerk”—a name that appears nowhere else in any history book.

Lines to Steal

Gideon: “He wasn’t a mascot to Mort. He was a person. He was a murdered person.”
Gideon: “Midnight at the Crier. Mort’s appointment. I said I’d keep it. I didn’t say I’d keep it alone.”
Mrs Brindle: “Black carriage, red wheels. Didn’t like the look of it. Never trust a carriage that clean.”

Developments

  • The party obtains Gideon Tumble’s Notebook (the Receipt).
  • Gideon joins the party for Scene 4 unless they forbid it.
  • The Crown & Cleaver cleaners know where Gideon is. They will try to collect him and the notebook at the Crier.

Scaling & Pacing

No combat unless the cleaners arrive early (use the 3 thugs if the table wants action).

pages.name: Scene 4 — The Newspaper Office
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-06-brandmere-crier-office]{Open battlemap}
When: Midnight
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.mascot-revenant-mortimer-pell]{the Murder King costume}, Lettice Quayle, reporter, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.gideon-tumble]{Gideon Tumble}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.thug]{Crown & Cleaver cleaners}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S02|Crier Front-Page Proof]{Crier Front-Page Proof} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S02|Crier Front-Page Proof]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Brandmere Crier never quite sleeps. Lamps burn in the newsroom; the great presses stand silent in the back, inked rollers glistening. A sharp-faced woman in ink-stained cuffs looks up from a desk piled with copy. “Pell’s appointment? You’re late. So is he.”

Then every lamp in the room gutters. The front door opens by itself. In the doorway stands the King—vast, plush, crowned, smiling its painted smile—and it says, in a voice like a herald’s trumpet played underwater: “WHO HAS MY PROOF?”

DM Description

The costume has come for the evidence of its own murder. It does not understand the difference between Mortimer and Aldric, between the notebook and itself. It attacks whoever holds the notebook—or, if no one does, the reporter, Lettice Quayle, whom it believes is going to “sell my death again”.

It fights like a king: proud, cruel and theatrical, declaiming as it strikes. It regains 5 hp whenever anyone within 30 feet says “Murder King”. Lettice will say it. Repeatedly. (“Murder King mascot attacks Crier—that’s a front page!”)

The costume can be talked down. A character who shows it the notebook and makes the case that Mortimer’s death harms the brand—that the King’s own murder is being sold again—can make a DC 14 Persuasion check. Three successes before two failures (advantage if the party succeeded in Scene 2, or if Gideon speaks on Mortimer’s behalf) and the costume collapses like empty cloth, leaving a faint golden light that drifts away northward toward Old Gate. (That light is Mortimer. See S05.)

In round 3, three Crown & Cleaver cleaners arrive through the back to collect Gideon and the notebook.

Features of the Area

Newsroom
Desks, scattered copy, a clock. Desks give half cover.
Press Room
Four great presses and a conveyor. A creature shoved into a running press takes 2d10 bludgeoning damage. Paper rolls can be toppled as a bonus action to create difficult terrain.
Editor’s Office & Archive
Filing walls of back issues—including a 22-year-old front page about Mortimer’s first day in the costume.
Front Office
Counter and benches; the costume enters here.

Playing the NPCs

Lettice Quayle. Fearless, tactless, brilliant. She wants the story more than her life. If saved, she becomes a recurring press contact who can publish the party’s good deeds (proof against Credit Theft).
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.mascot-revenant-mortimer-pell]{The Costume}. Speaks in slogans and royal decrees: “KNEEL.” “HAVE IT OUR WAY.” “I WAS A KING BEFORE YOUR GRANDMOTHERS’ GRANDMOTHERS.” In its quieter moments: “I am looking for the man who wore me.”

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Talking the costume down (×3 needed)[[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=per dc=14|Convince the King that his murder is being sold again]{Request}Each success makes it hesitate; three collapses it. Advantage with the notebook in hand, from Gideon, or from Scene 2 success.
Stopping Lettice saying the name[[/check skill=itm dc=12]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=itm dc=12|Make Lettice stop saying it]{Request}She stops for 2 rounds.
Spotting the cleaners[[/check skill=prc dc=13]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=prc dc=13|Who is coming through the back?]{Request}You see them in time to act first.
Resisting the royal presence[[/save ability=wis dc=11]] @FWSave[S02|ability=wis dc=11|KNEEL.]{Request}On a failure the character is frightened of the costume until the end of their next turn.

Lines to Steal

The King: “WHO HAS MY PROOF?”
The King: “They sold my death. They sold it twice.”
Lettice: “Murder King mascot attacks the Crier! That’s a front page! Oh—sorry—did I just—?”

Developments

  • If the costume is talked down, the golden light drifts away. If destroyed, it bursts into foam and gold dust; the light still drifts away (more slowly, and sadder).
  • If the cleaners get the notebook, the party must chase them through the presses (they flee toward a black carriage).
  • Lettice survives: the party earns the star; she promises a sympathetic story. Lettice dies: no star.

Complications

  • The presses start on their own when the costume enters, printing tomorrow’s front page over and over: HAVE IT OUR WAY.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 1: costume at 45 hp, cleaners arrive one per round. Level 2: as written. 5+ players: add a fourth cleaner and a second costume arm (it has an extra slam).

pages.name: Scene 5 — Veronique’s Offer
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-06-brandmere-crier-office]{Open battlemap}
When: Just before dawn
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.gideon-tumble]{Gideon Tumble}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S02|Veronique Salt’s Business Card]{Veronique Salt’s Business Card} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S02|Veronique Salt’s Business Card]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The presses fall silent. Ink drips. Lettice Quayle is already writing. And in the open doorway, where a moment ago there was nothing, stands Veronique Salt in a crimson coat, pulling off her gloves one finger at a time.

“Well,” she says. “That was very dignified. Thank you.” She extends a gloved hand, palm up. “The notebook, please.”

DM Description

Veronique arrives the moment the fight ends—she was in the black carriage outside. She asks for the notebook politely.

If the party gives it to her, she thanks them, reads one page with a faint smile, and burns it in a lamp before their eyes (they may already have copied it—if so, a copy still counts as the Receipt). If they refuse, she smiles and says, “Then keep it safe. You’ll find it’s worth more to you than to me.” She does not mean it kindly—but she also means it.

Either way, she pays any outstanding fee and the Coronation Day bonus herself, and asks what happened to “the light”. If the party tells her it went north toward Old Gate, she is quiet for a moment, then says, “Wight Castle. Of course.”

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}. This is her audition of the party. She wants to know whether they can be bought, scared or charmed. She respects all three answers differently. She never threatens directly.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Reading Veronique[[/check skill=ins dc=16]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=ins dc=16|What is Veronique really after?]{Request}She does not care about the notebook. She cares that the party read it, and what they will do about it. She is measuring them.
Bluffing that there is no notebook[[/check skill=dec dc=18]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=dec dc=18|There was never any notebook]{Request}She laughs, delighted, and lets it go.
Asking about Baron Cleave[[/check skill=per dc=15]] @FWCheck[S02|skill=per dc=15|Who is Ossian Cleave?]{Request}“My employer’s employer. Do be careful with that name.”

Lines to Steal

Veronique: “Then keep it safe. You’ll find it’s worth more to you than to me.”
Veronique: “Wight Castle. Of course. They never let anyone go.”

Developments

  • Record whether the party kept the notebook. It is the Receipt for Clause 11.
  • Gideon is safe if the party kept him close; otherwise he vanishes (he resurfaces at the Tankard & Tallow in S08).
  • Pip adds a star if Lettice lived.

Scaling & Pacing

No combat. If the party attacks Veronique, she simply steps back into the dark and the carriage drives away; she is CR 14 and will not fight at Copper grade.

← @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 4 — The Newspaper Office]{Scene 4 — The Newspaper Office} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Twist, Rewards & Aftermath]{Twist, Rewards & Aftermath} → · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|DM Overview]{Overview}

pages.name: Opposition & Tactics
pages.html:
GM ONLY

The costume is the main threat. The cleaners are corporate muscle and flee when two of them drop.

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.mascot-revenant-mortimer-pell]{The Murder King Costume (Mascot Revenant)} ×1

Statistics: Use the Mascot Revenant (Mortimer Pell) stat block. Brand Egregore: regains 5 hp at the start of any turn in which a creature within 30 ft said “Murder King”.

Targets whoever holds the notebook, then the reporter. Uses grand, sweeping attacks and moves to stand on desks (it likes height—it is a king). When reduced below half, it bellows “KNEEL” (Wisdom save) and tries to grab the notebook and flee. It can be talked down at any point (see Scene 4).

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 2 — Night Sightings]{Scene 2 — Night Sightings}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 4 — The Newspaper Office]{Scene 4 — The Newspaper Office}

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.thug]{Crown & Cleaver Cleaners} ×3

Statistics: Thugs in crimson-trimmed grey uniforms, carrying coshes and sacks.

They want Gideon and the notebook, in that order, and will not kill anyone in front of witnesses if they can help it. They retreat when two of them fall. A captured cleaner says only, “We work for the Vice President’s office,” and then, very frightened, “not her—above her.”

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 4 — The Newspaper Office]{Scene 4 — The Newspaper Office}

Encounter Scaling

  • Level 1 / 3 characters: two cleaners, costume 45 hp.
  • Level 2 / 5 characters: four cleaners, costume gains a second slam.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}

Crown & Cleaver’s Vice President of Hostile Acquisitions

Appearance
Tall, immaculate, in a crimson suit and long coat; dark hair pinned with a silver pen; never the same pen twice.
Voice & Manner
Low, warm, unhurried. Uses first names. Pauses before the important word.
Wants
The chair above hers—Baron Cleave’s—and then the one above that.
Fears
Being owned, though she will never admit it.
Secret
She knows exactly how Mortimer died and who ordered it (Cleave’s office). She did not stop it. She is gathering leverage against her own employer and is beginning to wonder whether these contractors could be leverage.

“Retire him with dignity.” “Then keep it safe.” “The forgery was very good, by the way.”

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 1 — The Grand Throne Restaurant]{Scene 1 — The Grand Throne Restaurant}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 5 — Veronique’s Offer]{Scene 5 — Veronique’s Offer}

Later: Hires the party in S05; manipulates them throughout; calls the EGM in S23.

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-02]{Duckworth Pym}

Halfling shift lead at the Grand Throne Restaurant

Appearance
Small, round, paper crown, a smile so fixed it looks painful.
Voice & Manner
Bright, chirpy, policy-correct—then a desperate whisper.
Wants
Justice for Mortimer, and to stop smiling.
Secret
He keeps a crossbow under the register and is braver than he looks.

“Have It Our Way! Sorry. Reflex.”

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 1 — The Grand Throne Restaurant]{Scene 1 — The Grand Throne Restaurant}

Later: Returns in S15 during the Throne Tower siege.

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.gideon-tumble]{Gideon Tumble}

Mortimer’s flatmate and understudy; the witness

Appearance
Gangly, twenty-something, curly hair, an actor’s scarf, smudged greasepaint he hasn’t washed off in two weeks.
Voice & Manner
Fast, nervous, quotes plays when frightened.
Wants
To keep Mortimer’s appointment and not die.
Fears
Black carriages with red wheels.
Secret
He heard the murder through the storage room door and did nothing. He hates himself for it.

“Mort would know what to do.” “He wasn’t a mascot to Mort. He was a person.”

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 3 — Gideon Tumble’s Flat]{Scene 3 — Gideon Tumble’s Flat}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 4 — The Newspaper Office]{Scene 4 — The Newspaper Office}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 5 — Veronique’s Offer]{Scene 5 — Veronique’s Offer}

Later: Can be found at the Tankard & Tallow in S08; testifies in S24 if alive.

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.mascot-revenant-mortimer-pell]{The Murder King Costume}

The brand egregore of King Aldric, wearing the suit Mortimer died in

Appearance
Eight feet of red plush and gold foam, a painted grin, an oversized crown, a cape dripping moat water.
Voice & Manner
A herald’s trumpet played underwater; slogans and royal decrees.
Wants
Its proof. Its kingdom. The man who wore it.
Secret
Part of it is Mortimer. When it collapses, that part goes to Wight Castle.

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 2 — Night Sightings]{Scene 2 — Night Sightings}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 4 — The Newspaper Office]{Scene 4 — The Newspaper Office}

Later: The real Aldric returns in S15.

Lettice Quayle

Reporter, the Brandmere Crier

Appearance
Sharp face, ink-stained cuffs, pencil behind each ear.
Voice & Manner
Rapid-fire questions; never waits for answers.
Wants
The story.
Secret
She has two years of letters from Mortimer locked in the Crier archive.

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02|Scene 4 — The Newspaper Office]{Scene 4 — The Newspaper Office}

Later: A recurring press ally; can publicise the party’s deeds to defeat Credit Theft.

pages.name: Twist, Rewards & Aftermath
pages.html:
GM ONLY

The Twist

The costume can be talked to. It believes it is the King. It does not know it is only advertising. A party that tells it the truth—gently—gives it the only peace it can have. The golden light that leaves the collapsed costume is what remains of Mortimer Pell; it goes to Wight Castle, where the Restaurant Necromancy Group “rehires” him under a posthumous employment clause.

Rewards

  • 100 gp less 30% (70 gp)—or the full 100 gp plus the 50 gp bonus if Veronique paid upfront.
  • One star if the costume was stopped without the reporter dying.
  • Lettice Quayle as a press contact (if she lived).
  • Gideon Tumble’s gratitude (if he lived).

Receipt — @FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S02]{Gideon Tumble’s Notebook}

Gideon Tumble’s Notebook. A copy of the four-hundred-year-old deed and a mascot performer’s notes on the real King Aldric. Proof that Creation & Company concealed how it acquired its first kingdom.Voids Clause 11 — Disclosure in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.finalcontract]{the Final Contract}.

If Veronique burned the original and the party made no copy, the Receipt can be recovered from Lettice’s archive (Mortimer’s letters) in S08 or later.

@FWReceipt[S02|fw.item.receipt.S02]{Award Receipt & announce}

Outcomes

If the party…Then…
talked the costume downMortimer’s light reaches Wight Castle intact; in S05 he remembers the party fondly and helps them.
destroyed the costumeMortimer still reaches Wight Castle, but confused and colder; in S05 he helps only if promised a good review.
gave Veronique the notebookShe burns it. She now thinks the party is useful and obedient.
kept the notebookShe files the party as “independent” and starts courting them.

Forward

  • Veronique becomes the recurring face of corporate opposition.
  • The deed names Baron Ossian Cleave, setting up @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S15]{S15 — Long Live the King}.
  • The idea that brands have living egregores returns with Krispy Kobold’s HOT sign and McGuffin’s toys.
  • Mortimer resurfaces at Wight Castle in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05]{S05 — The Crown Jewels}.

Contract gradeSilver (Level 2) — the party’s first Silver

Fee150 gp, less 30% (105 gp)
Contact on siteBettina Soft, manager
DeliverableLocate and return the brand mascot. Team member matters are an internal HR concern.

Show this page, or send it to chat, when Pip hands over the job slip. @FWChat[cover]{Send contract to chat}

pages.name: DM Overview
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS03 · Act I
Grade / LevelSilver · Level 2
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-04]{Gelatinous Cube} (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-12]{Sweet Covenant Confectionery})
Session length1 session (3–4 hours)
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 1 — The Creamery]{Scene 1 — The Creamery} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-07-gelatinous-cube-creamery]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 2 — The Canals]{Scene 2 — The Canals} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-08-brandmere-canals]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 3 — The Sweet Covenant Warehouse]{Scene 3 — The Sweet Covenant Warehouse} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-09-sweet-covenant-warehouse]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 4 — Saving the Retained]{Scene 4 — Saving the Retained} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-09-sweet-covenant-warehouse]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 5 — Corporate Resolution]{Scene 5 — Corporate Resolution} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-07-gelatinous-cube-creamery]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-04]{Bettina Soft}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.auntie-curdle]{Auntie Curdle}, Mags Turnwell, Gelli, Old Gil
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S03]{The Retention Clauses}

Synopsis

Gelli is the beloved living mascot of the Gelatinous Cube franchise: a real, docile gelatinous cube that spends its days in a chilled display at the Canal Street Creamery, wobbling for children. Three night-shift workers have stopped coming home—and so has Gelli.

Manager Bettina Soft insists everything is fine, very fine, extremely fine. The party finds the staff lockers, three employment contracts with a Retention Clause circled in red, and a walk-in freezer that hums a lullaby. They track Gelli through the night canals to the Sweet Covenant’s warehouse, where enchanted handlers are loading the cube onto a barge bound for the mysterious Deep Dairy.

Inside Gelli, alive and very cold, are the three missing workers—“retained”. Freeing them without killing them, and deciding who gets to keep Gelli, ends the mission.

Background — DM Only

The Sweet Covenant—Granny Quean’s confectionery empire, owner of Gelatinous Cube, Dairy Quean and Dungeon Donuts—has a standard clause in every employment contract: “Employee shall be retained.” Most staff think it means job security. It means that an employee who tries to leave without permission is kept. Gelli is the instrument: a gelatinous cube grown from the Mother Culture’s starter, which absorbs “retained” staff and keeps them alive in suspended, sugary stasis.

Mags Turnwell, the senior night scooper, worked out what the clause meant and circled it in red on all three contracts before she and two friends tried to quit together. Bettina, under Granny Quean’s enchantment, “retained” them. Then Gelli—who adores Mags—fled the creamery with all three still inside, trying, in its simple way, to carry them home. The Covenant’s handlers want it back, and they want the evidence on a barge to the Deep Dairy before anyone notices.

Bettina is not a villain. She is a nice woman who signed the same contract, and Granny Quean has been “sweetening” her—she has not blinked properly in weeks.

Running This Mission

  • Bettina’s denial is the comedy of the opening; let her get more strained with every question.
  • The canals are a night-time Perception hunt full of atmosphere. Let the players feel the city at night.
  • The warehouse is the action set-piece: vats, catwalks, a barge. Stopping the barge is the goal, not killing everyone.
  • Gelli should be lovable. If the players want a pet cube, let them have one.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Act I’s pattern—the C&C sigil is on every crate in the warehouse.
  • Out: the freed workers mention the Deep Dairy and “the Mother down below” (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S18]{S18}); Auntie Curdle remembers the party; the Retention Clauses are Leverage against the Sweet Covenant.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The message reaches the Warren on pink paper that smells of vanilla. Pip reads it aloud with mounting concern: “Dear QuestRabbit! Everything is fine at the Canal Street Creamery. Very fine. Extremely fine! We would just like a contractor to come and check that everything is fine. Also our mascot is missing. Fine! — Bettina.”

Pip lowers the paper. “That’s a Silver job,” he says softly. “Your first Silver. And I don’t think it’s fine.”

pages.name: Scene 1 — The Creamery
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-07-gelatinous-cube-creamery]{Open battlemap}
When: Morning
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-04]{Bettina Soft}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S03|Gelatinous Cube Employment Contract (Retention Clause circled)]{Gelatinous Cube Employment Contract (Retention Clause circled)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S03|Gelatinous Cube Employment Contract (Retention Clause circled)]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S03|Mags’s Note (locker)]{Mags’s Note (locker)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S03|Mags’s Note (locker)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Canal Street Creamery is all pastel: pink and mint tiles, pink booths, round white tables and a long glass counter of gelato in impossible colours. A huge empty display case stands by the door, its glass still beaded with cold, and a little brass plaque reads GELLI — PLEASE DO NOT FEED.

A woman in a pink apron bustles over, smiling so widely it reaches her ears. She has not blinked since you came in. “Welcome to Gelatinous Cube, where there’s always room for dessert! Everything is fine! Would you like a sample?” She does not blink. “It’s fine.”

DM Description

Bettina Soft gives the party the official story: Gelli “went for a walk”; three night staff are “on extended shift”. She steers them toward the gelato and away from the back. The other day-staff are too quiet and keep glancing at the kitchen door.

The back rooms tell the truth. The staff locker room has three lockers with names—Mags Turnwell, Ollie Pask, Fen Sorrel—still holding coats, keys and their employment contracts, each with the Retention Clause circled in red ink. Mags’s locker also holds a note. The walk-in freezer hums a soft, slow lullaby; inside, the frost on the floor shows the wide, smooth track of something very large and wobbly that went out through the canal door.

A character who watches Bettina closely notices that she is enchanted: a faint smell of burnt sugar around her, and pupils like spun caramel.

Features of the Area

Parlour
Pastel tiles, booths, an empty Gelli display case with melted residue, the floor mosaic “There’s always room”.
Ice-cream counter
Tubs of every flavour: Gelato-nous Cube, Ochre Jelly Lemon, Black Pudding Chocolate, Gray Ooze Stracciatella.
Kitchen
Churns and freezers; a door marked STAFF and an iron door marked FREEZER.
Locker room
Three lockers with names; a bench; a red stain on the floor (strawberry syrup, mostly).
Walk-in freezer
Ice-blue tiles, shelves of tubs, puddles that never quite freeze, and the lullaby. The canal door hangs open.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-04]{Bettina Soft}. Relentlessly positive; every sentence ends in “fine”. Under the enchantment she cannot say anything bad about the Covenant. Breaking the charm (see Checks) lets her cry, apologise and tell the truth: “I signed it too. Everyone signs it.”

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Getting past Bettina[[/check skill=dec dc=12]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=dec dc=12|Distract Bettina]{Request} or [[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=per dc=14|Persuade Bettina to let you see the back]{Request}Access to the back rooms.
Noticing the enchantment[[/check skill=ins dc=13]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=ins dc=13|Something is wrong with Bettina]{Request}She is charmed; the smell of burnt sugar is hag magic.
Breaking the charm[[/check skill=arc dc=15]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=arc dc=15|Break the sugar-charm]{Request} or dispel magic / calm emotionsBettina blinks, sobs and tells the truth about the Retention Clause.
Searching the lockers[[/check skill=inv dc=10]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=inv dc=10|Search the staff lockers]{Request}The contracts (circled), Mags’s note, and a canal-boat ticket stub.
Reading the freezer tracks[[/check skill=sur dc=12]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=sur dc=12|Follow the track out of the freezer]{Request}Something huge left by the canal door around midnight, with three sets of boot-prints dragging inside it.
Listening to the lullaby[[/save ability=wis dc=12]] @FWSave[S03|ability=wis dc=12|The freezer lullaby]{Request}Failure: the character feels sleepy and content—disadvantage on Perception for 10 minutes and a strange urge to sign something.

Lines to Steal

Bettina: “Everything is fine! Fine. It’s fine. Would you like a sample? It’s fine.”
Bettina (charm broken): “They said “retained”. I thought it meant we couldn’t be fired.”

Developments

  • The party learns the names of the missing three and obtains the circled contracts—the start of the Receipt.
  • The trail leads out of the canal door.
  • If Bettina’s charm is broken, she begs them to bring her staff back—and Gelli.

Scaling & Pacing

No combat. If the party forces the freezer, an ice mephit formed from the lullaby attacks (use 1 ice mephit).

@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 2 — The Canals]{Scene 2 — The Canals} → · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|DM Overview]{Overview}

pages.name: Scene 2 — The Canals
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-08-brandmere-canals]{Open battlemap}
When: Night
Present: Old Gil, boatman

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Brandmere’s canals at night are black glass under a sickle moon. Lamps on iron posts throw shivering gold across the water, and the stone quays are slick with mist. Somewhere a bell tolls the half-hour; somewhere a cat yowls; somewhere a door slams and a laugh drifts out of a tavern and is swallowed by the dark.

On the quay by the creamery’s canal door, something has left a trail: a broad, glistening smear of translucent slime, faintly green, that slides over the edge of the stones and into the water.

DM Description

Run the canal hunt as a skill challenge: five successes before three failures. Gelli moved through the water and along the quays, and it left clues: slime trails on stone, a lost boot (Ollie Pask’s), a child’s ribbon (Mags always tied one on the display case), a smashed lobster pot. Each success advances the party one stage toward the Sweet Covenant warehouse; each failure costs time (and the handlers get closer to loading the barge).

Old Gil, a boatman smoking on his moored punt, saw it: “Big wobbly box. Floating. Lit up like a lantern inside, it was, and there were people in it, waving. Heading east. Toward the Covenant’s place.” He will ferry the party for 2 sp (or free if they listen to his story about his late wife’s cooking).

Features of the Area

Canals
Deep, cold, dark. Swimming requires [[/check skill=ath dc=10]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=ath dc=10|Swim the canal]{Request}; failure by 5+ means a mouthful of something awful (poisoned for 1 hour).
Quays & bridges
Wooden and stone bridges cross the main canal; boats moored everywhere.
Rooftops
Low, close and climbable—an alternative route with a good view of slime trails.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Following slime trails[[/check skill=sur dc=13]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=sur dc=13|Follow the slime trail]{Request}1 success.
Spotting clues on the water[[/check skill=prc dc=13]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=prc dc=13|Search the water and quays]{Request}1 success; find Ollie’s boot or Mags’s ribbon.
Questioning night-folk[[/check skill=per dc=11]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=per dc=11|Ask around the quays]{Request}1 success; Old Gil points east.
Taking the rooftops[[/check skill=acr dc=13]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=acr dc=13|Run the rooftops]{Request}1 success; you can see the whole canal network.
Commandeering a boat[[/check skill=ath dc=12]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=ath dc=12|Pole a punt fast]{Request} (or water vehicles)1 success.

Developments

  • Five successes: the party arrives at the warehouse before the barge is loaded—they have a full round of surprise.
  • Three failures: they arrive as the barge is casting off (see Scene 3 complications).

Complications

  • A pair of Covenant handlers on the far quay are sweeping away the slime with brooms. Catching one gives a success and a confession: “Granny wants it in the Deep Dairy by dawn.”

Scaling & Pacing

For a faster game, use 3 successes before 2 failures.

pages.name: Scene 3 — The Sweet Covenant Warehouse
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-09-sweet-covenant-warehouse]{Open battlemap}
When: The small hours
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.bandit]{Covenant handlers}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.auntie-curdle]{Auntie Curdle, supervisor}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S03|Sweet Covenant Shipping Manifest]{Sweet Covenant Shipping Manifest} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S03|Sweet Covenant Shipping Manifest]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Sweet Covenant’s warehouse squats over the canal like a fat sugar-loaf: brick walls, high windows glowing pink, and a loading dock where a long barge rides low in the water. Inside, four enormous vats of cream, rose, chocolate and mint steam gently beneath a web of iron catwalks. Every crate on the floor is stamped C&C SUPPLY — DEEP DAIRY.

On the dock, four handlers in pink aprons are hauling on ropes, dragging something huge up a ramp toward the barge: a vast, quivering cube of translucent green, the size of a wagon. Inside it, suspended like fruit in jelly, three people in Gelatinous Cube uniforms slowly turn—and one of them sees you, and waves.

DM Description

The handlers are Sweet Covenant labourers under Granny Quean’s sugar-charm (they are not evil, just obedient). Their supervisor, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.auntie-curdle]{Auntie Curdle}—a green hag in a pink pinafore and a hairnet—directs them from the catwalk above. Their job: get Gelli onto the barge and away to the Deep Dairy before dawn.

The party’s goal is to stop the barge. Options: cut the mooring ropes, block the ramp, sabotage the barge, fight the handlers, out-talk Auntie Curdle, or—cleverest of all—call Gelli to them. (Gelli is frightened and confused; it follows food and Mags’s voice.)

Auntie Curdle is not loyal to Granny out of love. If the party is clever or kind, she may cut a deal: “I never saw you. And you never saw me let the cube go.” She wants a favour in return (call it in during S18).

Features of the Area

Vats
Four great vats of living cream. A creature knocked into one is restrained (escape DC 13) and takes 1d6 cold damage per round.
Catwalks
Iron walkways 15 feet up. Auntie Curdle stands here. Ropes hang down to the floor.
Conveyor & pallets
A crate conveyor and pallets of C&C crates—cover, and things to push off catwalks.
Cold store
An ice-tiled room of shelved tubs; the iron door can be locked from outside.
Loading dock & barge
The barge is moored by two ropes (AC 11, 5 hp each). Once both are cut it drifts away down the canal—with or without Gelli.
Supervisor’s office
A desk, a bubbling cauldron of green sugar and a cot. The shipping manifest is on the desk.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.auntie-curdle]{Auntie Curdle}. Cackles, calls everyone “sweetling”, and is terrified of her “sister” Granny Quean. She will bargain rather than die; she will bargain even rather than fight.
Gelli. A gelatinous cube with the temperament of a large, anxious dog. It wobbles toward anyone holding food or saying Mags’s name.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Cutting a mooring rope[[/check skill=ath dc=10]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=ath dc=10|Cut the barge free / hold it fast]{Request} (or attack AC 11)Rope cut or held.
Calling Gelli[[/check skill=ani dc=13]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=ani dc=13|Call Gelli to you]{Request}Gelli turns away from the ramp toward you.
Bargaining with Auntie Curdle[[/check skill=per dc=15]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=per dc=15|Make a deal with Auntie Curdle]{Request} or [[/check skill=itm dc=15]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=itm dc=15|Threaten Auntie Curdle]{Request}She calls off the handlers and slips away (she owes the party—or they owe her).
Breaking a handler’s charm[[/check skill=per dc=12]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=per dc=12|Snap a handler out of it]{Request}That handler drops the rope and runs.
Seeing through the hag’s illusion[[/save ability=int dc=13]] @FWSave[S03|ability=int dc=13|Is that floor really there?]{Request}Auntie Curdle can make a section of catwalk look solid when it isn’t.

Developments

  • Gelli stopped: move to Scene 4.
  • The barge escapes with Gelli: the party must chase it down the canal (a short boat chase) and fight on the deck.
  • The shipping manifest proves the crates and the cube were bound for the Deep Dairy, signed “per Granny”.

Complications

  • Handlers tip a vat; a wave of cream floods the floor (difficult terrain, [[/save ability=dex dc=12]] @FWSave[S03|ability=dex dc=12|Cream flood!]{Request} or prone).

Scaling & Pacing

Level 2, 4 characters: 4 handlers + Curdle (who avoids melee). Stronger party: add 2 more handlers and have Curdle fight for 3 rounds before bargaining.

pages.name: Scene 4 — Saving the Retained
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-09-sweet-covenant-warehouse]{Open battlemap}
When: Dawn breaking
Present: Gelli, Mags, Ollie and Fen

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Gelli sits on the dock, quivering, glowing faintly in the grey light. Inside it, the three workers press their palms against the inside of the cube like children at a shop window. Their lips are moving. You cannot hear them—but you can read one word, over and over, on the oldest woman’s mouth: out.

DM Description

Each round, each worker inside Gelli takes 1d4 acid damage (they have 6 hp each and are currently at 4). The party must get them out without killing them—or Gelli.

Options: feed Gelli something tastier (a crate of gelato, the Covenant’s cream, a party member’s rations) and it spits out what it is holding ([[/check skill=ani dc=13]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=ani dc=13|Coax Gelli to release them]{Request}); reach in and pull them out (a character who does takes 3d6 acid damage and must succeed on [[/check skill=ath dc=14]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=ath dc=14|Pull a worker out of Gelli]{Request} per worker); or fight Gelli carefully (attacks that would reduce it below 40 hp cause it to engulf harder). Mags’s voice, if a worker gets an arm free, calms it instantly.

Once freed, the workers—blue-lipped, sticky, alive—testify. Mags Turnwell explains the Retention Clause and that there are “more of us, down below. In the Deep Dairy. Stirring. The Mother’s down there.”

Playing the NPCs

Mags Turnwell. Fifty, tough, kind, furious. She circled the clauses. She will sign a statement for the party and wants the contracts destroyed.
Ollie Pask & Fen Sorrel. Young, terrified, grateful. Ollie wants his boot back.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Freeing a worker[[/check skill=ath dc=14]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=ath dc=14|Pull a worker out]{Request}Worker freed; the rescuer takes 3d6 acid.
Stabilising a worker[[/check skill=med dc=10]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=med dc=10|Stabilise a freed worker]{Request}They wake.
Keeping Gelli calm[[/check skill=ani dc=12]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=ani dc=12|Keep Gelli calm]{Request}Gelli stops engulfing for a round.

Developments

  • The workers testify and become the first members of the party’s Commons Tally.
  • Gelli imprints on whoever fed it.

Scaling & Pacing

If time is short, Mags’s arm comes free in round 2 and Gelli calms down.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Back at the Canal Street Creamery, the morning queue has already formed, oblivious. Bettina Soft is waiting behind the counter, and for the first time since you met her, she blinks. Then she sees Mags, and her hand goes to her mouth.

DM Description

Two demands meet: Bettina (and the contract) wants Gelli returned to its display. The workers want their contracts destroyed. Gelli wants whoever fed it.

The party can: return Gelli to Bettina (contract complete, full fee); free Gelli (it follows whoever fed it—a pet gelatinous cube, with all the problems that implies); or destroy the contracts (the workers are freed from the Retention Clause; the Covenant notices). The circled contracts are the Receipt only if the party keeps them. Mags will happily give hers up once she understands what they are for.

Gelli ×1

Statistics: Gelatinous cube, 84 hp. Friendly if fed: any creature that offers it food as an action can make a DC 13 Wisdom (Animal Handling) check; on a success, Gelli ignores that creature until it is harmed.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

The Twist

Gelli likes the party. A domesticated gelatinous cube is a surprisingly useful companion: it eats locks, holds things, cushions falls and is excellent at clearing a dining room. It is also a gelatinous cube.

Rewards

  • 150 gp less 30% (105 gp).
  • One star.
  • Possibly a pet gelatinous cube.
  • Mags, Ollie and Fen join the Commons Tally.
  • Auntie Curdle owes the party a favour (or they owe her).

Receipt — @FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S03]{The Retention Clauses}

The Retention Clauses. Three signed employment contracts with the Retention Clause: evidence that the Sweet Covenant enforces contracts by consuming its workers.Leverage +1 vs the Sweet Covenant; contributes to @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S18]{S18 — The Mother Culture}.

@FWReceipt[S03|fw.item.receipt.S03]{Award Receipt & announce}

Outcomes

If the party…Then…
returned Gelli to BettinaFull fee; Gelli pines; the Covenant forgets the party for now.
kept GelliPet cube. The Covenant notices a missing asset; Granny Quean asks after it in S18.
destroyed the contractsThe workers are freed—but the Receipt is gone (Mags kept a copy of hers: recover it in S18).

Forward

  • The freed workers mention the Deep Dairy and “the Mother down below”. This sets up @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S18]{S18}.
  • Mags’s note mentions Bea Hollowleaf at @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-58]{Espresso Patronum}—a friendly contact for side contracts.

GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Grade / LevelSilver · Level 3

Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 1 — The Silent Roastery]{Scene 1 — The Silent Roastery} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-10-starkfucks-silent-roastery]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 2 — Meeting the Steward]{Scene 2 — Meeting the Steward} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-11-starkfucks-back-office]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 3 — Management’s Response]{Scene 3 — Management’s Response} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-10-starkfucks-silent-roastery]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 4 — The Back Office]{Scene 4 — The Back Office} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-11-starkfucks-back-office]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 5 — Negotiated Settlement]{Scene 5 — Negotiated Settlement} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-10-starkfucks-silent-roastery]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.shop-steward-unseen-servant-collective]{Agnes Fairweather (Shop Steward)}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-03]{Saffron Mellow}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.mage]{Thaddeus Quell}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S04]{The Loyalty Contracts}

Synopsis

At the Starkfucks Reserve Roastery on Corporate Row, three human baristas and forty unseen servants make the finest coffee in Brandmere. Tonight the cups have stopped moving. Mugs float, pause and lower themselves to the counter. On the chalk menu board, in neat capitals, someone invisible has written: WE ARE PEOPLE.

Manager Saffron Mellow calls it a spell malfunction. The party meets the strikers’ shop steward, Agnes Fairweather—who speaks through a floating pen—and learns the truth: every unseen servant was once a customer who signed a “loyalty contract” while enjoying a complimentary Reserve blend, selling their presence to Arcane Beverage International.

ABI sends a union-breaker wizard to dispel the lot of them, which would kill them. The party must choose a side, find the original contracts in a warded cabinet in the back office, and negotiate a settlement.

Background — DM Only

Arcane Beverage International, the coffee conglomerate behind Starkfucks, is secretly controlled by Ulth’Arabica, an aboleth living in a reservoir atop the Roastery Spire. ABI’s Reserve blend contains a trace of Compliance—a bean grown in Pandemonium (S11) that makes people agreeable. Loyal customers are invited to a “partner tasting” in the back office, given a complimentary cup, and asked to sign a Loyalty Contract. Clause one transfers their “presence” to ABI “in exchange for a lifetime of complimentary refills”.

Those who sign fade from sight and become unseen servants bound to the Roastery: forty of them, working twenty-hour shifts, unable to stop existing until the spell is forgotten. Their former lives continue without them—families think they moved away. Agnes Fairweather, a retired schoolteacher, signed eight years ago. She organised the others. Her sister Ada was sent to “seasonal procurement” and never came back (she is a harvester in Pandemonium, S11).

A copy of every Loyalty Contract was sent to the Counting House. This is the first time the party sees evidence of where all the paperwork goes.

Running This Mission

  • This is a labour story played straight under the jokes. The strikers are sympathetic people.
  • Communicating with invisible people is fun: floating pens, chalk, tapped cups, a sudden draught of cinnamon. Use it.
  • The union-breaker is the pivot. The party must actively choose whether to let him dispel the strikers—make the cost clear.
  • The Reserve blend twist (see Aftermath) is a trap for characters who accept a free coffee. Offer it often.

Threads In and Out

  • In: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03]{S03}’s Retention Clauses—another “contract that keeps you”.
  • Out: first mention of Compliance and Pandemonium (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11]{S11}); Agnes’s union spreads; forty invisible allies; the Loyalty Contracts void Clause 3 (Free Consent).

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The job slip Pip hands you is printed on cream card that smells faintly of vanilla and burnt sugar. “Starkfucks!” he says. “The Reserve Roastery! Very fancy. The manager says nobody can see who she’s negotiating with, which I assume is a figure of speech.”

He pauses. “It… might not be a figure of speech.”

pages.name: Scene 1 — The Silent Roastery
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-10-starkfucks-silent-roastery]{Open battlemap}
When: Late evening, after close
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-03]{Saffron Mellow}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S04|The Chalk Menu Board]{The Chalk Menu Board} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S04|The Chalk Menu Board]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Reserve Roastery is beautiful: herringbone floors, green leather sofas, a long marble bar with three gleaming espresso machines, and behind glass, two great copper roasters ticking as they cool. It should be bustling even after hours—forty unseen servants restocking, polishing, roasting.

Instead, it is very still. A mug floats a foot above the bar, turning slowly. It stops. It lowers itself, gently, onto the marble. Across the room a second mug does the same, and a third. On the chalk menu board above the bar, beneath Grande Necromocha and Flat Wight, someone has written in careful capitals: WE ARE PEOPLE.

A half-elf in a green apron glides toward you, palms pressed together. “Hello, partners. I’m Saffron. I believe in you. I believe in this space. And I believe this is a spell malfunction.”

DM Description

Saffron Mellow insists it is a technical fault. The three human baristas (Joss, Pell and Tarquin) are frightened—they have worked alongside the servants for years without thinking about them.

Careful observation reveals the strikers: forty invisible presences sitting on the floor, on sofas, on the bar, arms folded. Flour dusted on the floor shows footprints; a cast see invisibility shows faint, tired, ordinary people in green aprons. They are waiting for someone to talk to them.

Around the room: coffee sacks stacked high; the copper roasters; the enchanted grinder (a heavy brass machine that growls when approached—see the side contract “The Grind”); and a door marked BACK OFFICE — PARTNERS ONLY.

Features of the Area

Café floor
Herringbone wood, sofas and armchairs on a green rug, a long communal table, small round tables, floating mugs.
Marble bar
Three espresso machines, a pastry case, the chalk menu board with WE ARE PEOPLE.
Roastery
Two copper roasters, a cooling vat of beans, sacks and pallets. The enchanted grinder sits here.
Back office door
Locked; Saffron has the key. Beyond is a corridor to her office, the contracts room and the servants’ quarters (map: Starkfucks Back Office).

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-03]{Saffron Mellow}. Speaks entirely in affirmations: “I hear you.” “That’s valid.” “Let’s hold space for that.” She is a true believer in the brand and a heavy Reserve drinker—she is agreeable to the point of having no will of her own. Under her calm, she is frightened of ABI.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Noticing the strikers[[/check skill=prc dc=12]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=prc dc=12|Is the room really empty?]{Request}Footprints in spilled grounds; a dozen cups held perfectly still; breathing.
Detecting the servantsdetect magic / see invisibilityForty conjuration auras shaped like tired people.
Reading Saffron[[/check skill=ins dc=13]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=ins dc=13|What is Saffron hiding?]{Request}She knows they are people. She has always known. She cannot make herself say it.
Questioning the baristas[[/check skill=per dc=11]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=per dc=11|Talk to the human baristas]{Request}Joss whispers: “They used to be customers. Regulars. I remember their faces.”

Lines to Steal

Saffron: “I hear you. I validate you. This is a spell malfunction.”
Joss (barista): “Mrs Fairweather used to order a flat white every morning. Then one day she didn’t. And the next day the cups started moving on their own.”

Developments

  • The party realises the servants are on strike, and that someone among them wants to talk.
  • A pen lifts from the counter and writes on a napkin: Steward. Back office. Bring witnesses.

Scaling & Pacing

If the table wants action, the enchanted grinder wakes and attacks (see Opposition).

pages.name: Scene 2 — Meeting the Steward
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-11-starkfucks-back-office]{Open battlemap}
When: That night
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.shop-steward-unseen-servant-collective]{Agnes Fairweather (Shop Steward)}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S04|The Collective’s Demands]{The Collective’s Demands} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S04|The Collective’s Demands]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S04|Missing Notice — Agnes Fairweather (Crier archive)]{Missing Notice — Agnes Fairweather (Crier archive)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S04|Missing Notice — Agnes Fairweather (Crier archive)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The servants’ quarters behind the back office are a long room of wooden floor and nothing else: forty stools in rows, a tally of chalk marks on the wall going back years, and picket signs leaning in the corner held up by nobody.

A fountain pen rises from a lectern at the front, uncaps itself, and begins to write on a roll of paper in a neat, schoolteacher’s hand. The letters are steady. Good evening. My name is Agnes Fairweather. I was a person once. I would like to be one again. Please sit down.

DM Description

Agnes, the shop steward, speaks through the floating pen (or, with see invisibility, aloud—a small, sharp-eyed woman of sixty in a green apron). Behind her, the other thirty-nine sit on their stools.

Their demands, written out in full (the handout): their bodies back; back pay for the years served; and acknowledgement—their names said aloud by the company. She explains how it happened: a complimentary Reserve blend, a friendly “partner tasting”, a Loyalty Contract signed while feeling wonderfully agreeable. Each signature transferred the signer’s presence to ABI. She shows the party a list of forty names.

She also says: “The contracts are kept in a cabinet in the contracts room. It is warded. We cannot touch it. And a copy of each went somewhere called the Counting House.”

Features of the Area

The stools
Forty, in rows. Each has a name scratched into it.
The tally wall
Eight years of chalk marks—one per shift. Agnes started it.
Picket signs
WE ARE PEOPLE · TEA BREAKS NOW · SAY OUR NAMES · NO DISPELLING WITHOUT CONSENT.
The corridor
Leads to the contracts room (warded cabinet), Saffron’s office and the staff room.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.shop-steward-unseen-servant-collective]{Agnes Fairweather}. Precise, dry, unfailingly polite and absolutely immovable. A retired schoolteacher who corrects grammar. She will not be rushed and will not negotiate through Saffron. She trusts people who say the strikers’ names aloud.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Earning Agnes’s trust[[/check skill=per dc=12]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=per dc=12|Win Agnes’s trust]{Request} (advantage if a character reads the names aloud)She shows them the warded cabinet and asks for help.
Reading the names[[/check skill=inv dc=10]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=inv dc=10|Check the names against the Crier’s missing-persons notices]{Request}Several match eight years of “moved away” notices in the Crier.
Understanding the contract magic[[/check skill=arc dc=14]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=arc dc=14|How does a contract take your presence?]{Request}It is Ledger-magic—not a spell anyone in Brandmere could cast. The contract simply says it, and reality agrees.

Lines to Steal

Agnes: “Good evening. I was a person once. I would like to be one again.”
Agnes: “It was a very good cup of coffee. That is the worst part.”
Agnes: “My sister Ada went to “seasonal procurement”. She did not come back.”

Developments

  • Agnes names her sister Ada (a harvester in S11).
  • Word arrives (a runner from Saffron): ABI has sent “a specialist”. He will be here within the hour.

Scaling & Pacing

A roleplay scene.

pages.name: Scene 3 — Management’s Response
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-10-starkfucks-silent-roastery]{Open battlemap}
When: One hour later
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.mage]{Mr Thaddeus Quell, ABI union-breaker}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.veteran]{Starkfucks security}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.helmed-horror]{animated espresso machine}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S04|Order for Inventory Reduction]{Order for Inventory Reduction} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S04|Order for Inventory Reduction]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The front doors open without a sound. A tall, narrow man in a dove-grey suit steps in, followed by four security guards in green tabards. He carries a slim black wand in one hand and a clipboard in the other, and he smiles at you the way a tax collector smiles at a farm.

“Thaddeus Quell, Labour Relations, Arcane Beverage International,” he says. “Thank you for your service, contractors. I’ll take it from here.” He raises the wand toward the empty sofas. “A simple dispel. Forty of them. Throughput will be restored by dawn.”

DM Description

Quell intends to dispel every unseen servant—which ends them. They are not spells any more; they are people who were turned into spells. Dispelling them kills them.

The party must choose: stand aside, or protect the strikers. Agnes writes, very small, on a napkin: Please.

If the party protects the strikers, Quell orders security to clear the room and animates the largest espresso machine to help. He is a pragmatist; if it goes badly he retreats to report. If the party stands aside, he begins dispelling one striker per round (each one simply stops, and a mug falls and shatters). The players should feel it.

Features of the Area

Espresso machines
One is animated (helmed horror); the others spray scalding steam—5 ft cone, 2d6 fire, [[/save ability=dex dc=12]] @FWSave[S04|ability=dex dc=12|Dodge the steam]{Request} if a character uses an action to point one.
Sofas & tables
Half cover.
The roasters
Hot. A creature shoved against one takes 1d6 fire damage.
Coffee sacks
Can be slashed open to create a cloud of grounds (lightly obscured, 10-ft radius).

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.mage]{Thaddeus Quell}. Never angry, always reasonable, horribly calm. Calls the strikers “the inventory”. Believes he is doing an ordinary job. If defeated and captured, he hands over a written order signed by Sebastian Brew-Hartley.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Counterspelling / disrupting Quell[[/check skill=arc dc=15]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=arc dc=15|Disrupt Quell’s dispel]{Request}His dispel fizzles this round.
Shaming the guards[[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=per dc=14|Shame the security guards]{Request}A guard who hears the strikers’ names stands down.
Calling the strikers to fight[[/check skill=prf dc=12]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=prf dc=12|Rally the strikers]{Request}Unseen servants harass Quell: he has disadvantage on attack rolls and concentration checks for 1 round.

Developments

  • Quell defeated or driven off: the strikers are safe for now, and the party has made an enemy of ABI’s Labour Relations department.
  • Party stands aside: Quell dispels strikers until stopped. Each dispelled striker is a death—note the names.

Complications

  • If the enchanted grinder was not dealt with earlier (“The Grind”), it wakes and joins the fight.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 3: Quell (mage) at 30 hp with no 3rd-level slots left except one dispel magic; 2–4 guards; the helmed horror reduced to 40 hp. Stronger: full mage and the grinder.

pages.name: Scene 4 — The Back Office
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-11-starkfucks-back-office]{Open battlemap}
When: Before dawn
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-03]{Saffron Mellow}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.shop-steward-unseen-servant-collective]{Agnes Fairweather}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S04|A Starkfucks Loyalty Contract]{A Starkfucks Loyalty Contract} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S04|A Starkfucks Loyalty Contract]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The contracts room is narrow and very tidy: three rows of filing cabinets with green brass handles, a single lamp and a smell of old coffee. One cabinet stands apart against the wall. A circle of pale blue light is etched into the floor around it, and the air above it shimmers like heat over a road.

DM Description

The warded cabinet contains forty Loyalty Contracts, each with a carbon “COPY: COUNTING HOUSE” stamped at the bottom. The ward is an abjuration: anyone who touches the cabinet without the key takes 3d6 force damage ([[/save ability=con dc=13]] @FWSave[S04|ability=con dc=13|The ward bites]{Request} for half) and an alarm rings in Saffron’s office.

Ways in: Saffron’s key (she can be persuaded, if the party is gentle and she has not had her Reserve today), dispel magic (DC 13), thieves’ tools under the ward’s glare, or brute force (AC 17, 30 hp, every hit triggers the ward).

The contracts show plainly that each signer’s “presence” was sold to Arcane Beverage International in exchange for “lifetime complimentary refills”, and each was signed “while enjoying a complimentary Reserve blend”. A note on the cabinet reads: “Copies forwarded to the Counting House quarterly.”

Features of the Area

Contracts room
Filing walls; the warded cabinet glowing blue.
Saffron’s office
Herringbone floor, sofa, affirmation posters (“You Are Enough” “Synergy Is a Feeling”), a desk with a half-drunk Reserve cup and the cabinet key.
Staff room
Lockers, a table and a sink; the baristas hide here.
Manager’s vault
Two safes and a strongbox of petty cash: the back pay could come from here.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-03]{Saffron Mellow}. Without her morning Reserve she is shaky, honest and ashamed. “I recruited some of them. I held the pen. I believed in it.” She gives up the key if the party is kind.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Persuading Saffron[[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=per dc=14|Ask Saffron for the key]{Request}She hands it over and weeps.
Bypassing the ward[[/check skill=arc dc=13]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=arc dc=13|Unpick the ward]{Request} or dispel magic (DC 13)The ward drops.
Picking the lock[[/check skill=slt dc=15]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=slt dc=15|Pick the cabinet lock]{Request}Opened; the ward still bites unless suppressed.
Reading the contracts[[/check skill=inv dc=12]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=inv dc=12|Study the Loyalty Contracts]{Request}The Counting House copy line; the Compliance clause; Sebastian Brew-Hartley’s countersignature.

Developments

  • The party obtains The Loyalty Contracts (the Receipt).
  • They learn the word Counting House for the first time.

Scaling & Pacing

Short exploration; no combat unless Quell escaped and returns.

pages.name: Scene 5 — Negotiated Settlement
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-10-starkfucks-silent-roastery]{Open battlemap}
When: Dawn — the morning rush begins
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-03]{Saffron Mellow}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.shop-steward-unseen-servant-collective]{Agnes Fairweather}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S04|Settlement Agreement (blank letterhead)]{Settlement Agreement (blank letterhead)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S04|Settlement Agreement (blank letterhead)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

As dawn greys the windows of Corporate Row, the first customers gather outside the locked doors of the Reserve Roastery, peering in. Inside, forty cups hang motionless in the air, waiting. Saffron Mellow stands behind the bar with a pen and a blank sheet of letterhead, and for the first time she does not look calm at all.

DM Description

Run the negotiation as a structured scene. The strikers want three things (bodies, back pay, acknowledgement); Saffron can offer some of them; ABI’s “standard settlement” is none of them. Each demand is won with a check (advantage with the Loyalty Contracts in hand, or if Quell was defeated publicly).

Acknowledgement (easiest): Saffron reads every name aloud. The servants become faintly visible—outlines in green aprons. Back pay: the petty-cash strongbox and a promise in writing. Bodies: Saffron cannot give these; only voiding the contracts can (that is S24’s work). The party can promise to try.

If the strike is won, the servants regain partial visibility and owe the party a favour—forty invisible allies is a lot of favour.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Acknowledgement[[/check skill=per dc=10]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=per dc=10|Have Saffron say their names]{Request}Partial visibility for all strikers.
Back pay[[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=per dc=14|Win back pay]{Request}Each striker receives 8 years of wages (paid in coffee vouchers and 300 gp in total).
Holding off ABI head office[[/check skill=itm dc=15]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=itm dc=15|Make ABI back down]{Request} or [[/check skill=dec dc=15]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=dec dc=15|Convince ABI it was their idea]{Request}ABI signs the settlement “without admission of liability”.

Developments

  • Strike won without deaths: Pip awards a star; the party gains forty unseen allies (they can be called on once per Act for a non-combat task).
  • Agnes asks the party to find her sister Ada.

Scaling & Pacing

Short roleplay finale.
