Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The kitchen of Five Wights is the same kitchen in every branch—and right now it is several of them at once. A grill flickers between steel and iron. A prep table is briefly two prep tables. Through the pass, you glimpse other kitchens, other dining rooms, other customers, like reflections in a broken mirror.

DM Description

Each Five Wights branch is a single, oath-bound kitchen experienced in many places at once. With Four missing, the oath is failing. Glitches: menu items “exist slightly less” (a fry passes through a hand), customers repeat sentences, the brothers finish one another’s sentences but leave gaps where Four’s words belong.

The brothers explain: they swore to be in every kitchen, always, together. Four vanished three nights ago from every branch at once. They can feel where he is—“north, cold, stacked”—and will lead the party there.

Features of the Area

The glitch
Each round in the kitchen, roll [[/r 1d6]]: 1 — a character is duplicated for a moment (an echo that copies their last action); 2 — an item flickers out of existence for a round; 3–6 — nothing.
The pass
A window into other branches.
Four’s station
An empty grill where the hat hangs on its hook, unworn.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-06]{The Harrow Brothers}. They speak in sequence, one word or phrase each, in order: One, Two, Three, [gap], Five. They are polite, solemn and frightened. They will remember every order the party has ever placed.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The doors slide open with a sigh of cold air. Inside, the warehouse goes on further than the building outside should allow: aisles of steel shelving forty feet high, stacked with pallets of everything, lit by lanterns that buzz. Staff in red vests drive mechanical pallet-lifters along the aisles. Near the entrance, a smiling woman at a sample table holds out a tiny paper cup of something pale and sweet that moves very slightly in the cup.

“Free sample?”

DM Description

A membership card is required to go past the entrance (Hal Grundy enforces it, miserably). Options: Membership Drive’s cards (from the side contract), a forgery (Deception or forgery kit DC 16), or a real sign-up—which binds the signer and all their descendants to CostCo-op membership forever (a real, permanent Ledger entry; note it).

The free samples are the Mother Culture (S18): eating one is harmless, delicious and makes the character feel briefly watched by something vast and slow. Gelli (if with the party) quivers violently near them.

The executive vault is at the back, beyond the bulk aisles, past a door marked EXECUTIVE MEMBERS ONLY.

Features of the Area

Bulk aisles
Endless pallets. Getting lost: [[/check skill=sur dc=13]] @FWCheck[S09|skill=sur dc=13|Navigate the infinite aisles]{Request}.

Mother Culture samples, roast owlbear chunks, potion shots.

Hal Grundy and a ledger.

Carriages and the way out.

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.hal-grundy]{Hal Grundy}. A sweating, decent middle manager with a clipboard and a membership lanyard that has become part of his neck. He will look the other way if the party is kind and convincing; he dreads the dragons.

pages.name: Scene 4 — The Executive Vault
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-20-executive-collateral-vault]{Open battlemap}
When: Night
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.compliance-officer]{a Compliance Officer}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.kobold]{Hoard kobolds}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.guard-drake]{guard drakes}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.mimic]{mimic pallets}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S09|Four’s Collateral Tag]{Four’s Collateral Tag} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S09|Four’s Collateral Tag]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The executive vault is cold enough to see your breath. Steel floors, steel walls, rows of steel cages, each holding a single crate with a single tag. Some tags you can read from here: A KING’S SOUL. THE RIVER BRANDE (UPPER). ONE (1) YEAR — SPRING, UNUSED.

In the centre of the vault, under a lamp, sits a long crate the size of a coffin. Through the slats, a pale face in a paper hat lies very still. The tag reads: COLLATERAL — RNG — PARTNER No. 4.

Between you and the crate stands a figure in a grey suit, with a grey face and a lanyard with no name. It is reading a clipboard. It does not look up. “Membership number?”

DM Description

The vault is guarded by a Compliance Officer, six kobolds of the Hoard, two guard drakes and four mimics disguised as pallets. Opening Four’s box without the Ledger’s permission sounds an alarm.

Other collateral can be taken—one item more—but the Ledger will notice (and the Hoard will want it back in S19).

Features of the Area

Cages
Steel cages holding collateral crates; picking a cage lock: thieves’ tools DC 15.
Four’s crate
Under the lamp. Alarmed.
Guard post
A kobold card table and bunk.
Drake pen
Straw, bones, a trough; two guard drakes.
The mimic pallets
Four of the pallets near the exit are mimics.

Checks & Roll Requests

As the lid comes off, the vault wakes. Lamps flare red along the ceiling. Cages rattle. Somewhere deep in the warehouse, something very large shifts its weight, and the floor shivers. Four Harrow opens his eyes, looks at you, and says, very simply, the word his brothers have been missing: “Four.”

DM Description

A reverse chase out of the warehouse: the vault doors close one by one; mimic pallets lunge from the aisles; kobolds pursue; the Compliance Officer walks after the party, never hurrying, never stopping, until they leave CostCo-op property.

When the party carries Four out of the doors, every Five Wights in Brandmere snaps back into reality at once. The brothers, wherever they are, say together: “Thank you.”

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS10 · Act II
Grade / LevelSilver · Level 8
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-65]{Wand-Mart} (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-06]{Adventure Retail Consortium})

Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S10|Scene 1 — Rollback Day]{Scene 1 — Rollback Day} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-21-wand-mart-supercentre]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S10|Scene 2 — The Numbers]{Scene 2 — The Numbers} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-21-wand-mart-supercentre]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S10|Scene 3 — The Cash Office]{Scene 3 — The Cash Office} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-22-wand-mart-cash-office]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S10|Scene 4 — The Folio]{Scene 4 — The Folio} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-22-wand-mart-cash-office]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S10|Scene 5 — Veronique’s Confession]{Scene 5 — Veronique’s Confession} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-22-wand-mart-cash-office]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-06.public-face]{Doris Plank}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}, Benny Abacus
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S10]{The Wand-Mart Cost Ledger}

Synopsis

Wand-Mart, the vast supercentre on the city’s edge, sells everything for less than it costs: healing potions, spell scrolls, rations, torches—all rolled back. An anonymous shareholder wants to know how. The party arrives on Rollback Day, the biggest sale of the year, and watches customers grow a few days older with every purchase.

In the stockroom, invoices show every item costs more than it sells for; a clerk mentions “time payments”. A heist into the cash office brings the party face to face with General Manager Doris Plank, cheerfully unmoved, with a Folio on her desk whose entries rewrite themselves. She explains how it works—and offers them lifetime free shopping.

Then Veronique Salt, the anonymous shareholder, reveals the truth: “C&C doesn’t stand for Crown & Cleaver. It stands for Creation & Company. We all belong to it. So do you.” She offers the party a partnership against the Board.

Background — DM Only

A Folio is a branch-ledger: a page of the Grand Ledger delegated to a subsidiary. Anything written in it is true, but every line is paid for in the writer’s—or the customer’s—time. Wand-Mart’s “Rollback” prices are real: the difference is debited from customers in days of their lives, recorded in the Folio and remitted to the Counting House.

The Adventure Retail Consortium is fronted by Doris Plank and controlled by SKÜ, the Warehouse Mind—a colony of mimics grown through IKEA Mimic’s furniture into a single intelligence. The shelves of Wand-Mart are, in places, alive.

Veronique hired the party as “anonymous shareholder” to gain leverage over ARC—and the Board. She has decided the party is worth recruiting.

Running This Mission

  • Rollback Day is crowd chaos. Use the ageing effect as horror-comedy: a teenager buys a sword and comes out with a moustache.
  • The cash office is a heist with a twist: Doris isn’t hiding anything; she’s proud of it.
  • End Act II on Veronique’s confession. It reframes the whole campaign.
  • The Folio has a page for the party. Show it to them.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Veronique’s leverage plans (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S08]{S08}).
  • Out: end of Act II; the party learns C&C means Creation & Company; a Folio (@FWLink[Item|fw.item.magic.01]{Folio}) in hand; the Mandate Progress meter.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The job slip is unsigned, printed on heavy cream card, and paid in advance in a sealed purse. Pip turns it over twice. “An anonymous shareholder,” he says. “That’s… fancy. Wand-Mart, though! Rollback Day! You could pick up some potions while you’re there.”

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The doors of the Wand-Mart Supercentre open at the first bell, and the crowd surges in like the sea through a broken dam. Inside, the store is enormous: forty aisles under a roof of lanterns, yellow ROLLBACK! signs on every shelf, a smiling greeter in a blue vest at the door with a basket of stickers.

A young man in a College Ward scarf grabs a discounted longsword off a shelf, pays at the nearest till, and turns away grinning. He is a few steps from the door when you notice his chin: a faint shadow of stubble that wasn’t there before. By the time he reaches the exit, he has a moustache.

DM Description

Rollback Day is chaos: crowds, sales, fights over the last cheap potion. Customers age a few days per purchase (a week for a big item); nobody notices except the party.

Run a short crowd scene: the party can observe purchases, talk to shoppers (an old woman who has shopped here weekly for thirty years and is, she thinks, about forty), follow staff into the back, and avoid buying anything. If a character buys something, they age too (a day per gold piece saved—roll [[/r 1d6]] days for a small item).

Features of the Area

Aisles
Forty aisles of gondola shelving. Some shelves are mimics (SKÜ).
Checkouts
Eight tills with queue ropes. Each till has a small brass plate: TIME PAYMENTS ACCEPTED.
Customer service
A desk where complaints are “noted”.
Stockroom
Back doors marked STAFF; pallets of goods.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The cash office is quieter than the store and much colder. Rows of counting tables with neat piles of coin. Brass scales. Filing cabinets to the ceiling. And at the far end, behind a broad desk on a blue rug, a silver-haired woman in a blue blazer with a killer smile, writing in a thick book bound in grey.

She looks up, unsurprised. “Contractors! Come in, come in. I’m Doris. Would you like a coffee? We have a rollback on coffee.”

DM Description

Doris Plank is not hiding anything. She is proud of the system. She explains, cheerfully, how it works: Wand-Mart sells below cost; the customer pays the difference in time, which is written in the Folio and remitted upstairs; everyone gets a bargain; “and honestly, who misses a few days?”

She offers the party lifetime free shopping (a card that debits nothing—or rather, debits someone else). If they refuse and try to take the Folio, she calls security: four shelf mimics, two helmed horrors and a SKÜ drone (a giant mimic) from the vault.

Features of the Area

The Folio, a glowing lamp, a rug.

Coin piles and scales—scattering coins creates difficult terrain.
Vault

Back to the stockroom.

The Folio is heavier than a book should be. Its pages are grey and soft, like ash pressed flat. As you watch, the entries rewrite themselves in neat clerical script: names, purchases, prices, and a column headed DEBITED, filled with numbers of days. Then the pages turn by themselves, and stop on one with your names at the top.

DM Description

The Folio’s entries rewrite themselves as the party watches. Writing in it makes things true—but uses the writer’s time (a line costs 1d4 years for a small change, more for a large one). It is a delegated page of the Grand Ledger.

The party’s page reads: Representatives of the Commons — Rating: 3 stars — Mandate Progress: 60%. Their Rabbit Rating is also a mandate.

The Folio is a magic item (@FWLink[Item|fw.item.magic.01]{Folio}) and, its pages of debited years, the Receipt.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

When: Dawn
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Veronique is waiting in the empty Wand-Mart car park, leaning against her black carriage, smoking a thin cigarette. She takes the Folio from you—or doesn’t—and looks at your page for a long time.

“I’m your anonymous shareholder,” she says. “I wanted leverage on ARC. Now I have it.” She drops the cigarette and grinds it out. “You’ve been very patient with me, so I’ll be honest, once. C&C doesn’t stand for Crown & Cleaver. It stands for Creation & Company. We all belong to it. So do you.” She holds out a gloved hand. “I’d like a partnership. Against the Board.”

DM Description

Veronique reveals the truth: Creation & Company owns everything—every umbrella corporation, every franchise, QuestRabbit too—and it is buying the Material Plane. She wants to depose Baron Cleave and take his Board seat, and she wants the party as allies. She will share information if they share Receipts.

This ends Act II. The party learns what C&C means and sees the Mandate Progress meter beside their Rabbit Rating.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS11 · Act III
Grade / LevelGold · Level 9
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-03]{Starkfucks} / @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-57]{Bean There, Summoned That} (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-04]{Arcane Beverage International})
Session length1–2 sessions; a planar expedition with a moral fork
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11|Scene 1 — The Portal]{Scene 1 — The Portal} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-coffee-04-bean-there-summoned-that]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11|Scene 2 — The Plantations]{Scene 2 — The Plantations} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-24-pandemonium-bean-plantations]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11|Scene 3 — The Harvesters]{Scene 3 — The Harvesters} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-24-pandemonium-bean-plantations]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11|Scene 4 — The Overseer]{Scene 4 — The Overseer} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-25-pandemonium-overseers-station]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11|Scene 5 — Sabotage or Harvest]{Scene 5 — Sabotage or Harvest} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-25-pandemonium-overseers-station]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.ada-fairweather]{Ada Fairweather}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.skarrow-vane]{Skarrow Vane}, Thaddeus Quell, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-04.public-face]{Sebastian Brew-Hartley}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S11]{The Harvesters’ Testimony}

Synopsis

Arcane Beverage International—unaware the party has turned, or hoping they haven’t—hires them through QuestRabbit for the Seasonal Premium harvest. Pip calls it “a big step up!” The portal is in the back room of Bean There, Summoned That, and the wind starts before anyone opens it.

Pandemonium is a plane of endless wind-carved tunnels. In them grow glowing beans tended by harvesters who remember nothing but their shifts. One, Ada, remembers only her daughter’s name—and she is Agnes Fairweather’s sister, lost when ABI broke the Starkfucks union.

A cambion overseer rides a howler between the rows. Beyond him is the processing shed, where the beans are packed as Compliance: the secret ingredient in every ABI drink, a mild, constant agreeableness poured into the whole city every morning. The party can harvest as contracted, poison the crop, or free the harvesters and lead them home.

Background — DM Only

Compliance is ABI’s great secret. Ulth’Arabica, the aboleth in the Roastery Spire, found that beans grown in Pandemonium’s madness absorb it in reverse: the drinker becomes calmer, more reasonable, more willing to sign. Every latte in Brandmere carries a trace. It is why nobody complains about the purple awnings.

The harvesters are workers who signed ABI “retention” contracts—people from broken unions, debtors, the missing. Pandemonium’s wind scours their memories until only the shift remains. They are not chained; they simply cannot remember anywhere else to be.

The overseer, Skarrow Vane, is a cambion on an ABI performance bonus. He is cruel because cruelty hits targets.

Running This Mission

  • The wind is the star. Describe it constantly: it howls, whispers, sings, mocks, and says the characters’ own names back to them.
  • The memory-loss save is player-facing: let players choose what their characters forget (a name, a favourite food, how they met). Write them down. They return when the party leaves Pandemonium—mostly.
  • Ada is the emotional centre. If Agnes Fairweather is alive and allied (S04), bring a letter from her.
  • Make the fork clear: harvest (paid, complicit), burn (ABI knows), or free (no fee, the harvesters’ testimony).

Threads In and Out

  • In: the Marchetti Memo (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S06]{S06}) named Pandemonium; Agnes’s union (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04]{S04}).
  • Out: ABI’s supply is cut; Ulth’Arabica takes notice; Compliance wears off across the city. The harvesters guide the party through Pandemonium again in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S22]{S22}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Pip slides the contract across the table with both paws, ears up, whiskers trembling. “Gold grade,” he whispers. “Gold! Planar procurement for ABI—that’s a big step up! There’s hazard pay. And ear protection, apparently.” He frowns at the line. “Why would you need ear protection to pick beans?”

pages.name: Scene 1 — The Portal
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-coffee-04-bean-there-summoned-that]{Open battlemap}
When: Before dawn
Present: Thaddeus Quell (ABI procurement), barista summoners
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S11|ABI Procurement Order]{ABI Procurement Order} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S11|ABI Procurement Order]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Bean There, Summoned That is quiet at this hour: chairs upturned on tables, the espresso machines cold, a chalkboard reading TODAY’S FAMILIAR: OWL. But the back room is loud. Behind a door marked STOCK, something is howling.

The door opens on a summoning circle chalked in coffee grounds, ringed with burlap sacks. In the centre, the air is torn like a sheet of paper, and through the tear pours wind—cold, dry, and full of voices. Your hair stands on end. Somewhere inside the wind, something says your name, and laughs.

DM Description

Thaddeus Quell, ABI’s procurement manager (the union-breaker from S04, if the party met him), briefs the party with a clipboard and earmuffs. Twelve sacks; the overseer will sign for them; the portal stays open for twelve hours.

The baristas maintaining the circle are summoners on minimum wage. One, a tired tiefling named Jory, mutters: “Nobody who goes for the harvest comes back the same. Some don’t come back.”

Features of the Area

The circle
Coffee-ground chalk; disturbing it collapses the portal in 1 minute.
Burlap sacks
Stamped SEASONAL PREMIUM — ABI — DO NOT INHALE.
Earmuffs
ABI-issue; grant advantage on the first madness save only.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Reading the procurement order[[/check skill=inv dc=14]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=inv dc=14|Read the procurement order closely]{Request}The product code is CMPL-01: “Compliance (Seasonal Premium)”.
Talking to Jory[[/check skill=per dc=12]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=per dc=12|Get Jory talking]{Request}Harvesters are “retained staff”. Jory’s cousin went through two years ago.
Studying the portal[[/check skill=arc dc=15]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=arc dc=15|Study the portal]{Request}A one-way pull: things pass in easily; memories do not pass back.

Developments

  • Through the portal.

pages.name: Scene 2 — The Plantations
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-24-pandemonium-bean-plantations]{Open battlemap}
When: On-plane (hours pass strangely)
Present: harvesters
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S11|What I Have Forgotten (player tracker)]{What I Have Forgotten (player tracker)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S11|What I Have Forgotten (player tracker)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

You step into a tunnel the width of a cathedral, carved by wind through black rock. Its walls are terraced, and on every terrace grow bean bushes whose pods glow a soft, sick gold, lighting the tunnel like a thousand lanterns. The wind never stops. It pours down the tunnel in waves, and every wave carries voices: whispers, sobs, laughter, snatches of song.

Along the terraces, figures in grey sacking move slowly, picking, humming. They do not look up. They hum the same four notes, over and over, and you realise the wind is humming them too.

DM Description

Pandemonium’s madness: every hour on-plane, each creature makes [[/save ability=wis dc=14]] @FWSave[S11|ability=wis dc=14|Pandemonium’s wind]{Request}. On a failure, the character forgets one thing (the player chooses: a name, a place, a skill they learned, the face of a loved one). Three failures: the character starts humming and must be led.

The plantations are a maze of tunnels; the harvesters, the overseer’s station and the processing shed are deeper in. Harvesting a sack takes 1 hour per character.

Features of the Area

Terraces
Climbing between them: [[/check skill=ath dc=13]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=ath dc=13|Climb the terraces]{Request}.
Wind gusts
At initiative 20, roll [[/r 1d6]]: on a 1, a gust; each creature in the open makes [[/save ability=str dc=15]] @FWSave[S11|ability=str dc=15|Brace against the gust]{Request} or is pushed 15 ft.
Glowing pods
Tasting a bean: [[/save ability=wis dc=15]] @FWSave[S11|ability=wis dc=15|Resist Compliance]{Request} or become agreeable (disadvantage on checks to refuse a request) for an hour.
Echo-vents
Shouting into one carries a message through the tunnels.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Navigating[[/check skill=sur dc=15]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=sur dc=15|Navigate the wind tunnels]{Request}You find the harvesters’ camp.
Identifying the beans[[/check skill=nat dc=16]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=nat dc=16|What are these beans?]{Request}Not coffee. They drink in madness and give back calm.

Developments

  • The party reaches the harvesters.

Scaling & Pacing

Weak party: madness save every two hours.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-24-pandemonium-bean-plantations]{The harvesters’ terraces}
When: Deeper in
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.ada-fairweather]{Ada Fairweather}, harvesters
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S11|The Scratched Wall]{The Scratched Wall} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S11|The Scratched Wall]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S11|Agnes’s Letter (if allied)]{Agnes’s Letter (if allied)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S11|Agnes’s Letter (if allied)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

One harvester has stopped humming. She is thin, with grey sacking for a dress and a sack of glowing beans over her shoulder, and she is staring at a scratch in the rock wall. She has scratched one word, over and over, hundreds of times, until the stone is pale with it: MOLLY.

“That’s my daughter,” she says, when she sees you looking. “I think that’s my daughter. I can’t remember anything else.”

DM Description

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.ada-fairweather]{Ada Fairweather} is Agnes Fairweather’s sister (S04), taken when ABI broke the Starkfucks union. She remembers only her daughter’s name—Molly—and nothing else. Agnes has looked after Molly since.

If the party carries Agnes’s letter, or describes Agnes, Ada weeps and starts to remember. She knows the harvest routine, the overseer’s patrol and the way to the processing shed. She also knows how many harvesters there are: forty-one. “We can’t leave. Where would we go?”

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.ada-fairweather]{Ada Fairweather}. Quiet, careful, holding onto one word. As memories return she becomes braver and angrier. She will lead the harvesters out if someone gives her a reason.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Reaching Ada[[/check skill=per dc=13]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=per dc=13|Reach Ada through the fog]{Request}She remembers her name and Agnes’s.
Rousing the harvesters[[/check skill=prf dc=15]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=prf dc=15|Wake the harvesters from their hum]{Request}They stop humming and listen. (Advantage with Ada’s help.)
Healing a mindlesser restoration / greater restorationRestores one harvester’s memory (or the character’s own).

Lines to Steal

Ada: “That’s my daughter. I think that’s my daughter.”
A harvester: “Where would we go? The shift is all there is.”

Developments

  • The harvesters will follow if the overseer is dealt with.

pages.name: Scene 4 — The Overseer
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-25-pandemonium-overseers-station]{Open battlemap}
When: Shift change
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.skarrow-vane]{Skarrow Vane, cambion overseer}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.howler]{howlers}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.air-elemental]{wind-elemental storm}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S11|The Quota Board]{The Quota Board} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S11|The Quota Board]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The overseer’s station sits on a stone spur over a great wind-chasm: a watchtower, a whipping post, a quota board chalked with harvester numbers, and a long shed with brass doors from which comes the smell of roasting. Riding up the spur on a howler—a hound with too many teeth and a mouth that screams—comes a tall, handsome figure in an ABI quality-control tabard, horns polished, whip coiled on his hip.

“Contractors!” Skarrow Vane says. “Wonderful. You’re behind quota.”

DM Description

Skarrow Vane, a cambion, oversees the harvest for a bonus. He signs for the sacks and can be bargained with (he is greedy) or fought. If the party tries to free the harvesters, he whistles: four howlers and a living storm (two air elementals) come down the chasm.

Beating him opens the processing shed: brass roasters, packing tables and crates stamped COMPLIANCE — FOR ALL ABI BRANCHES.

Features of the Area

The chasm
Falling: 6d6 bludgeoning (the wind slows the fall—roll [[/r 6d6]]); the wind can hurl a creature back up on a gust.
The watchtower
Height advantage; Vane’s ledger of quotas.
The quota board
Each harvester as a number.
Processing shed
Roasters (fire hazard), crates of Compliance, an ABI shipping manifest.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.skarrow-vane]{Skarrow Vane}. Smooth, mocking, bonus-motivated. Will sell out ABI for a better offer but always try to take both payments.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Bribing Vane[[/check skill=per dc=16]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=per dc=16|Make Vane a better offer]{Request}He looks away for an hour (and later reports it).
Intimidating Vane[[/check skill=itm dc=17]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=itm dc=17|Make Vane back down]{Request}He flees on his howler.
Disabling the roasters[[/check skill=inv dc=14]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=inv dc=14|Sabotage the roasters]{Request} (or tinker’s tools)The shed can’t process the crop.

Developments

  • The processing shed is open.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 9: cambion + 4 howlers + 2 air elementals. Weak: 2 howlers, 1 elemental.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-25-pandemonium-overseers-station]{Open battlemap}
When: The portal’s last hour
Present: Ada and the harvesters
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S11|The Harvesters’ Testimony]{The Harvesters’ Testimony} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S11|The Harvesters’ Testimony]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The processing shed is warm and smells like the best cup of coffee you have ever had—which makes it worse. Crate after crate stands ready for shipping, each stamped with the names of ABI branches across Brandmere. Behind you, forty-one harvesters stand in the doorway, waiting to see what you will do.

DM Description

Three choices, which can be combined:

Harvest as contracted. Twelve sacks back through the portal; full fee; Compliance keeps flowing.Burn or poison the crop. Ends Compliance for the season. ABI will know who did it.Free the harvesters. Lead forty-one people back through the portal before it closes. They give testimony—signed with handshakes, not quills—and join the Commons Tally.

Returning through the portal restores most forgotten memories. Each character who failed three or more saves loses one memory permanently (the player chooses).

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Burning the crop[[/check skill=sur dc=12]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=sur dc=12|Set the fields alight with the wind]{Request}The terraces burn for a day.
Leading the harvesters out[[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=per dc=14|Keep forty-one people moving]{Request}Everyone makes it. Failure: [[/r 1d6]] are lost to the wind.
Getting through the closing portal[[/save ability=dex dc=14]] @FWSave[S11|ability=dex dc=14|Dive through the closing portal]{Request}Through.

Developments

  • Back in Brandmere: Ada and Agnes reunited; Molly meets her mother.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS12 · Act III
Grade / LevelGold · Level 9–10
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-34]{Goodberry’s} (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-04]{ABI Wellness}) — opposed by the temples
Session length1–2 sessions: a crisis, a heist and a court case
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S12|Scene 1 — Temples in Crisis]{Scene 1 — Temples in Crisis} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-26-temple-healing-hand]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S12|Scene 2 — The Shrine]{Scene 2 — The Shrine} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-26-temple-healing-hand]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S12|Scene 3 — Goodberry’s Head Office]{Scene 3 — Goodberry’s Head Office} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-27-goodberrys-head-office]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S12|Scene 4 — The Trademark Hearing]{Scene 4 — The Trademark Hearing} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-28-guild-arbitration-court]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S12|Scene 5 — Freeing Healing]{Scene 5 — Freeing Healing} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-27-goodberrys-head-office]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.brother-allard]{Brother Allard}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.sister-wren]{Sister Wren}, Arbiter Maud Penhallow, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.rakshasa]{Messrs Sallow & Tine}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S12]{The Healing Deed}

Synopsis

Brother Allard of Death Save Delivery sends word: clerics across Brandmere cannot heal. Cure wounds fizzles; potions taste of chalk; prayers get a polite refusal. Outside every temple stands a Goodberry’s licensing booth selling HEALING™ by the prayer. People are dying on temple floors.

At the oldest shrine, Sister Wren confesses: years ago she signed away Healing’s deed to save her dying son. It was a Goodberry’s wellness contract. The deed is now in ABI Wellness’s vault at Goodberry’s Head Office—alongside the deeds to Sleep, Courage and Weekends.

The party can steal the deed in a heist through a wellness-themed office of meditation rooms and juice bars, or force a trademark hearing at the Guild Arbitration Court and argue that Healing cannot be owned. Either way, writing “owned by nobody” on the deed sets Healing free.

Background — DM Only

In the Ledger, a concept can be owned like land. Creation & Company’s subsidiaries have spent decades acquiring them quietly: Rest (Nine Circles), Weekends (Planar Hospitality), Sleep and Courage (ABI). Healing was the boldest purchase: obtained from its keeper under duress, it is now licensed back to the world.

Concepts that are owned but unused are stored in the Third Place, the grey limbo where the Company keeps what it has acquired and forgotten. Healing itself—a thin, kind presence—is there now (S17).

Goodberry’s is ABI’s wellness brand: berries, juice cleanses and smiling druids who “heal 1 hp per berry, terms apply”.

Running This Mission

  • Open on the crisis: someone dies who shouldn’t. Make the stakes personal (a recurring NPC injured in an earlier mission).
  • Sister Wren is not a villain. Let her confession land.
  • Offer both routes—heist or hearing. The hearing is a structured debate with three arguments.
  • Party healers are affected too. Their spells require a licence (see the Licence handout). Paying is an option—and a moral cost.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Brother Allard (Death Save Delivery); ABI after @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11]{S11}.
  • Out: Healing, the personified concept, remains in the Third Place until @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S17]{S17}; Allard’s temple becomes a Last Independents sanctuary.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The message comes by a temple runner, a boy of ten with blood on his sleeves that isn’t his. “Brother Allard says come,” he gasps. “The prayers don’t work. Nobody can heal. There’s a man at the Lantern who fell off a roof and they’ve been praying over him all night and nothing’s happening, and there’s a booth outside selling—” he swallows— “selling healing. For money. Please come.”

pages.name: Scene 1 — Temples in Crisis
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-26-temple-healing-hand]{Open battlemap}
When: Morning
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.brother-allard]{Brother Allard}, the wounded, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.druid]{a Goodberry’s licensing druid}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S12|HEALING™ Trademark Notice]{HEALING™ Trademark Notice} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S12|HEALING™ Trademark Notice]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S12|HEALING™ Licence (per prayer)]{HEALING™ Licence (per prayer)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S12|HEALING™ Licence (per prayer)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Temple of the Healing Hand is full. Pews have been pushed aside to make room for pallets, and on every pallet lies someone hurt: a roofer with a broken back, a child burning with fever, a guardsman with a sword-cut that will not close. Clerics kneel among them, praying, hands glowing—and the glow flickers and dies, again and again, like a candle in a draught.

Outside, on the temple steps, stands a neat green booth with a striped awning and a smiling young druid in a Goodberry’s apron. A sign reads: HEALING™ — LICENSED BY THE PRAYER. FIRST CONSULTATION FREE.

DM Description

Every healing spell cast without a licence fails unless the caster succeeds on a [[/check skill=rel dc=18]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=rel dc=18|Force a prayer through the trademark]{Request} (the spell slot is spent either way). Potions of healing heal only the minimum. A licence costs 10 gp per spell level, per cast, paid to Goodberry’s.

Brother Allard has spent all the temple’s coin on licences and run out. He asks the party to find out who owns Healing and how it was sold. The druid at the booth, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.fennel]{Fennel}, is cheerful and honestly thinks this is good business.

Features of the Area

Pallets of wounded
Stabilising: [[/check skill=med dc=12]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=med dc=12|Stabilise a wounded patient]{Request} (no magic needed).
The altar
An old hand-shaped altar; the shrine beneath it is older still.
Licensing booth
Ledger, receipts, a cash box, berry samples.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.brother-allard]{Brother Allard}. Big, kind, exhausted, his hands shaking from praying all night. He runs Death Save Delivery, the temple’s ambulance service. He is furious and too tired to show it.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.druid]{@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.fennel]{Fennel} (Goodberry’s druid)}. Sunny, sincere, completely misguided. Will refund a licence if shown someone dying because of it—and quit, if pushed.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Questioning @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.fennel]{Fennel}[[/check skill=per dc=13]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=per dc=13|Question the licensing druid]{Request}The trademark was “acquired from the shrine”—Sister Wren’s shrine.
Studying a failed spell[[/check skill=arc dc=15]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=arc dc=15|Why do the spells fail?]{Request}The word has been taken. Spells reach for Healing and find a locked door.
Shaming @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.fennel]{Fennel}[[/check skill=itm dc=14]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=itm dc=14|Show @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.fennel]{Fennel} the dying]{Request} or PersuasionShe quits and gives the party her ABI keycard.

Developments

  • Allard sends the party to Sister Wren’s shrine.

pages.name: Scene 2 — The Shrine
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-26-temple-healing-hand]{The shrine beneath the temple}
When: Midday
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.sister-wren]{Sister Wren}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S12|Wren’s Copy of the Wellness Agreement]{Wren’s Copy of the Wellness Agreement} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S12|Wren’s Copy of the Wellness Agreement]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Beneath the temple, down worn stone steps, is a shrine no bigger than a cottage kitchen: a spring in a stone basin, a single lamp, a wall of handprints pressed into old plaster—every one a healing given here, over centuries. The spring has stopped. The lamp is out. An old woman in a grey habit sits beside the dry basin with her hands in her lap.

“You’ve come about the deed,” Sister Wren says. “I know. I’m the one who sold it.”

DM Description

Sister Wren was the keeper of Healing’s shrine. Twelve years ago her son @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.tobin]{Tobin} was dying of the grey fever. A Goodberry’s wellness consultant offered a cure in exchange for “a simple licensing agreement”. She signed. @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.tobin]{Tobin} lived. Healing became a trademark.

She explains: the deed to Healing is held by ABI Wellness in a vault of trademarks at Goodberry’s Head Office. If someone writes “owned by nobody” on the deed, Healing returns to the world. She cannot do it herself—her signature is the problem.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.sister-wren]{Sister Wren}. Small, upright, unflinching. She does not ask for forgiveness and does not justify herself. She would do it again. Her son @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.tobin]{Tobin}, now twenty-two, works at Goodberry’s Head Office as a juice-bar attendant and knows nothing.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Comforting Wren[[/check skill=ins dc=14]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=ins dc=14|Understand Sister Wren]{Request}She would do it again, and she knows what it cost.
Reading her copy of the contract[[/check skill=inv dc=16]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=inv dc=16|Read Wren’s copy of the contract]{Request}Clause 3: the deed is “held in trust at the Licensor’s principal office”—and a hearing may be demanded by any “affected party”.

Lines to Steal

Sister Wren: “I’m the one who sold it. I’d do it again.”

Developments

  • Two routes: the heist (Scene 3) or the hearing (Scene 4).

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Goodberry’s Head Office looks like a garden that has been told to behave: white stone, living walls of green, a lobby with a burbling fountain and a smell of crushed mint. A sign by the lifts lists the floors: MEDITATION · JUICE BAR · NUTRITIONAL ALIGNMENT · LEGAL. Somewhere a harp is playing. The security guards wear plate armour painted a calming sage green.

DM Description

A heist. The vault of trademarks is on the Legal floor, behind the meditation rooms (which are silence-enchanted—useful) and the juice bar (where @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.tobin]{Tobin} works). Security: four knights in sage plate, wards on the vault, and the ABI legal team—two rakshasas in lawyer suits—working late.

The vault holds the deeds to Healing, Sleep, Courage and Weekends, each a thick vellum document under glass. The party can take Healing’s—or more.

Features of the Area

Meditation rooms
Permanent silence; perfect for sneaking.
Juice bar
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.tobin]{Tobin}; a blender loud enough to cover a break-in.
Nutritional Alignment
Druid offices; a living wall that is also a shambling mound (optional).
Legal
Rakshasa offices; the vault of trademarks.
The vault
Glass cases; wards ([[/check skill=arc dc=17]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=arc dc=17|Disarm the vault wards]{Request}).

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.tobin]{Tobin}. Twenty-two, cheerful, a little lost. If told the truth about his mother, he is horrified and helps—he has a staff keycard.

  • If caught, the rakshasas demand a hearing instead of a fight: they prefer to win in court.

pages.name: Scene 4 — The Trademark Hearing
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-28-guild-arbitration-court]{Open battlemap}
When: The next morning (if the party is caught or demands a hearing)
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.rakshasa]{ABI legal team (Messrs Sallow & Tine)}, Arbiter Maud Penhallow
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S12|Order of the Guild Arbitration Court]{Order of the Guild Arbitration Court} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S12|Order of the Guild Arbitration Court]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Guild Arbitration Court is a round hall of dark wood under a dome painted with scales. The public gallery is packed: clerics in torn robes, the families of the wounded, curious guild-folk. At one table sit two impeccable lawyers in charcoal suits, with gloves on and smiles a little too wide. At the bench, Arbiter Maud Penhallow, a dwarf with spectacles and a gavel the size of a hammer, peers down.

“The matter of ABI Wellness against the Commons,” she says. “Regarding the ownership of Healing. Counsel for the Commons, you may begin.”

DM Description

A debate in three rounds. Each round, the party makes an argument and a check (DC 16); evidence grants advantage. The ABI lawyers counter each round with a rebuttal (which the party can undercut with Insight).

Round 1 — Can a concept be owned? [[/check skill=rel dc=16]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=rel dc=16|Argue that Healing belongs to no one]{Request} or History. Evidence: the shrine’s handprints.Round 2 — Was the sale fair? [[/check skill=per dc=16]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=per dc=16|Argue the sale was made under duress]{Request}. Evidence: Sister Wren’s testimony.Round 3 — Public harm. [[/check skill=ins dc=16]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=ins dc=16|Show the court the harm]{Request} or Persuasion. Evidence: the wounded, the licences, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.fennel]{Fennel}’s testimony.

Two successes win the hearing; the arbiter orders the deed released. Three successes and the arbiter also voids Sleep, Courage and Weekends.

Features of the Area

The gallery
Can be roused (Performance DC 14) for advantage on Round 3.
The rakshasas
Will try to cast suggestion on the arbiter—spotted with [[/check skill=prc dc=17]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=prc dc=17|Spot the lawyers’ spell]{Request}.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Spotting the rakshasas’ true nature[[/check skill=ins dc=18]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=ins dc=18|What are these lawyers?]{Request}Their hands are reversed inside their gloves.

Developments

  • If the party loses, or the rakshasas are exposed, the lawyers drop the pretence and attack, with four knights and a druid.

pages.name: Scene 5 — Freeing Healing
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-27-goodberrys-head-office]{Goodberry’s Head Office — the vault}
When: Climax
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.sister-wren]{Sister Wren}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.brother-allard]{Brother Allard}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The deed to Healing is a single sheet of thick, soft vellum, warm to the touch, like a hand that has been holding another. At the top, in a hand older than the city: Healing, given freely, to whoever has need. Beneath it, newer ink: Assigned to ABI Wellness Ltd. All Rights Reserved. And beneath that, a shaky signature: Wren.

DM Description

Writing “owned by nobody” on the deed frees Healing. The moment the ink dries, every healing spell in Brandmere works again; the spring in the shrine flows; across the city, people who were dying sit up. Healing itself—thin, kind, very tired—does not return to the world immediately: it has been in the Third Place too long, and lingers there until S17.

The other deeds (Sleep, Courage, Weekends) can be freed the same way if the party has them. Each freed concept goes on to the Commons Tally.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Writing the words—No roll. Anyone can write it. Sister Wren asks to—it releases her too.

Developments

  • Healing is free; the licensing booths close by noon; @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.fennel]{Fennel} quits.

pages.html:

Mission at a Glance

Grade / LevelGold · Level 10

Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S13|Scene 1 — The Franchisee]{Scene 1 — The Franchisee} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-29-chickn-familiar-midnight-kitchen]{map}

@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S13|Scene 3 — Counsel Ixabeth Vorr]{Scene 3 — Counsel Ixabeth Vorr} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-29-chickn-familiar-midnight-kitchen]{map}

@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S13|Scene 5 — The Offer]{Scene 5 — The Offer} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-30-nine-circles-legal-floor]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-31]{Wendel Clasp}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.counsel-ixabeth-vorr]{Counsel Ixabeth Vorr}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-08.controlled-by]{Duke Malphas Vellichor}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.quasit]{Chickadee}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S13]{Infernal Due-Diligence Report}

Synopsis

Wendel Clasp, a human wizard who swears he read the franchise agreement, runs the Magus Ward Chick’n Familiar. Ten years ago he signed with Nine Circles Hospitality. The consideration was “one soul, payable on maturity”. Maturity is midnight tonight. He begs the party for help.

At midnight a barbed devil collector arrives with a contract and a bucket. The contract has a loophole—the payment is “the first soul that enters the restaurant after midnight”—and the party can send in a chicken. Or argue. Or fight.

Then Counsel Ixabeth Vorr, an erinyes attorney, appears, amused. She’ll enforce the loophole if the party carries her due-diligence report to someone who can use it. The report says something astonishing: Creation & Company’s claim on the Material Plane is contested under infernal law—because Hell is being acquired too. Duke Vellichor wants an alliance. “Even Hell has antitrust concerns.”

Background — DM Only

Nine Circles Hospitality is Creation & Company’s infernal umbrella: Seven-Eleven Hells, Chick’n Familiar, the Long Rest Inn. Duke Malphas Vellichor, a pit fiend, signed a partnership with the Company centuries ago and has discovered—through Ixabeth’s due diligence—that the partnership terms let Tallis Vend absorb the Nine Hells on the same night he takes the Material Plane.

Infernal law is strict about contracts and very strict about jurisdiction. If Hell has a competing claim on the Material Plane, then the Final Contract’s Governing Law clause is false. Vellichor needs someone mortal and credible to carry that into the Counting House.

Chickadee, the Chick’n Familiar mascot, is an actual quasit in a chicken suit. It is loyal to nobody and will do whatever is funniest.

Running This Mission

  • Run it in real time if you can: a candle clock on the table counting to midnight.
  • The loophole is a gift. Let the players feel clever.
  • Ixabeth is the best lawyer in the multiverse and knows it. She enjoys the party.
  • Vellichor’s offer is a genuine choice with long consequences.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Chick’n Familiar’s franchise contract; @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-08]{Nine Circles}.
  • Out: Hell is an uneasy ally. Ixabeth Vorr represents the party at the AGM (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S20]{S20}); Vellichor’s vote in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S23]{S23}; Avernus in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S22]{S22}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Wendel Clasp is waiting outside the QuestRabbit office when you arrive, in a wizard’s robe with a Chick’n Familiar name badge pinned crookedly to the front. He is clutching a document in both hands and he has clearly not slept.

“I read it,” he says, before anyone can speak. “I swear I read it. Everyone said read the small print and I read the small print. But there’s smaller print. Under the small print. In red.” He holds it out. “It’s due at midnight. Please.”

pages.name: Scene 1 — The Franchisee
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-29-chickn-familiar-midnight-kitchen]{Open battlemap}
When: Evening (six hours to midnight)
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-31]{Wendel Clasp}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.quasit]{Chickadee, the mascot}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S13|Chick’n Familiar Franchise Agreement]{Chick’n Familiar Franchise Agreement} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S13|Chick’n Familiar Franchise Agreement]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S13|Matured Invoice]{Matured Invoice} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S13|Matured Invoice]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Magus Ward Chick’n Familiar is a red-and-white shop on a corner full of wizards’ towers. Inside: buckets stacked on the counter, fryers hissing, a menu board of FAMILIAR MEALS (“Owl Wings”, “Toad-in-the-Bucket”), and a mascot in a fuzzy yellow chicken suit dancing by the door to a tune only it can hear. As you pass, the mascot turns its head all the way round, and its eyes behind the mesh glow red.

DM Description

Wendel explains: the contract’s consideration is “one soul, payable on maturity”; ten years; tonight. He has tried to cancel, sell, and dissolve the franchise. Nothing works.

The party has six hours to prepare: read the contract, research devils, set traps, consult lawyers. Chickadee (a quasit) watches everything and reports to whoever bribes it best.

Features of the Area

Fryers
Boiling oil: 3d6 fire to anyone pushed in—roll [[/r 3d6]].
The bucket stack
Hundreds of empty buckets.
Wendel’s office
Spellbooks, a framed franchise certificate, a hidden magic circle he drew badly.
Walk-in cooler
Crates of chicken—and live chickens for “freshness”.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-31]{Wendel Clasp}. Anxious, pedantic, desperate. A competent wizard with terrible judgement. He will do anything except lose.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.quasit]{Chickadee}. Chaotic. Will steal the contract, swap it, hide it, or give it to the devil—whatever is funniest. Can be bought with a bucket of chicken and a promise of mischief.

SituationRollResult
Reading the contract[[/check skill=inv dc=18]] @FWCheck[S13|skill=inv dc=18|Find the loophole]{Request}Payment is “the first soul that enters the restaurant after midnight”—not Wendel’s.
Knowing devils[[/check skill=rel dc=15]] @FWCheck[S13|skill=rel dc=15|What do you know about infernal collectors?]{Request}They must honour the letter of a contract. They hate it.
Spotting Chickadee[[/check skill=prc dc=14]] @FWCheck[S13|skill=prc dc=14|Is the mascot… real?]{Request}A quasit in a chicken suit.

Developments

  • Prepare for midnight.

pages.name: Scene 2 — The Midnight Invoice
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.collector-grix]{Collector Grix (barbed devil)}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.imp]{imps}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.chain-devil]{a chain devil}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

At the twelfth stroke the lights go out. The fryers stop hissing. The smell of chicken becomes the smell of sulphur. The front door, which was locked, swings open, and in walks a devil covered in barbs, eight feet tall, in a tidy waistcoat, carrying a briefcase in one hand and an empty Chick’n Familiar bucket in the other.

“Collector Grix, Nine Circles Accounts Receivable,” it says. “I’m here for the consideration.” It sets the bucket on the counter. “Who’s first?”

DM Description

Grix must take the first soul to enter after midnight. If the party sent a chicken in at 12:00:01, Grix glares, checks the contract, and—bound by the letter—puts the chicken’s soul in the bucket. Furious, it then tries to provoke a breach (if anyone attacks it, the contract is “disputed” and it can call for enforcement: four imps and a chain devil).

If the party has no loophole, Grix claims Wendel. The party can argue (see checks), fight, or bargain.

Features of the Area

The doorway
Whoever crosses first after midnight is the payment.
Darkness
Lights out; the devils see in it.
Chains
The chain devil animates the shop’s chains (the bucket rack, the queue barriers).

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Arguing with Grix[[/check skill=per dc=18]] @FWCheck[S13|skill=per dc=18|Argue the contract with Grix]{Request}Grix concedes a point and must confer with counsel. (Ixabeth arrives.)
Catching Grix out[[/check skill=ins dc=16]] @FWCheck[S13|skill=ins dc=16|Read the collector]{Request}Grix is on commission and terrified of a bad review.
The chicken trick—If arranged in advance, it simply works.

Developments

  • Ixabeth Vorr arrives, amused, before the fight escalates.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 10: barbed devil + 4 imps + chain devil.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-29-chickn-familiar-midnight-kitchen]{Open battlemap}

Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.counsel-ixabeth-vorr]{Counsel Ixabeth Vorr}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

A woman steps out of the dark beside the counter as if she had always been there: tall, black-winged, in a perfectly cut suit the colour of dried blood, with a silver pen behind one ear. She looks at the chicken in the bucket and laughs—a real, delighted laugh.

“Oh, that’s good,” she says. “That’s very good. Grix, go home.” The barbed devil goes, without a word. She turns to you. “Counsel Ixabeth Vorr. Nine Circles. I’d like to hire you.”

DM Description

Ixabeth enforces the loophole (Wendel is free; the franchise is dissolved) in exchange for a favour: carry her due-diligence report to “someone who can use it”. She explains its contents with relish.

She is an erinyes, a fallen angel of law, and the best attorney in the multiverse. She respects precision and cleverness and despises cruelty that isn’t billable.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.counsel-ixabeth-vorr]{Counsel Ixabeth Vorr}. Delighted by good arguments; bored by bad ones. Never lies; omits beautifully. She treats the party as promising junior associates.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Negotiating with Ixabeth[[/check skill=per dc=17]] @FWCheck[S13|skill=per dc=17|Negotiate terms with Ixabeth]{Request}She adds her card: one free legal representation, anywhere, any plane.
Reading her[[/check skill=ins dc=19]] @FWCheck[S13|skill=ins dc=19|What does Ixabeth really want?]{Request}She wants to win a case against Tallis Vend. Nobody ever has.

Lines to Steal

Ixabeth: “Oh, that’s good. That’s very good.”
Ixabeth: “I never lie. I simply decline to volunteer.”

Developments

  • She takes the party to the Nine Circles legal floor.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Nine Circles legal floor is reached by a lift that goes down further than the building should. Its doors open on an open-plan office of black marble, lit by braziers: hundreds of desks, each with a quill scratching by itself and an imp clerk filing. Along one wall, a window looks out—not onto Brandmere but onto a red plain under a burning sky.

DM Description

Ixabeth shows the party the report. Its findings: under infernal law, Creation & Company’s claims on the Material Plane are not recognised; Hell itself has a competing jurisdictional claim (by ancient treaty); and the Nine Circles partnership allows Tallis Vend to absorb the Nine Hells on Acquisition Night. Hell is being acquired. Hell does not like it.

The report is the Receipt. Whoever carries it into the Counting House can contest the Final Contract’s Governing Law.

Features of the Area

Self-writing desks
Each a contract in progress; reading one: [[/check skill=inv dc=15]] @FWCheck[S13|skill=inv dc=15|Read an infernal contract]{Request}.

A view of Avernus (a preview of S22).
Ixabeth’s office
Glass walls, a bonsai of thorns, the report.

pages.name: Scene 5 — The Offer
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-30-nine-circles-legal-floor]{Nine Circles — Duke Vellichor’s office}
When: Before dawn
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-08.controlled-by]{Duke Malphas Vellichor}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.counsel-ixabeth-vorr]{Ixabeth Vorr}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S13|Vellichor’s Alliance Offer]{Vellichor’s Alliance Offer} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S13|Vellichor’s Alliance Offer]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Duke Vellichor’s office is the size of a cathedral and almost empty: a desk of black iron, two chairs, and behind the desk a pit fiend in a tailored suit, wings folded, sipping something that steams. He does not stand.

“Sit,” he says, in a voice like a furnace door opening. “You’ve read the report. You understand my position. Creation & Company intends to own the Nine Hells by the end of the year. Even Hell has antitrust concerns.” He sets down his cup. “I propose an alliance.”

DM Description

Vellichor offers an alliance against Tallis Vend: Nine Circles will vote against the Final Acquisition (S23), block the road through Avernus (S22) and lend Ixabeth to the party at the AGM (S20). In exchange: the party carries the report, and—small print—grants Nine Circles “first refusal” on any franchise the party ever owns.

The party can accept, refuse or negotiate. If they refuse, he offers a smaller deal: his vote in S23 in exchange for the report reaching the Counting House.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-08.controlled-by]{Duke Malphas Vellichor}. Enormous, calm, reasonable—terrifyingly so. He never threatens. He states facts. He keeps every bargain to the letter.

Developments

  • Hell is an uneasy ally—or a watchful neutral.

The Twist

If the party refuses Vellichor’s alliance, he offers a smaller one: his vote in S23 in exchange for the report reaching the Counting House.

Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.dobbs]{Dobbs}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.clerk-first-sale]{The Clerk of the First Sale}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-01]{Hollis Quench}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S14]{The First Entry}

Synopsis

Hollis Quench calls the party: the iron door in THAC0 Spell’s cellar—sealed since before the party’s first job, the one Dobbs went missing near—is open. Beyond it, stairs go down for too long. And at the bottom, behind a counter, stands Dobbs, the missing line cook, calm and blank, serving customers.

The First Shop is every shop: a counter, a scale, a till, a bell. Customers who have waited centuries queue patiently. Ghostly clerks from every era work behind the counter. They are not hostile. They will serve the party. But buying anything means signing.

Behind the counter, on a lectern, is a page torn from the Grand Ledger’s first volume: Entry 1. Tallis Vend owns Tallis Vend, in perpetuity. Witnessed by: Tallis Vend. The party can take it—and four Compliance Officers will come for it. Beyond the lectern is a grey door marked STAFF ONLY. Behind it, a quill scratches.

Background — DM Only

Four hundred years ago a mortal clerk named Tallis Vend kept the books at the first shop: the first place where something was bought and sold. One night he wrote himself into the shop’s ledger as its owner, and himself as his own witness. That self-witnessed entry became the foundation of the Grand Ledger and of Creation & Company.

The First Shop never closed. Its customers are the first people ever to be sold something; they are waiting for change. The clerks are every shop worker who ever signed a contract of employment with a Company subsidiary and died in service.

Dobbs wandered through the door on the party’s first night at THAC0 Spell (S01) and took a shift. He has been working for what feels to him like an afternoon.

Running This Mission

  • This is the campaign’s quietest, eeriest mission. Slow everything down. No music.
  • The Clerk of the First Sale is the shop’s conscience, not a boss monster. Fight only if the party is careless.
  • Buying anything means signing: make it clear the moment anyone reaches for a coin.
  • The Staff Only door cannot be opened yet. Let them hear the quill.

Threads In and Out

  • In: the iron door and Dobbs (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S01]{S01}).
  • Out: the party knows where the Counting House is; the Staff Only door opens in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S20]{S20}; Entry 1 is the key to @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S24]{S24}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Hollis Quench sounds strange on the speaking-stone: not panicked, but hushed, as if afraid of being overheard in his own kitchen. “The door’s open,” he says. “The iron one. In the cellar. I went down to fetch a keg and it was just… open.” A long pause. “There are stairs. I didn’t go down. But I could hear a bell. A shop bell. And Dobbs. I heard Dobbs say, ‘Next, please.’”

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

THAC0 Spell’s cellar is as you remember it: kegs, crates, the smell of old ale and dragon-pepper. But at the far end, the iron door—the door that has been rusted shut since the tavern was built—stands open a hand’s width. Cold air breathes through the gap. It smells of dust, old coins and candle-wax.

Beyond, a stone staircase spirals down. You count a hundred steps before you lose sight of it. Far below, so faint you are not sure you heard it, a small bell rings: ting.

DM Description

The stairs go down for too long: roughly an hour of descent, though only a few minutes pass above. Time behaves oddly—each hour below is a minute above.

Along the walls, carved into the stone, are tally marks: millions of them, the oldest worn smooth.

Features of the Area

The iron door
Inscribed in old script: FIRST SHOP — OPEN.
The stairs
Endless; [[/save ability=con dc=12]] @FWSave[S14|ability=con dc=12|The long descent]{Request} or gain a level of exhaustion, recovered on return.
Tally marks
Each a sale.

pages.name: Scene 2 — The First Shop
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-31-franchise-below-first-shop]{Open battlemap}
When: Below (time uncertain)
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.dobbs]{Dobbs}, the waiting customers

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The stairs end in a room that is every shop you have ever been in. A wooden counter, worn into a dip by centuries of elbows. A brass scale. A till with a crank. A bell on a spring above the door. Shelves of jars and bolts of cloth and loaves and lamps, all faintly translucent, like memories of goods.

A queue stretches from the counter, out of the room and into the dark: men and women in clothes from every century, holding coins, waiting patiently. At the counter, wearing a THAC0 Spell apron, stands Dobbs. He looks well. He looks calm. He looks right through you.

“Next, please,” he says.

DM Description

The customers are the first people ever sold something. They are waiting for change, and have been for centuries. They will talk, softly, if spoken to: about the price of bread, about a town long gone.

Dobbs believes he started his shift an hour ago. He is under the shop’s spell; he will serve the party courteously and does not recognise them. He can be freed (see Twist): if someone pays for his shift with a coin that means something to them.

Features of the Area

The counter
Worn; behind it, the lectern and the Staff Only door.
The scale
Weighs whatever is placed on it—including a soul.
The queue
Endless.
The bell
Rings when anyone enters or leaves. Every ring is a sale.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.dobbs]{Dobbs}. Polite, calm, blank. Responds to THAC0 Spell orders by habit: “one pepper-mash, extra crit”. A flicker of recognition if someone uses his nickname or mentions Hollis.

Talking to a customer[[/check skill=ins dc=12]] @FWCheck[S14|skill=ins dc=12|Listen to the waiting customers]{Request}They were the first to be sold something. They have forgotten what.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

From the back of the shop come the clerks: dozens of them, pale and translucent, in uniforms from every age—a Murder King paper crown, a Wand-Mart blue vest, a medieval guild apron, a Starkfucks green one. They are not hostile. They are busy. They smile the same tired smile.

An old, old clerk in a black coat steps to the counter, ink-stained fingers folded. “Welcome,” says the Clerk of the First Sale. “What can I get you?”

DM Description

The clerks will serve the party anything they ask for—a memory, a lost thing, a future—at a price. Buying anything means signing: the purchase is entered in the shop’s ledger, binding the buyer to the Company. (A purchase made here gives a real boon of the DM’s choice—and a real Ledger entry that Tallis Vend can use in S24.)

The Clerk of the First Sale was Tallis Vend’s apprentice. He saw what Vend wrote and said nothing. He has stood behind this counter for four centuries out of guilt.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.clerk-first-sale]{The Clerk of the First Sale}. Courteous, ancient, sorrowful. Tells the truth if asked directly. He will not stop the party from taking the page, but the shop will.

Lines to Steal

The Clerk: “Welcome. What can I get you?”
The Clerk: “I watched him write it. I said nothing. That is my sale.”

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Behind the counter, under a single candle, stands a lectern of black wood. On it lies a single page, torn from a very large book: yellowed, brittle, written in a small, precise hand. You lean close to read it.

Entry 1. Tallis Vend owns Tallis Vend, in perpetuity. Witnessed by: Tallis Vend.

As you read, the candle flame bends toward you, and somewhere far away, a bell rings that is not the shop bell.

DM Description

Taking the page triggers the shop’s defence: four Compliance Officers step out of the walls. The Clerk of the First Sale, weakened (lich statistics at half hp, no legendary actions), defends the lectern only if the party threatens the customers or Dobbs; otherwise he steps aside—“I said nothing once. I will say nothing again.”

The page is the First Entry, the Receipt: proof that Creation & Company’s founding act was a circular claim that no one else witnessed.

Features of the Area

The lectern
Removing the page: [[/check skill=slt dc=14]] @FWCheck[S14|skill=slt dc=14|Lift the page without tearing it]{Request} (a torn page still works but makes the Compliance Officers act first).
The queue
Customers stand still during combat; harming them angers the Clerk.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Behind the lectern is a second door: plain, grey, flush with the wall, without a handle. A small brass plate reads STAFF ONLY. You press your ear to it. On the other side, very faint, very steady, a quill is scratching—line after line after line, never pausing.

DM Description

The Staff Only door opens onto the Counting House, but not yet: it has no handle until the party is invited (S20). Nothing opens it now—not knock, not force, not wish.

Dobbs can be freed before leaving if someone pays for his shift with a coin that means something to them (a first wage, a lucky penny, a gift). The Clerk accepts it, rings the till, and says: “Shift over.” Dobbs blinks, sees the party, and starts to cry.

@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S15|Scene 2 — The Revenant King]{Scene 2 — The Revenant King} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-32-throne-tower-boardroom]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S15|Scene 3 — Baron Cleave]{Scene 3 — Baron Cleave} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-32-throne-tower-boardroom]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S15|Scene 4 — The Choice]{Scene 4 — The Choice} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-32-throne-tower-boardroom]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S15|Scene 5 — Aftermath]{Scene 5 — Aftermath} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-33-revenant-kings-crypt]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.aldric-the-unkind]{King Aldric the Unkind}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-03.controlled-by]{Baron Ossian Cleave}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S15]{Aldric’s Testimony}

Synopsis

Veronique Salt calls in a panic: “He’s in the Throne Tower. He’s eating everyone.” King Aldric the Unkind—the original Murder King, murdered four centuries ago by his steward, Ossian Cleave—has risen as a revenant, wearing the Promotional Crown from S05. He has fought his way to the top floor of Crown & Cleaver headquarters and is eating executives.

Aldric is proud, cruel and correct: his kingdom was stolen, his face turned into a mascot, his murder made into a brand. He demands his kingdom back and Cleave’s death. Then Baron Ossian Cleave—a death knight, controller of Crown & Cleaver—arrives with his guards, intending to kill Aldric and every witness.

The party can ally with Aldric against Cleave, stop both, or broker a deal: Aldric gets his revenge and relinquishes his claim. Veronique wants Cleave dead so she can take his seat; she helps—until she doesn’t.

Background — DM Only

Four hundred years ago Aldric was king of the land where Brandmere now stands: cruel, vain, and lawful. His steward, Ossian Cleave, murdered him with a meat cleaver at the royal feast and sold the kingdom—its land, its crown, its very name—to Tallis Vend in exchange for a Board seat and undeath. The Murder King brand was built from Aldric’s face as a joke.

Revenants rise to avenge a wrong. Aldric rose when the Promotional Crown (his real crown, recast as merchandise) was worn in the Throne Tower—an event the party may have triggered in S05.

Veronique has spent years undermining Cleave. If he is destroyed, Crown & Cleaver loses its Board seat and she becomes CEO.

Running This Mission

  • Aldric is not a misunderstood hero. He was a bad king. He is still right.
  • Cleave is the true villain of the piece: courteous, cold, and utterly without remorse.
  • Veronique’s turn should be telegraphed: she helps against Cleave until Aldric wins, then tries to kill Aldric to end the claim.
  • If the Rabbit Rating reaches five stars here, go straight to S16.

Threads In and Out

  • In: the Promotional Crown and the Vault Inventory (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05]{S05}); Veronique’s partnership (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S10]{S10}).
  • Out: end of Act III; Crown & Cleaver’s seat in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S23]{S23}; Aldric as a witness in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S24]{S24}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Veronique Salt has never sounded like this. Her voice on the speaking-stone is high and quick and there is screaming behind it. “He’s in the Throne Tower,” she says. “The king. The real one. He’s wearing the crown and he’s—” a crash, a wet sound— “he’s eating everyone. Budget unlimited. Come now. Please.”

Then, more quietly, almost to herself: “Cleave’s on his way. Get there first.”

When: Night

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Throne Tower is Crown & Cleaver’s headquarters: forty storeys of black glass and gold, shaped like a crown, its spires lit red. Tonight the red light is flickering. Executives in torn suits are fleeing out of the revolving doors into the square. One of them has a bite out of his shoulder. Another is not fleeing; he is shuffling, grey-faced, eyes glowing, back toward the tower.

Veronique meets you at the doors, her crimson coat spattered with something dark. “Top floor,” she says. “The boardroom. He’s turning them as he eats them. Go.”

DM Description

A siege up the tower. Aldric’s victims rise as wights (risen executives) and hold the stairs. Tower security (helmed horrors) is malfunctioning: they attack anything that isn’t wearing a Crown & Cleaver lanyard.

Run it as three short floors: Marketing (wights among mascot costumes), Accounts (a helmed horror; filing cabinets for cover), Executive (a corridor of portraits of Cleave through the centuries—and one of Aldric, with the face scratched out).

Features of the Area

Lifts
Stopped. The stairs are the only way up.
Mascot costumes
Murder King suits; a wight hides in one.
Portrait gallery
Cleave in every century, never ageing.
Lanyards
Wearing a C&C lanyard makes the helmed horrors ignore you.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}. Shaken, then very quickly composed. She comes with the party, staying behind them, and helps. She wants Aldric to kill Cleave, and then Aldric to die.

pages.name: Scene 2 — The Revenant King
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-32-throne-tower-boardroom]{Open battlemap}
When: The top floor
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.aldric-the-unkind]{King Aldric the Unkind}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The boardroom has been redecorated. The long table is overturned and dragged to the head of the room to make a dais. The chairs are piled into a throne. On the throne sits a figure in rotted royal robes, gaunt and grey, with burning eyes and a crown of gold that you have seen before—in a vault, on a velvet cushion, labelled PROMOTIONAL.

He is eating. He stops. He looks at you, and wipes his mouth with the back of a hand.

“More of Cleave’s servants,” says King Aldric the Unkind. “Kneel, or join the meal.”

DM Description

Aldric is proud, cruel and correct. He tells his story—he was murdered by his steward at his own feast, his kingdom sold, his face made a mascot—and makes his demands: his kingdom back, and Cleave’s death. He does not care how many people work here.

He can be talked to. He respects courage, despises grovelling, and will bargain with anyone who acknowledges that he was wronged. He will not relinquish his claim easily.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.aldric-the-unkind]{King Aldric the Unkind}. Regal, contemptuous, dangerous. He speaks like a king and expects to be addressed as one. He was never kind; he was always lawful. His one weakness: he wants his name back more than his kingdom.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Addressing him as king[[/check skill=per dc=17]] @FWCheck[S15|skill=per dc=17|Parley with the revenant king]{Request}He listens.
Understanding a revenant[[/check skill=rel dc=16]] @FWCheck[S15|skill=rel dc=16|What drives a revenant?]{Request}It cannot rest until its murderer is destroyed. After that, it will fade.
Spotting his weakness[[/check skill=ins dc=17]] @FWCheck[S15|skill=ins dc=17|What does Aldric really want?]{Request}His name restored, more than the throne.

Lines to Steal

Aldric: “Kneel, or join the meal.”
Aldric: “I was a bad king. I was still the king.”

Developments

  • Cleave arrives.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The lift, which was stopped, chimes. The doors slide open, and Baron Ossian Cleave steps out: tall, armoured in black plate under a perfectly tailored coat, a meat cleaver the size of a greatsword across his back. He takes in the room—the throne of chairs, the bodies, the king—and inclines his head politely.

“Your Majesty,” he says. “Again.” Then, to you, without turning: “Thank you for containing him. You may go. You were never here.”

DM Description

Cleave intends to destroy Aldric and kill every witness—including the party, Veronique, and any surviving executives. He is a death knight with a hellfire orb and absolute confidence.

Now there are three sides: Aldric, Cleave and the party (with Veronique wavering). The party chooses.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-03.controlled-by]{Baron Ossian Cleave}. Courteous, cold, utterly without remorse. He refers to the murder as “the transaction”. He is not afraid of anything except the Ledger.

For a moment nobody moves: the dead king on his throne of chairs, the murderer by the lift with his cleaver drawn, and you between them. Behind you, Veronique Salt says, very softly, “Choose.”

DM Description

The party’s options:

Ally with Aldric against Cleave. Two against one. When Cleave falls, Aldric’s purpose is fulfilled—and Veronique tries to kill the weakened king to end his claim. The party must stop her or let her.Stop both. A three-way fight. Hardest; most chaotic.Broker a deal. The party then helps (or watches) Aldric destroy Cleave.

If Cleave is destroyed, Crown & Cleaver loses its Board seat and Veronique becomes CEO.

The crypt beneath the Throne Tower was a royal tomb long before it was a basement: a vaulted chamber of old stone, with an empty sarcophagus carved with a king’s face—the real one, stern and unhandsome, not the cartoon on the burger boxes.

Aldric lowers himself onto the stone lid. The fire in his eyes is guttering. “Write it down,” he says. “All of it. My name, and what was done. Then let me sleep.”

DM Description

If Aldric’s vengeance is complete, he gives his testimony—the first acquired king, describing how his kingdom was sold—and fades. The party writes it down (the Receipt). He can return as a witness in S24 if called by name.

If Cleave is destroyed, Veronique is CEO of Crown & Cleaver by morning. She thanks the party, sincerely, and adds: “I’ll remember this.” She means both halves.
