pages.name: DM Overview
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS16 · Act IV
Grade / LevelPlatinum · Level 13
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-59]{Long Rest Inn} (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-08]{Nine Circles Hospitality})
Session length1 session; a mystery, a revelation, and a fight in a hotel corridor
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S16|Scene 1 — The Room]{Scene 1 — The Room} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-inn-01-long-rest-inn]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S16|Scene 2 — The Sleepers]{Scene 2 — The Sleepers} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-34-long-rest-inn-room-303]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S16|Scene 3 — The Truth]{Scene 3 — The Truth} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-34-long-rest-inn-room-303]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S16|Scene 4 — The Compliance Officers]{Scene 4 — The Compliance Officers} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-inn-01-long-rest-inn]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S16|Scene 5 — The Choice]{Scene 5 — The Choice} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-35-sleepers-dream]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.cadwyn-lark]{Cadwyn Lark}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.tomas-brand]{Tomas Brand}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.ysolde-fenn]{Ysolde Fenn}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.hark]{Hark}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-02.public-face]{Harriet Hopwell}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S16]{The Five-Star Testimony}

Synopsis

Pip, nervous, hands over a contract printed on black card: “They said you’re the only ones qualified.” Room 303 of the Long Rest Inn has displayed DO NOT DISTURB for ninety-four years. Corporate wants it cleaned and the guests checked out.

Behind the door is a time-stop field, a century of dust, and four legendary heroes asleep: Cadwyn Lark, Tomas Brand, Ysolde Fenn and Hark—the Last Five-Star Party, the only adventurers before the party to reach five stars on QuestRabbit. They went to sleep rather than sign.

Cadwyn explains the truth: the Rabbit Rating measures public trust. At five stars, a party can sign for the commons. Every good deed brought the party closer. Then the Counting House notices the room has been opened, and Compliance Officers arrive to escort someone to the signing—the old heroes, or the new ones.

Background — DM Only

Clause 77-B of every QuestRabbit Contractor Agreement appoints any five-star party as Representatives of the Commons: authorised to sign on the world’s behalf. Harriet Hopwell built QuestRabbit believing she was helping adventurers; Tallis Vend built Clause 77-B into it. Ninety-four years ago the Last Five-Star Party reached five stars, saw the Final Contract and fled into Room 303.

Ysolde Fenn cast a time-stop sleep on the room. As long as they sleep, they cannot sign—and nobody else can reach five stars while their rating stands. Their rating has begun to decay. The party’s is rising. The Ledger needs only one five-star party.

The Long Rest Inn is Nine Circles’ hotel chain; its staff are bearded devils in bellhop uniforms.

Running This Mission

  • The reveal is the point. Let Cadwyn tell it, slowly.
  • Each of the four sleepers can be woken separately; each has a different reaction.
  • Make the corridor fight feel like an escort mission gone wrong: the Compliance Officers are not trying to kill, they are trying to take.
  • The Twist—passing signature authority—is a real decision.

Threads In and Out

  • In: QuestRabbit and Pip; the party’s Rabbit Rating; the Sleeper (Plane Inn, “Late Checkout”).
  • Out: the party knows what it is; Harriet Hopwell can help if persuaded; the Last Five-Star Party’s allegiance for @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S24]{S24}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Pip slides the contract across the table without looking at it. It is printed on heavy black card with silver letters, and he holds it by the very corner as if it might bite. “I’m not supposed to say,” he says. “But they said you’re the only ones qualified. On the whole system. Nobody else can even see the job.” His ears flatten. “Who else has ever been qualified for something like this?”

The Long Rest Inn is plush and very quiet: thick red carpets, brass lamps, a lobby that smells of lavender and sulphur. The bellhops are bearded devils in pillbox hats who carry luggage as if it weighed nothing and smile with too many teeth.

The third floor corridor ends at a door unlike the others. The paint is a century out of date. The brass numbers—3 0 3—are green with age. On the handle hangs a card, its ink faded to brown: DO NOT DISTURB. Dust lies on the carpet before it in a perfect drift, untouched, a finger deep.

DM Description

The night manager briefs the party: ninety-four years; no room service; housekeeping has tried everything; three staff aged forty years in a second trying to force the door. The door is held by a time-stop field.

Getting in requires a counterspell or dispel magic against 9th level (DC 19), a wish, or Cadwyn’s song (from the side contract Authenticity Guaranteed): singing it through the keyhole makes the field part.

Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.cadwyn-lark]{Cadwyn Lark}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.tomas-brand]{Tomas Brand}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.ysolde-fenn]{Ysolde Fenn}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.hark]{Hark}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S16|The Last Five-Star Party’s Rating Card]{The Last Five-Star Party’s Rating Card} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S16|The Last Five-Star Party’s Rating Card]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The room is frozen in a single moment. A candle on the nightstand burns with a flame that does not flicker. Dust hangs in the air in a sunbeam from a window that shows a sky ninety-four years old. And on the beds and chairs, four people sleep.

A half-elf with a lute across her chest, her lips still parted mid-song. A grey-bearded human in a paladin’s plate, sitting upright in a chair with a sword across his knees. An old woman in star-embroidered robes, a wand slipping from her fingers. A lean ranger curled by the window, one eye half-open, as if keeping watch even in sleep.

On the dresser, in a frame, is a QuestRabbit rating card: five gold stars.

DM Description

The Last Five-Star Party. They can be woken one at a time (touch them and speak their names; each wakes with a gasp).

Cadwyn Lark (bard) wakes first and best: she understands immediately and starts talking. Tomas Brand (paladin) wakes reaching for his sword. Ysolde Fenn (wizard) wakes furious: waking ends her spell, and she is very old now. Hark (ranger) wakes silently and is already at the window watching for what will come.

Features of the Area

The frozen candle
Starts burning once Ysolde wakes; when it gutters, the Counting House knows.
Dust in the air
Falls all at once when Ysolde wakes.
The rating card
Five stars, dated ninety-four years ago.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.cadwyn-lark]{Cadwyn Lark}. Warm, wry, quick; a storyteller who has had nearly a century to rehearse this.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.tomas-brand]{Tomas Brand}. Grave, honourable, guilty: he wanted to stay and fight.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.ysolde-fenn]{Ysolde Fenn}. Sharp, imperious, frightened of how old she has become.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.hark]{Hark}. Silent; speaks only to warn.

Checks & Roll Requests

Waking a sleeper gently[[/check skill=med dc=13]] @FWCheck[S16|skill=med dc=13|Wake a sleeper gently]{Request}They wake without panic.
Recognising them[[/check skill=his dc=16]] @FWCheck[S16|skill=his dc=16|Who are these people?]{Request}The Last Five-Star Party: the most famous adventurers of the last century, vanished.

Developments

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Cadwyn sits on the edge of the bed, strokes the strings of her lute once to see if they still work, and looks at you for a long moment.

“How many stars?” she asks. When you tell her, she closes her eyes. “Then you’re nearly there. I’m sorry. Let me tell you what the stars are for.”

DM Description

Cadwyn explains: the Rabbit Rating measures public trust. Every five-star review, every rescued cat, every grateful client is a vote. At five stars, under Clause 77-B, a party becomes Representatives of the Commons and can sign for everyone. The Final Contract needs that signature. Ninety-four years ago it was theirs. They saw the contract and chose to sleep rather than sign or be made to sign.

She tells the party what they saw at the Counting House (the AGM; their names on the line). And she says: “Every good deed you did brought you closer. That’s the cruelty of it. It was meant to.”

The four will testify to this: the Five-Star Testimony, the Receipt.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Every door along the corridor opens at once. From every room step figures in grey suits with grey faces and lanyards with no names, carrying clipboards. At the far end of the hall, the lift chimes, and something enormous ducks out of it: a towering figure of ledger-grey stone with an abacus for a chest, its beads clicking.

“Representatives,” says the Senior Auditor, in a voice like a vault door. “Your escort has arrived.”

DM Description

The Counting House sends four Compliance Officers and a Senior Auditor to escort “the Representatives” to the signing. They will take whichever five-star party they can—the old heroes or the new ones. The Long Rest Inn’s bellhop devils join them (staff obey corporate).

The Officers try to grapple and carry; anyone grappled and carried to the lift is taken to the Counting House (they return, shaken, an hour later—unsigned this time, because the Final Contract isn’t ready). The Last Five-Star Party fights beside the party if woken: but they are ninety-four years out of practice (each has half hp).

When it is over, Ysolde Fenn sits down heavily on the stairs, her robes grey with dust, and laughs without humour. “Well,” she says. “We’re awake now. That was the only thing we were good at—being asleep.”

Cadwyn looks at the four of them, and then at you. “There’s one more thing we can do,” she says. “We can give you our stars. All of them. Or we can keep them, and go back to sleep, and stand in your way.”

DM Description

The Last Five-Star Party can:

Go back to sleep (Ysolde can recast the spell once). Their rating stands; the party’s cannot reach a full five—but the Ledger will find a way (S20).Pass their signature authority to the party. The party becomes the only Representatives—and gains the old heroes as allies and witnesses for S24.Refuse to pass it and fight beside the party as equals.

Optionally, the Sleeper’s dream (Plane Inn, Room 13) can be entered from here—a vision of the Third Place.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS17 · Act IV
Grade / LevelPlatinum · Level 14
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-03]{Starkfucks} (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-04]{Arcane Beverage International})
Session length1–2 sessions; an eerie exploration and a fight on scaffolding over nothing
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S17|Scene 1 — The Way In]{Scene 1 — The Way In} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-retail-12-ikea-mimic]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S17|Scene 2 — The Grey Café]{Scene 2 — The Grey Café} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-36-third-place-grey-cafe]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S17|Scene 3 — The Concepts]{Scene 3 — The Concepts} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-36-third-place-grey-cafe]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S17|Scene 4 — The Construction Site]{Scene 4 — The Construction Site} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-37-third-place-construction-site]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S17|Scene 5 — The Site Office Folio]{Scene 5 — The Site Office Folio} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-37-third-place-construction-site]{map}
Key NPCsHealing, Courage, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.knight]{Foreman Gerrit Hask}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-04.controlled-by]{Ulth’Arabica}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S17]{The Third Place Folio}

Synopsis

ABI, reeling from S11 and S12, still needs contractors, and QuestRabbit hires the party on autopilot. Or Healing itself leaves a donut hole on the party’s pillow with a note: “Help.” Starkfucks is building a branch in the Third Place.

The Third Place is grey: a café that goes on forever, with tables of lost things arranged by acquisition date. The party finds items from their own past—taken by the Ledger as “onboarding consideration” when they signed their first QuestRabbit agreement. Every hour, the grey takes a proper noun.

In the grey live the exiled concepts: Healing, Weekends, Courage, Sleep and Rest. ABI’s crews are building a Starkfucks around a pillar of compressed concepts, overseen by a thrall of Ulth’Arabica. In the site office is a Folio listing everything in the Third Place. Writing “owned by nobody” beside a name frees it—at a cost in blood.

Background — DM Only

The Third Place is where Creation & Company keeps what it owns but does not use: concepts, places, people, small treasured things. It is not home, not work: the place between, drained of colour and name.

ABI’s “Branch 1 of ∞” is an attempt to make the Third Place profitable—to sell coffee to everything that has been forgotten—by grinding concepts into bricks. Ulth’Arabica watches through its thrall, the site foreman Gerrit Hask.

If Healing was freed in S12, it has been sheltering the others and knows a hidden exit to Plane Inn’s Room 13, where the Sleeper waits.

Running This Mission

  • Drain colour from your descriptions as the session goes on. End in greyscale.
  • The proper-noun save is a player-facing horror: players pick which name they lose. Write them down.
  • The concepts are gentle, frail and funny. Courage hiding is a joke that becomes moving.
  • The Folio choice is a resource problem: hit points for freedom.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Healing (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S12]{S12}); ABI after @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11]{S11}; the Sleeper (“Late Checkout”); IKEA Mimic (“Assembly Required”); Dungeon Donuts (“The Hole Problem”).
  • Out: Ulth’Arabica has seen the party; the Board considers the party a threat; concept boons for @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S24]{S24}; the chase in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S22]{S22}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

You wake to find a donut hole on your pillow: a small, perfect sphere of fried dough, dusted with sugar, still warm. Beneath it, a scrap of grey paper in very faint handwriting, as if written by someone with almost no strength left.

Help.

Within the hour, QuestRabbit sends an automatic job offer: Starkfucks Real Estate, Platinum grade, pocket-dimension site clearance. Pip has added a note at the bottom: “I didn’t send this. The system did. I don’t like it.”

There are three ways in. In the IKEA Mimic showroom, the back of a flat-pack wardrobe named GRÅVÄRLD opens onto nothing. In the storeroom of a Dungeon Donuts, there is a crack in the wall the exact shape of a donut hole. And on Corporate Row, overnight, a new Starkfucks door has appeared on a blank wall: grey, with a sign reading BRANCH 1 OF ∞ — COMING SOON.

Whichever you choose, the moment you step through, the colour drains out of you like water from a sink. Your clothes go grey. Your skin goes grey. Your voice sounds further away.

Choose an entrance (or let the party). Each leads to a different edge of the grey café: the wardrobe to the furniture district (lost homes), the donut crack to the concepts’ refuge, the Starkfucks door to the construction site.

It is a café that goes on forever. Grey tables, grey chairs, grey cups on grey saucers, in rows that vanish into a grey haze in every direction. There is no counter. There is no barista. There is only the faint smell of coffee that has gone cold, and the sound of a spoon stirring somewhere far away.

Every table holds things. A child’s wooden horse. A wedding ring. A letter tied with string. A pair of boots. A key. Each has a small grey card beside it, and on each card, a date and a word: ACQUIRED.

DM Description

The tables are arranged by acquisition date. Searching the right era, each character can find something of their own: a toy, a letter, a keepsake, a memory, taken by the Ledger when they signed their first QuestRabbit agreement as “onboarding consideration”.

Retrieving one’s own item grants inspiration and restores one proper noun lost to the grey. It also makes the item’s colour return—a single point of colour in all that grey.

pages.name: Scene 3 — The Concepts
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-36-third-place-grey-cafe]{The concepts’ table}
When: Deeper in
Present: Healing, Weekends, Courage, Sleep, Rest
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S17|The Concepts’ Table]{The Concepts’ Table} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S17|The Concepts’ Table]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

At a table a little apart from the others sit five figures who are not quite people. One is thin, kind and very tired, with gentle hands: Healing. One is slumped with its head on the table, wearing slippers: Weekends. One is asleep in its chair, breathing slowly: Sleep. One, translucent and stiff, sits very still as if it has been told to: Rest. And under the table, trembling, hiding behind a chair leg, is Courage.

Healing looks up and smiles at you. “You came,” it says. “I hoped. That was the last of my hope.”

DM Description

The concepts explain in soft voices: they were bought and stored here. Without them, the world has had less of each—less rest, worse sleep, shorter weekends, fragile courage. ABI is grinding the others into bricks for its pillar.

Healing is grateful (and weak, if not freed in S12). Weekends is exhausted. Sleep dozes and talks in its sleep. Rest was sold by Nine Circles. Courage asks the party to lend it some: any creature that does gains advantage on saves against being frightened for the rest of the mission—and Courage comes out from under the table.

Playing the NPCs

Healing. Gentle, generous, frail. If freed in S12 it knows the hidden exit to Plane Inn, Room 13.
Courage. Terrified—the joke is the point. Becomes brave when someone is brave for it.
Weekends. Groans; wants a lie-in; surprisingly good at stalling time.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Comforting Courage[[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S17|skill=per dc=14|Lend Courage some of your own]{Request}Courage stands; advantage vs. fear for the mission.
Waking Sleep[[/check skill=med dc=15]] @FWCheck[S17|skill=med dc=15|Rouse Sleep (gently)]{Request}Sleep tells you, sleepily, where the site office is.

Lines to Steal

Healing: “You came. That was the last of my hope.”
Courage: “I’m not hiding. I’m… strategically elsewhere.”

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Out of the grey rises scaffolding: a skeleton of timber and iron around a pillar of something that glows faintly—a hundred colours pressed so tight they look like grey. Stone golems in hard hats lay bricks cut from it, one by one, building the walls of a café. A sign on the scaffold reads: STARKFUCKS — BRANCH 1 OF ∞ — NOW HIRING (ETERNALLY).

On the top platform stands a man in a high-visibility tabard with a clipboard. His eyes are milky white. When he speaks, a second voice speaks beneath his—wet, vast and very old. “Contractors. You were supposed to clear the tenants.”

DM Description

A fight on scaffolding over nothing. The foreman, Gerrit Hask, is a thrall of Ulth’Arabica (knight statistics; the aboleth can cast dominate person through him once). Four stone golems are the construction crew. Two grey concept-eaters—wraith-like things that feed on concepts—guard the pillar.

Stopping the build means defeating or freeing Hask, toppling the scaffolding or reaching the site office.

The pillar
Compressed concepts; touching it shows a vision of everything the world has lost.
Cranes

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The site office is a portable cabin with a desk, a kettle, a calendar for a year that never happened, and a grey book open on the desk. It is a Folio: a page of the Grand Ledger, delegated to this site. Its lines run on and on, page after page: Healing — concept — held. Weekends — concept — held. The River Brande (upper) — place — held. Molly Fairweather’s first word — memory — held…

DM Description

Writing “owned by nobody” against a name frees it. Each line costs the writer 1 hit point per level of the thing freed—a concept counts as level 10 (10 hp), a place 5, a person 3, a memory 1. Hit points spent this way cannot be healed until the party leaves the Third Place.

The party chooses what to free with the time and blood they have. Each freed concept grants a boon usable once in S24: Healing (every creature regains 50 hp), Courage (immunity to fear), Sleep (one Compliance Officer falls asleep), Weekends (an extra round in the clause debate), Rest (a short rest in a moment).

If Healing was freed in S12, it knows a hidden exit that drops the party into Plane Inn’s Room 13, where the Sleeper waits.

The Twist

Healing, if freed in S12, has been sheltering the others and knows a hidden exit that drops the party into Plane Inn’s Room 13—where the Sleeper (“Late Checkout”) waits.

The Third Place Folio. A branch ledger listing every concept, place and life Creation & Company owns but does not use. Proof that the Company acquires far beyond any fair purpose.

Leverage +2 against ABI; each freed concept +1 Commons Tally.

@FWReceipt[S17|fw.item.receipt.S17]{Award Receipt & announce}

If the party…Then…
freed all five conceptsThe world gets better weekends, sleep, rest, courage and healing overnight—and the Board marks the party as a threat.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS18 · Act IV
Grade / LevelPlatinum · Level 14–15
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-04]{Gelatinous Cube} / @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-11]{Dairy Quean} (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-12]{Sweet Covenant Confectionery})
Session length1–2 sessions; a city crisis, a hag bargain, and an audience with something older than the gods
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S18|Scene 1 — The Crawling City]{Scene 1 — The Crawling City} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-38-crawling-city]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S18|Scene 2 — The Glamoured Farm]{Scene 2 — The Glamoured Farm} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-39-glamoured-farm]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S18|Scene 3 — The Deep Dairy]{Scene 3 — The Deep Dairy} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-40-deep-dairy]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S18|Scene 4 — Granny Quean]{Scene 4 — Granny Quean} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-40-deep-dairy]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S18|Scene 5 — The Mother]{Scene 5 — The Mother} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-40-deep-dairy]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-11]{Granny Quean}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.auntie-curdle]{Auntie Curdle}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-04]{Bettina Soft}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.the-mother-culture]{The Mother Culture}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S18]{Sample Zero}

Synopsis

Bettina Soft calls in hysterics: every cube in the Canal Street Creamery is humming the freezer’s lullaby, and the gelato is crawling out of the display. Across Brandmere, every Sweet Covenant shop is leaking. Desserts are going home.

Home is the Deep Dairy, beneath the Dairy Quean farm, where the Mother Culture—a primordial ooze, the starter of every dessert the Sweet Covenant ever sold—has woken. Granny Quean, the night hag who runs the Covenant, is trying to force Sample Zero, the first starter ever taken from the Mother, back into her to re-establish control.

The party herds the desserts through the city, bargains past Auntie Curdle at the glamoured farm, frees the workers taken by the Retention Clause in S03, and faces Granny Quean at the heart of the dairy. Then the Mother rises, and listens.

Background — DM Only

The Mother Culture was old when the first god woke. The Sweet Covenant’s founder—Granny Quean—stole a single starter from her, Sample Zero, and from it grew every gelato, donut, blizzard and cube in the portfolio. Granny kept the Mother asleep in the deep cold beneath her farm.

The Mother has woken because her children are being used up faster than ever: the Acquisition needs dessert in every corner of the Material Plane. She is calling them home. If Sample Zero is returned, she will be whole, and calm, and withdraw.

The Retention Clauses (S03) sent workers who “left” the Covenant down to the Deep Dairy to stir the vats forever.

Running This Mission

  • The Crawling City is slapstick horror: gelato oozing up gutters, donuts rolling like wheels, the city watch glazed and sticky.
  • Auntie Curdle is the hinge: desperate, funny, treacherous.
  • Granny Quean is charming and terrifying. Her offer—youth for service—should tempt.
  • The Mother should not be fought. Make her vast and patient. She listens.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Gelli, Bettina and Auntie Curdle (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03]{S03}); the CostCo-op samples (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S09]{S09}).
  • Out: the Sweet Covenant breaks; the Board convenes emergency sessions; Hal Grundy calls about the dragons (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S19]{S19}).

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Bettina Soft’s voice comes through the speaking-stone in a shriek, over a strange sound—a low, sweet, many-voiced humming, like a choir of jellies. “They’re all humming!” she cries. “Every cube! The lullaby! The one the freezer plays! And the gelato’s—oh gods—the gelato’s getting out of the display! It’s going down the drain! It’s going home, it says! How can gelato say anything?!”

pages.name: Scene 1 — The Crawling City
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-38-crawling-city]{Open battlemap}
When: Morning, city-wide
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-04]{Bettina Soft}, the glazed city watch, Gelli (if allied)
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S18|Sweet Covenant Continuity Alert]{Sweet Covenant Continuity Alert} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S18|Sweet Covenant Continuity Alert]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Brandmere is sticky. From every Sweet Covenant shop—Gelatinous Cube, Dairy Quean, Dungeon Donuts, Baskin Liches—desserts are pouring into the streets. Gelato oozes along the gutters in rivers of pistachio and raspberry. Donuts roll down the hills like cartwheels. A blizzard from a Dairy Quean drifts down Market Street, a small snowstorm with a spoon in it.

They all go the same way: down, toward the canals, toward the old docks, toward the farmland north of the city. And everywhere, softly, they hum.

The city watch is trying to stop them with swords. It isn’t working. Half the watch is glazed from Dungeon Donuts and keeps stopping to lick their blades.

DM Description

Run a city crisis in three short beats: the Creamery (Bettina, the humming cubes, Gelli if allied), Market Street (the blizzard and a crowd), the canals (where the desserts are heading).

The party can herd the desserts into the canals—they know the way home and will flow north through the old drainage to the Dairy Quean farm. Fighting them is pointless and messy. Gelli (if befriended in S03) can lead them, humming.

Features of the Area

Rivers of gelato
Difficult terrain; [[/save ability=dex dc=14]] @FWSave[S18|ability=dex dc=14|Don’t slip in the gelato]{Request} or fall prone.
Rolling donuts
Each round, roll [[/r 1d6]]: on 1–2, a donut stampede crosses the area (2d6 bludgeoning, [[/save ability=dex dc=15]] @FWSave[S18|ability=dex dc=15|Leap the donut stampede]{Request} halves).
The canals
Where the desserts go; the way north.

Calming Bettina[[/check skill=ins dc=12]] @FWCheck[S18|skill=ins dc=12|Calm Bettina down]{Request}She blinks, finally. She tells you about the farm.

Developments

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Dairy Quean farm sits on gentle hills north of the city: white fences, red barn, a pretty farmhouse with lace curtains, cows grazing that are slightly too perfect. And then the farmhouse flickers. For a heartbeat, where it stood is a sinkhole of churning cream, a hundred feet across, steaming with cold. Then it is a farmhouse again.

On the porch, in a rocking chair, sits a green-skinned hag in a frilled apron, knitting very fast. “Oh, it’s you,” says Auntie Curdle. “Thank goodness. I need protecting.”

DM Description

The farm’s glamour is failing: the farmhouse flickers into the sinkhole that leads to the Deep Dairy. Auntie Curdle (from S03) guards the way down. She is bargaining desperately: she’ll open the path in exchange for protection from Granny Quean, who blames her for the Mother’s waking.

She will betray the party to Granny if a better offer comes. If she sides with Granny in Scene 4, she fights.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.auntie-curdle]{Auntie Curdle}. Panicky, flattering, scheming, funny. Knits constantly (the knitting is a curse in progress). Will sell anyone for safety—including Granny, if the price is right.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The path spirals down through cold white rock into a cavern so large you cannot see its far wall. It is full of vats: vats the size of lakes, each brimming with living cream that moves slowly, as if breathing. Faces rise in the cream and sink again—faces of people, animals, things that never had faces—smiling, sleeping.

On walkways above the vats, workers in white overalls stir with long paddles, slowly, endlessly. Some have been stirring for years. One looks up as you pass, and you recognise the name embroidered on his overalls from a list you saw long ago: a Gelatinous Cube employee who “left”.

DM Description

The workers from S03’s Retention Clause are here, alive, stirring. Each freed worker is +1 Commons Tally. They are not chained—they are retained: the clause makes them unable to stop. A remove curse, the Retention Clauses Receipt, or a successful check frees one.

Ochre jellies guard the walkways (the vats’ “quality control”).

Features of the Area

The vats
Living cream; falling in: [[/save ability=con dc=16]] @FWSave[S18|ability=con dc=16|Resist the living cream]{Request} or be restrained and pulled under.

pages.name: Scene 4 — Granny Quean
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-40-deep-dairy]{The heart of the Deep Dairy}
When: Climax
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-11]{Granny Quean}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.auntie-curdle]{Auntie Curdle (if she turns)}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.black-pudding]{black puddings}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S18|Granny’s Offer]{Granny’s Offer} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S18|Granny’s Offer]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

At the heart of the dairy is a pool of cream wider than a town, glowing faintly blue from beneath. On a stone jetty above it stands a small, round, rosy-cheeked old woman in a frilled pinafore, holding a jar no bigger than a jam jar. Inside the jar something pale and alive turns slowly.

She is trying to pour it into the pool, and the pool is refusing: the cream pulls back from the jar like a child from medicine.

Granny Quean turns and smiles at you, the sweetest smile you have ever seen. “Visitors! Oh, how lovely. Come and help Granny, dears. Granny will make it worth your while.”

DM Description

Granny Quean (a night hag, 150 hp, casting as a 15th-level warlock: hold monster, dominate person, banishment) is trying to force Sample Zero back into the Mother to re-establish control. She offers each party member one day of their youth back per year they serve her.

If refused, she fights, with two black puddings rising from the pool and Auntie Curdle (if Curdle sided with her). Defeating or deposing Granny removes the Sweet Covenant’s Board vote.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-11]{Granny Quean}. Sweet, doting, and absolutely monstrous. Calls everyone “dear”. Never raises her voice. Her offers are real.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The pool rises. Not a wave: the whole pool, lifting, slow and enormous, a wall of pale living cream that fills the cavern from floor to roof. Faces swim in it by the thousand. And then every face turns to look at you, and the Mother Culture speaks—through the pool, through the vats, through the gelato in the canals and every donut in Brandmere, all at once, in a voice so deep you feel it in your teeth.

“…child. You hold my child. Give it back.”

DM Description

The Mother Culture will listen. Returning Sample Zero makes her whole and calm: she withdraws beneath the earth, taking her children, and the Sweet Covenant’s product lines collapse overnight. The Deep Dairy empties. The freed workers walk out.

Destroying her is possible (see the Bestiary) but ends every dessert in the world forever, and she is the oldest living thing the party will ever meet.

Keeping Sample Zero (refusing the Mother) is possible: she sinks, grieving, and the party keeps the Receipt. Either way, the Mother offers a gift: one drop of Sample Zero, which dissolves any written contract it touches (see Twist).

pages.name: Twist, Rewards & Aftermath
pages.html:
GM ONLY

The Twist

The Mother offers the party a gift: one drop of Sample Zero, which dissolves any written contract it touches. It can be used once in S24 to void any single clause without its Receipt.

Rewards

  • Bettina Soft’s grateful testimony; the freed workers; the Mother’s drop.
  • The Sweet Covenant’s Board vote is removed if Granny is defeated or deposed.

Receipt — @FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S18]{Sample Zero}

Sample Zero. The first starter taken from the Mother Culture. Proof that every product in Creation & Company’s portfolio began as something the Company never owned—and that nothing it holds is perpetual.Voids Clause 12 — Perpetuity in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.finalcontract]{the Final Contract}.

@FWReceipt[S18|fw.item.receipt.S18]{Award Receipt & announce}

Outcomes

If the party…Then…
returned Sample ZeroThe Mother withdraws; desserts vanish overnight; the party keeps a drop and a written record (the Receipt).
kept Sample ZeroThe Mother sinks, grieving; desserts remain, wild.
destroyed the MotherNo desserts, anywhere, ever. A heavy cost.

Forward

  • With ABI wounded and the Sweet Covenant broken, the Board convenes emergency sessions.
  • Hal Grundy of CostCo-op calls QuestRabbit: the dragons must meet in person.

Next mission: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S19]{S19 — Executive Membership}

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS19 · Act IV
Grade / LevelPlatinum · Level 15
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-67]{CostCo-op} (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-10]{The Hoard Syndicate})

Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S19|Scene 1 — Seven Invitations]{Scene 1 — Seven Invitations}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S19|Scene 2 — Catering]{Scene 2 — Catering} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-retail-11-costco-op-warehouse]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S19|Scene 3 — The Meeting]{Scene 3 — The Meeting} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-41-crucible-dragon-boardroom]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S19|Scene 4 — The Motion]{Scene 4 — The Motion} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-41-crucible-dragon-boardroom]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S19|Scene 5 — The Vote]{Scene 5 — The Vote} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-41-crucible-dragon-boardroom]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.hal-grundy]{Hal Grundy}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-10.controlled-by]{Auntie Vermillia}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.aurum]{Aurum}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.frostmother-ysk]{Frostmother Ysk}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.old-tar]{Old Tar}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.grandmother-slate]{Grandmother Slate}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.pyrrhax]{Pyrrhax}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S19]{The Board Minutes}

Synopsis

Hal Grundy, sweating, explains: the Counting House requires a quorum of the Hoard Syndicate’s owners to ratify its vote in the Final Acquisition. If the dragons don’t show, the Hoard’s vote defaults to Tallis Vend. If they do, the party gets a chance to speak.

The party delivers seven invitations—each a short scene: a riddle with Aurum, a bluff with @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.dragon-twin-one]{Dragon Twin One} and @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.dragon-twin-two]{Dragon Twin Two}, a gift for Frostmother Ysk, a legal notice for Old Tar. Grandmother Slate insists on seeing the party’s Rabbit Rating; Auntie Vermillia, the chair, must be persuaded to attend at all.

Then the party caters the meeting in the cleared CostCo-op warehouse—with dragonroot hidden in the gravy, if they dare—and moves that the Hoard Syndicate withdraw from the Final Acquisition. Robert’s Rules of Order among apex predators.

Background — DM Only

The Hoard Syndicate is seven ancient dragons who bought into Creation & Company for a share of everything. They have voted by proxy—through Auntie Vermillia—for four centuries, because dragons do not attend meetings. Hal Grundy has the bylaws: an in-person meeting overrides every proxy.

Each dragon has a grievance: Old Tar resents Vermillia; Aurum hates the whole business; Frostmother Ysk wants her youngest back from the Hoots & Owlbears farm; the Twins (Verdigris and Azhure) want whatever the other doesn’t; Grandmother Slate respects stars.

Dragonroot (@FWLink[Item|fw.item.magic.03]{Dragonroot}): each dose binds one dragon to whatever it says during the meeting.

Running This Mission

  • Seven invitations is a lot—run three or four in full and summarise the rest.
  • The meeting is a skill challenge with a parliamentary procedure. Hand out the Agenda.
  • Track votes openly on a board. Four carry the motion.
  • If Vermillia loses, she attacks; the others will not help her if the vote was fair.

Threads In and Out

  • In: the CostCo-op vault and Hal Grundy (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S09]{S09}); Pyrrhax (“Delivery Territory”, Dragon Express); Kessik’s royalty debt (“Finger-Lichin’ Good”); the Five Colours receipts.
  • Out: the Hoard’s proxy for @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S23]{S23}; dragons fly to the Golden Tusks in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S21]{S21}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Hal Grundy is sweating so hard his lanyard is wet. He has a binder under one arm, as thick as a paving slab, and he opens it on your table to a page flagged in red. “Bylaws,” he says. “Section forty. An extraordinary meeting of the executive board, in person, overrides all standing proxies.” He swallows. “They’ve never come. Four hundred years. If they don’t, their vote goes to the Chairman by default. If they do…” He looks at you. “You get to speak. I need seven invitations delivered. Personally. To seven ancient dragons. Please don’t be eaten. I’d have to do the paperwork.”

pages.name: Scene 3 — The Meeting
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-41-crucible-dragon-boardroom]{The CostCo-op boardroom (warehouse floor)}
When: Noon
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-10.controlled-by]{Auntie Vermillia, Chair}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.aurum]{Aurum}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.frostmother-ysk]{Frostmother Ysk}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.old-tar]{Old Tar}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.grandmother-slate]{Grandmother Slate}, the Twins, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.compliance-officer]{a Compliance Officer observer}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S19|Agenda]{Agenda} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S19|Agenda]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

They come one by one, and the warehouse shakes with each arrival. A wind of fire through the loading bay: Auntie Vermillia, red and vast, wearing reading glasses on a chain. A gleam of gold: Aurum, already scowling. Frost spreads across the floor: Frostmother Ysk. A reek of the marsh: Old Tar. Twin shadows, green and blue, arguing as they land. And last, quietly, a silver dragon so old her scales are white, who looks at each of you in turn and counts your stars.

Vermillia lowers herself into the chair at the head of the table. She bangs a gavel made from a giant’s thighbone. “This extraordinary meeting of the Executive Board is called to order. Who moves?”

In the corner, a grey figure with a clipboard writes everything down.

DM Description

Robert’s Rules of Order among apex predators. Every dragon has a grievance (see Scene 1). Each speaks once on any motion. Insults are permitted; eating members is not (Section 12).

The Compliance Officer observer records the result and may try to annul it on a technicality (see Scene 5).

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-10.controlled-by]{Auntie Vermillia}. Grandmotherly, imperious, ruthless. Chairs like a tyrant. Has voted for all seven for four hundred years and enjoyed it.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.aurum]{Aurum}. Disgusted by commerce; wants out; too proud to say so first.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.old-tar]{Old Tar}. Procedural, petty, delighted by points of order.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.grandmother-slate]{Grandmother Slate}. Kind, grave; votes with the stars.

The party moves that the Hoard Syndicate withdraw from the Final Acquisition. Debate is a skill challenge: each character speaks once, making a DC 18 check (Persuasion, History, Insight, Intimidation) aimed at one dragon. Each Receipt and Leverage point against the Hoard grants advantage on one check. Kessik’s royalty debt (“Finger-Lichin’ Good”) and the Five Colours receipts are especially potent; Four’s Collateral Tag (S09) shows the Company holds the Hoard’s collateral too.

A success wins that dragon’s vote. A dragon bound by dragonroot votes as it spoke. Pyrrhax votes with the party if they helped him in “Delivery Territory”.

For a long moment the warehouse is silent except for the slow breathing of seven dragons. Then, one by one, claws rise.

DM Description

Four votes carry it. If the motion carries, the Hoard Syndicate withdraws; Hal Grundy writes the Minutes with shaking hands.

If Vermillia loses, she attacks—ancient red dragon, in a warehouse. The others will not help her if the vote was fair; Aurum and Slate may even help the party. Her kobold loyalists (20 kobolds, 4 dragonshields) swarm from the kitchens.

The Compliance Officer tries to annul the vote (“the motion was moved by a non-member”): [[/check skill=per dc=18]] @FWCheck[S19|skill=per dc=18|Defend the vote’s validity]{Request} (advantage if the party signed up for real membership in S09!) or defeat the Officer to validate it.

@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S20|Scene 5 — The Final Contract]{Scene 5 — The Final Contract} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-43-counting-house-boardroom]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-01.controlled-by]{Tallis Vend}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.pip-ashworth]{Pip-copy}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.counsel-ixabeth-vorr]{Counsel Ixabeth Vorr}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-02.public-face]{Harriet Hopwell}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S20]{The Final Contract (Courtesy Copy)}

Synopsis

An embossed invitation arrives, addressed to each character by full name, with the Rabbit Rating printed beside it. The Franchise Below’s grey door now has a handle.

Beyond it is the Counting House. A receptionist who is Pip Ashworth—except it isn’t; it is a Pip from a Ledger-page, a copy made when Pip signed—gives directions. The lift stops at floors the party didn’t press: Acquisitions, Collateral, Human Resources.

In the Boardroom every director is present or represented. Tallis Vend welcomes the party. Counsel Ixabeth Vorr (if allied) moves for an audit; the party reads the Grand Ledger. Then Item 7: the Final Contract is read aloud. Thirteen clauses. The signing date is the night the Golden Tusks are lit. The party’s names are typed on the signature line.

Background — DM Only

The Counting House is Creation & Company’s headquarters: a building outside every plane, reached through the first shop. Its floors are filing systems for everything the Company owns. Its Boardroom seats the ten umbrella directors and the Chairman.

Tallis Vend needs the party to sign willingly—or as willingly as Clause 77-B requires. He is courteous, patient and certain. He has been waiting four hundred years; he can wait a few more weeks.

Veronique Salt, if CEO of Crown & Cleaver, sits on the Board. She is planning an Extraordinary General Meeting.

Running This Mission

  • Make it clear through Ixabeth or Pip-copy that attacking in the Boardroom is suicide.
  • Each floor is a short vignette of dread and dark comedy.
  • The Final Contract reading is a set piece: read the clauses aloud, slowly, from the handout.
  • End with the party escorted out holding a courtesy copy—shaken, informed, and with a plan.

Threads In and Out

  • In: the Staff Only door (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S14]{S14}); Ixabeth (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S13]{S13}); Harriet Hopwell (S16); every director the party has met.
  • Out: end of Act IV. Three things must happen: break the seal (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S21]{S21}), stop the delivery (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S22]{S22}), turn the Board (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S23]{S23}).

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The invitation is waiting on your pillow when you wake: heavy grey card, embossed, with your full name—your real, full name, including the parts you never use—printed in silver, and beside it, your Rabbit Rating in stars.

Creation & Company requests your attendance at its Annual General Meeting. Attendance is not optional; it has been pre-recorded.

At THAC0 Spell, Hollis Quench meets you at the cellar steps, very pale. “The grey door,” he says. “It’s got a handle now.”

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The grey door opens onto a lobby of grey marble that goes up further than you can see. Filing cabinets line the walls, floor to unseen ceiling, with ladders on rails. Somewhere above, quills scratch, thousands of them, like rain. At the reception desk sits a harengon in a QuestRabbit cardigan, ears drooping, typing on a typewriter with no paper in it.

He looks up, and it is Pip. It is exactly Pip. Except his eyes are grey, and he does not recognise you.

“Welcome to the Counting House,” says Pip. “You’re expected. You’ve always been expected. Lifts are on the left.”

DM Description

The receptionist is a Pip from a Ledger-page: a copy made when Pip signed his QuestRabbit contract. The real Pip is at home, alive. This one is gentle and sad and gives directions. If asked, he knows he is a copy. He warns the party, quietly, not to attack anyone in the Boardroom: “Nobody leaves who does that. They become furniture.”

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.pip-ashworth]{Pip-copy}. Gentle, sad, helpful, grey-eyed. Everything Pip is, minus hope. He would like to be told about the real Pip.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Boardroom is a round grey room with a round grey table and a window onto nothing. Every director is here, in person or by proxy. Veronique Salt in crimson—or Baron Cleave in black. A glass tank of murky water in which something vast and eyed turns slowly: Ulth’Arabica. Papa Morvhal, grandfatherly and skeletal. The boardroom table itself breathes—that is SKÜ. Lady Crit, flipping a coin that always lands on its edge. Duke Vellichor, folded into a chair too small. Zafirah of the Brass Keys, smoke for hair. Auntie Vermillia, or Pyrrhax sweating in her chair. Deus Maxwell, wings folded, writing a plot twist on a napkin. Granny Quean’s chair—dripping cream, or empty. And the Mother Culture’s chair, dripping or empty.

At the head of the table, a small, precise man in a grey suit rises, smiling, and offers you each a chair with your name on it.

“Welcome,” says Tallis Vend. “We have been so looking forward to this.”

DM Description

Tallis Vend welcomes the party graciously and runs the meeting with perfect courtesy. Items 1–6 are routine (minutes, dividends, a moment of silence for the Sweet Covenant’s seat if broken). Each director reacts to the party according to what the party has done to them: hostility, interest, fear, respect.

Veronique (if present) passes a note under the table (the Twist).

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-01.controlled-by]{Tallis Vend}. Small, precise, kind in manner, utterly certain. Never angry. He addresses each character by full name. He means everything he says.

Counsel Ixabeth Vorr rises from the Nine Circles delegation with a sheaf of papers and a silver pen. “Mr Chairman,” she says. “Under the Infernal Codex, Article Nine, I move for an audit of the Grand Ledger on behalf of the Representatives.”

Tallis Vend smiles, amused. “Granted. One minute each.” He gestures, and in the centre of the table, a book rises from nothing: grey, vast, its pages turning by themselves.

DM Description

If Ixabeth is allied, she moves for an audit; Vend grants it, amused. Each character may read the Grand Ledger for 1 minute. Each reader learns one true secret (DM’s choice—often a Receipt they missed, or where Tallis Vend’s weakness lies: Entry 1 has only one witness).

Harriet Hopwell, if persuaded (S16), confirms under oath that she did not write Clause 77-B, giving the party advantage on the Clause 77-B debate in S24.

“Item seven,” says Tallis Vend. “Acquisition of the Material Plane. Progress.” He lays a single document on the table and reads it aloud, in his small, precise voice, clause by clause. Thirteen clauses. The room is silent except for the scratching of quills.

At the end, he turns the document around so that you can see the signature line. Your names are typed there. Your full names. Beside each, a small box, and in each box, five stars.

“The signing,” he says, “will take place on the night the Golden Tusks are lit. Do you have any questions?”

Read the Final Contract aloud from the Courtesy Copy handout (or @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.finalcontract]{the Final Contract}). Then answer questions with Vend’s perfect courtesy. He will not be baited.

Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-16]{Grukka Sweetfang}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-13.public-face]{Marda Hobb}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.cornelius-gaff]{Cornelius Gaff}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-43]{Centurion Marcus Crustus}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-07]{Don Pescatore Brine}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S21]{The Broken Seal}

Synopsis

Grukka Sweetfang—the Golden Orcs manager who is honestly great with kids—finds the party at the Tankard & Tallow. She has the survey maps. She’s been noticing for years: the golden tusk signs outside every branch are aligned, ley-line perfect, across the whole continent. They are a seal.

On Acquisition Eve, at midnight, every tusk will light, and whatever is signed in the Counting House will be notarised for all reality. Three tusks are anchors: the Brandmere Grand Tusks, the Summit Tusks in the mountains, and the Drowned Tusks beneath the harbour. Break two, and the seal cracks.

The Tankard & Tallow becomes a war room. Marda Hobb, Grukka, the Codfather families, kobold tunnel-runners and every ally the party has made gather. Three hours until midnight. Three anchors. Go.

Background — DM Only

Clause 6 of the Final Contract requires the Instrument to be “sealed under the Notarial Seal of the Company and witnessed by the Golden Tusks at the appointed hour.” The Golden Orcs chain was built as the seal: every branch’s sign is a node; the three anchor branches hold it together.

Each anchor tusk is a Golden Tusk construct when disturbed—a 40-foot golden iron golem. Compliance Officers guard each.

Pizza the Hutt’s land (“The Hutt Below”) was meant to be a fourth, reserve anchor. If the party sided with Grubbo, the reserve doesn’t exist.

Running This Mission

  • Use real time in the war room if you can: 3 hours of game time, tracked on a clock.
  • Split the party only if your table enjoys it. Otherwise, allies handle one anchor while the party takes two.
  • Each ally group can hold, scout or distract one site. Tally them openly.
  • Midnight is the climax whatever happens: describe the tusks lighting across the continent.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Grukka (Golden Orcs); Marda and the Tankard (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S08]{S08}); the dragons (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S19]{S19}); “Tunnel Vision”, “Sleeping with the Fishes”, “The Hutt Below”, “Blizzard”.
  • Out: with the seal broken, Tallis Vend changes tactics. At dawn, Dominoancy’s diviners start screaming (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S22]{S22}).

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Grukka Sweetfang comes into the Tankard & Tallow with a crayon drawing from a child in one hand and a roll of survey maps under her arm. She is a big half-orc in a Golden Orcs polo shirt with a name badge that says GRUKKA — ASK ME ABOUT BIRTHDAY PARTIES. She spreads the maps on Marda’s table and pins the corners with tankards.

“I’ve been noticing for years,” she says. “The tusks. They’re all lined up. Every branch. Same angle, same height, perfect lines across the whole continent. I drew it out one night after a party.” She traces the lines with a thick finger, and you see it: a vast seal, drawn across the map in golden lines. “Midnight, tomorrow, they light them all at once. I think they’re going to stamp something.”

pages.html:
GM ONLY

When: Acquisition Eve — 9 p.m.
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-13.public-face]{Marda Hobb}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-16]{Grukka Sweetfang}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-07]{Don Pescatore Brine (the Codfather)}, kobold tunnel-runners, every ally

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Tankard & Tallow has never been so full. Every table is taken: Last Independents with their sleeves rolled up; Codfather families in dark coats, smelling of the sea; kobold tunnel-runners with lamps on their helmets; freed harvesters, freed workers, temple folk, old heroes, anyone who has ever shaken a hand with you. The fire roars. Marda Hobb stands behind the bar with her arms folded.

“Three hours,” she says. “Three tusks. Tell us where you want us.”

DM Description

A heist-planning scene. Lay out the three anchors and let the players assign allies. Each ally group can hold (keep reinforcements away), scout (advantage on the first check at a site) or distract (remove one enemy group) at one site. Typical allies:

Kobold tunnel-runners (if “Tunnel Vision” preserved the tunnels): the party emerges beneath the Grand Tusks unseen. Codfather families: water breathing for the Drowned Tusks. Dragons who voted with the party in S19: fly the party to the Summit in minutes. Last Independents: hold the streets. The Last Five-Star Party: take an anchor themselves.

Track the time: travel between sites takes an hour without help.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-16]{Grukka Sweetfang}. Cheerful, practical, enormous, very brave. Treats the plan like a birthday party for forty kids: logistics, snacks, nobody gets left behind.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-13.public-face]{Marda Hobb}. Quiet command. She asks each ally group to shake on their job.

pages.html:

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Grand Tusks stand in the heart of Brandmere, outside the city’s largest Golden Orcs: two curved golden tusks forty feet high, arching over the drive-thru like a gate. Tonight the square is cordoned off. Little Caesars Legion holds the perimeter in a shield wall three deep, torches burning. Two grey figures with clipboards stand beneath the tusks, waiting for midnight.

The gold hums. You can feel it in your teeth.

DM Description

If the kobold tunnels were preserved (“Tunnel Vision”), the party emerges beneath the sign unseen. If not, they fight through Little Caesars Legion lines: 12 veterans and 2 centurions (Crustus leads, honourable as ever; he will accept a challenge).

Disturbing the tusk animates it: a Golden Tusk construct. Destroying it—or prying its core gem loose—breaks the anchor.

Features of the Area

The cordon
Shield wall; formation +2 AC.
The tusks
The construct; its core gem is in the arch’s keystone ([[/check skill=ath dc=18]] @FWCheck[S21|skill=ath dc=18|Climb the tusk to the keystone]{Request}).
The drive-thru
Cover; a speaker that plays the Golden Orcs jingle on loop.
Kobold tunnels
Exits in the drains.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Prying the core gem[[/check skill=ath dc=20]] @FWCheck[S21|skill=ath dc=20|Pry the core gem loose]{Request} (or thieves’ tools DC 20)The anchor breaks without destroying the construct.
Challenging Crustus[[/check skill=per dc=17]] @FWCheck[S21|skill=per dc=17|Challenge Crustus to single combat]{Request}If he loses, the Legion withdraws.

Developments

  • One anchor broken.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 17: construct + 2 COs + 12 veterans + 2 centurions. With tunnels: construct + 2 COs only.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Summit Tusks belong to a Golden Orcs at the top of a mountain pass—a branch that serves nobody, out of a blizzard that never stops. The tusks glow gold through the snow. Ice coats everything. And on the restaurant roof, coiled around the sign, is a white dragon, young and furious, chained to the tusks by a golden collar.

DM Description

A mountain branch in a blizzard (Granny Quean’s, if the “Blizzard” contract wasn’t stopped). Dragons who voted with the party in S19 can carry them here in minutes; otherwise it’s a teleport or a very long night.

The young white dragon is chained to guard the anchor. It is Frostmother Ysk’s youngest, if she asked for it back in S19—freeing it (break the golden collar: [[/check skill=ath dc=19]] @FWCheck[S21|skill=ath dc=19|Break the dragon’s golden collar]{Request}) turns it against the construct.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Beneath the harbour, in the black water, there is a Golden Orcs. It sank with the old dock district a century ago and never closed. Its lights are still on, green and drowned. Its tusks glow gold through the murk. Through its windows, grey figures in waterlogged suits sit at desks, clocking in, clocking out, adding up columns that dissolve.

A pale figure drifts out of the dark toward you: a drowned man in a Crown & Cleaver suit, with a ledger tied to his ankle by a chain. “Cornelius Gaff,” he says, bubbles rising. “Former CFO. I asked about the Ledger. This way.”

DM Description

The Codfather families provide water breathing (or the party arranges it). Cornelius Gaff’s ghost (“Sleeping with the Fishes”) guides them. Drowned accountants (4 ghasts) still clock in. A kraken priest guards the anchor and calls the deep.

Underwater combat: disadvantage on most weapon attacks except piercing; fire spells don’t work.

Features of the Area

The drowned branch
Desks, tills, a drive-thru lane full of eels.
The tusks
Rising from the seabed.
The deep
Below; the kraken priest’s god listens.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.cornelius-gaff]{Cornelius Gaff}. Mournful, precise, still an accountant. He would like his death recorded properly.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

At midnight, across the continent, the tusks light. From every town and crossroads and service station, two arches of gold blaze up into the night, and lines of light leap between them, mile after mile, drawing a seal across the sky like a signature on a page.

And where the anchors are broken, the lines falter. The light gutters. With a sound like paper tearing—a sound every person on the continent hears at once—the seal cracks across the sky.

DM Description

If two anchors are broken, the seal cracks: Clause 6 is void when the Broken Seal is presented in S24. If only one is broken, the seal holds but is flawed: the party gains advantage on Clause 6’s debate check in S24 instead of voiding it outright. If none, the seal holds.

If the party sided with Grubbo in “The Hutt Below”, the reserve anchor doesn’t exist, and the seal cracks with one fewer anchor (only one needed).

A shard of golden tusk, still warm, is the Receipt.

Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S22]{The Undelivered Order}

Synopsis

Madame Olive Aspire bursts into the Tankard & Tallow with her hair on end. “It’s you. You ordered it. You haven’t yet, but you will have. You did.” Every diviner in Dominoancy has foreseen one pizza order ending the world. It printed at every branch at once. It is the Final Acceptance of Offer, in the party’s names.

With the seal broken, Tallis Vend needs the party’s acceptance delivered before the signing—and Clause 7 requires delivery “in good time and in good condition.” The courier is Rook, Dominoancy’s best, compelled by prophecy. Her route crosses four planes: the Third Place, Pandemonium, Avernus, and the Counting House’s loading bay.

The party gives chase. At the last door, Rook is sobbing; the prophecy compels her. The party can take the pizza by force, persuade her to break fate, or eat it. An order consumed cannot be delivered.

Background — DM Only

Dominoancy is Probability Brands’ divination pizza chain: every order foreseen, every delivery on time, guaranteed by fate. Lady Crit, its controller, lost a wager to Tallis Vend and is bound to deliver.

Rook is a courier who has never missed a delivery. She is foresighted—she sees every move a heartbeat before it happens. She is freed by any creature offering her a delivery she’d rather make.

Every ally and boon the party has gathered can matter here: freed concepts in the Third Place, harvesters in Pandemonium, Vellichor and Ixabeth in Avernus.

Running This Mission

  • Run each leg as a short chase with 3–4 rounds of checks and one complication.
  • Track Rook’s lead in “threshold steps”: if she crosses a threshold before being caught, she reaches the next plane.
  • Rook is not a villain. She is a victim of foresight. Make her sympathetic.
  • Eating the pizza should feel like a feast, a memory and a victory.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Olive Aspire (Dominoancy); freed concepts (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S17]{S17}); harvesters (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11]{S11}); Vellichor and Ixabeth (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S13]{S13}).
  • Out: the contract can no longer be accepted in the party’s name; Veronique calls the Extraordinary General Meeting (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S23]{S23}).

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The door of the Tankard & Tallow bangs open at dawn and Madame Olive Aspire stumbles in, still in her Dominoancy apron, her hair standing straight up as if she has been struck by lightning. Her eyes are white from rim to rim. She points at you with a shaking finger.

“It’s you,” she says. “You ordered it. You haven’t yet, but you will have. You did.” She sits down hard on the floor. “Every diviner in the shop is screaming. One order. One pizza. And then everything is owned.”

pages.name: Scene 1 — The Ticket
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-pizza-02-dominoancy]{Open battlemap}
When: Dawn
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-42]{Madame Olive Aspire}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.rook]{Rook (departing)}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S22|The Order Ticket]{The Order Ticket} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S22|The Order Ticket]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S22|Olive’s Route (foreseen)]{Olive’s Route (foreseen)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S22|Olive’s Route (foreseen)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Every Dominoancy in Brandmere is in uproar. Order printers chatter out the same ticket, over and over, in every branch at once, spilling streamers of paper across the floor. The diviners at the ovens are on their knees, hands over their ears, seeing the same thing. The ticket reads: ONE (1) LARGE — FINAL ACCEPTANCE OF OFFER — DELIVER TO: THE COUNTING HOUSE — CUSTOMERS: and then your names.

Out in the yard, a lean woman in a Dominoancy jacket swings onto a delivery broom, a pizza box strapped to her back. She looks at you across the yard, and there are tears on her face. “I’m sorry,” says Rook. “I already saw you try.” And she is gone.

DM Description

Burning a copy of the ticket does nothing; the original is in Rook’s bag, inside the box. Olive Aspire can foresee the route: Brandmere, the Third Place, Pandemonium, Avernus, the Counting House. She gives the party a head start on each leg (advantage on the first check).

The party needs a way to follow: Olive knows each threshold (a Dominoancy oven that opens into the Third Place; the Bean There portal to Pandemonium; a Seven-Eleven Hells stockroom to Avernus).

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-42]{Madame Olive Aspire}. Foresees everything except her own divorce. Frantic, funny, brave. Speaks in mixed tenses.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Through the oven and into the grey. The café again, endless tables, the cold-coffee smell. And ahead, weaving between tables at impossible speed, a smear of Dominoancy red on a broom, the only colour in the world.

DM Description

A chase through the grey café. Freed concepts from S17 can slow Rook: Weekends stalls her (she loses a round), Sleep makes her drowsy (disadvantage on her next check), Courage lends the party advantage, Healing restores them. Four quicklings of the Brass Keys (Counting House couriers) run interference.

Each round, each pursuer makes a chase check; three successes before Rook crosses the threshold (three rounds) catches her—briefly. She uses foresight to slip away, but loses the lead.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The wind hits you like a wall. The tunnels howl. The terraces are half-burned or half-harvested, depending on what you did here—and on the terraces, if you freed them, stand harvesters in grey sacking who have come back to tend what is left. They see you and start shouting, pointing down a side tunnel: “That way! The red one went that way!”

DM Description

The howling wind-tunnels, now half-harvested (S11). Freed harvesters shout directions (advantage on chase checks). The wind carries away anything not held tight—including, possibly, the pizza: each round, Rook makes a check to hold onto the box; if she fails, it tumbles and the party can catch it (an opportunity to end the chase early).

Pandemonium’s madness still applies.

Red sky, red earth, a road of iron across a burning plain, and on the road, a toll booth: a little striped hut with a barrier pole, manned by devils in high-visibility tabards. A sign: AVERNUS — NINE CIRCLES TOLL ROAD — ALL DELIVERIES SUBJECT TO INSPECTION. Rook is ahead, slowing for the barrier.

DM Description

Duke Vellichor’s territory. If allied (S13), his devils form a roadblock at the toll booth and stop Rook cold. If not, they join the chase for their own reasons (they want the order too, as leverage).

Ixabeth Vorr can file an injunction against delivery: [[/check skill=per dc=20]] @FWCheck[S22|skill=per dc=20|File an injunction against the delivery]{Request} (advantage with the Infernal Due-Diligence Report). If it succeeds, the barrier comes down and Rook must stop for inspection.

Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.rook]{Rook}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.senior-auditor]{a Senior Auditor at the loading bay}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S22|The Undelivered Order]{The Undelivered Order} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S22|The Undelivered Order]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The loading bay of the Counting House is grey concrete and a single grey roller door, with a Senior Auditor standing beside it holding a clipboard, its abacus-beads clicking. Rook has stopped in front of it. She is shaking. The pizza box is in her arms. She is sobbing.

“I don’t want to,” she says. “I’ve seen it. I’ve seen what happens after. But I have to. I’ve never missed one. I can’t miss one.” She looks at you. “Please. Do something I haven’t seen.”

DM Description

The party can:

Take the pizza by force: Rook (assassin with foresight: advantage on everything, attackers have disadvantage) and the Senior Auditor fight.Persuade her to break fate: Rook is freed by any creature offering her a delivery she’d rather make (a letter home, a gift for her mother, a pizza to an orphanage). [[/check skill=per dc=18]] @FWCheck[S22|skill=per dc=18|Offer Rook a delivery she’d rather make]{Request}.Eat it. An order consumed cannot be delivered. The Last Slice tastes like every meal the party ever shared. (Twist.)

The Senior Auditor tries to sign for the order: if it touches the box, it counts as delivered—protect the box.

SituationRollResult
Keeping the box from the Auditor[[/check skill=ath dc=18]] @FWCheck[S22|skill=ath dc=18|Keep the box from the Auditor]{Request}The box stays undelivered.

Synopsis

Veronique’s card arrives: “Six votes. Bring them. I’ll bring the room.” She has requisitioned an Extraordinary General Meeting of Creation & Company to remove Tallis Vend as Chairman. Proxies must be lodged in person.

The party tallies what they have: directors turned, destroyed or bargained with across the whole campaign. Then they choose the director they have not yet dealt with and run a compressed version of that umbrella’s Platinum contract—one strong scene, one fight—as the final push.

In the Boardroom, directors step forward to hand the party a slip of paper, or refuse. Compliance Officers try to annul proxies. If six seats are gone from Vend, the motion carries. Vend smiles: “You may remove the Chairman. You cannot remove what owns itself.” He walks to the Signing Room.

Background — DM Only

The Board has eleven seats besides the Chair. Removing the Chairman requires six seats voting against him (or vacant). Seats can be turned (a proxy given to the party), removed (the director destroyed or deposed), or bargained.

Common sources (from the spine and side contracts): Papa Morvhal (phylactery or “Papa’s Back”), Lady Crit (“The Big Game” or Loaded Dice), Duke Vellichor (S13 report or “Closing Time”), the Hoard (S19), Deus Maxwell (“The Final Twist”), Crown & Cleaver (Veronique, if Cleave is gone). Removed seats: ABI (“The Reservoir”), ARC (“The Showroom”), Sweet Covenant (S18).

Veronique will betray the party if they have no Leverage against her: she tries to take the Chair herself.

Running This Mission

  • Do the vote count with the players before the session—or as Scene 1, on a big board.
  • The Last Holdout is a compressed Platinum contract. Keep it to one scene and one fight.
  • The meeting is theatre: each director stands, speaks once, and hands over a proxy or refuses.
  • End on Vend’s line and the empty room.

Threads In and Out

  • In: everything. Every Receipt, Leverage point and director.
  • Out: the signing room is open. Tallis Vend waits with the Quill (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S24]{S24}).

DM Description

Directors step forward one by one to hand the party a slip of paper, or refuse. For each contested vote, a Compliance Officer tries to annul the proxy (“improperly lodged”)—defeating that Officer, or out-arguing it, validates the proxy.

Wavering directors can be persuaded with a check; Leverage gives advantage. Commons Tally allies watching grant +1 to each check (to a maximum of +5).

Tallis Vend rises. He straightens his grey cuffs. He smiles, quite kindly.

“You may remove the Chairman,” he says. “You cannot remove what owns itself.” He walks to a small grey door at the back of the Boardroom you have never noticed before, and opens it. “I’ll be in the Signing Room. Take your time.”

Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-01.controlled-by]{Tallis Vend}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.pip-ashworth]{Pip Ashworth}
Receipt—

Synopsis

There is no hook. The door is open. There is a table, a contract, a quill and a small grey man who has been waiting four hundred years.

Tallis Vend offers tea and explains, calmly and persuasively, that he will be a very good owner—no war, no hunger, everything managed. Then the Clause Debate: each round he reads a clause aloud, and a character presents the matching Receipt and argues. Success burns the clause off the page; failure lets him make a Ledger Entry.

When six clauses are voided, Vend stands, and the room becomes the whole Counting House. He cannot be killed while Entry 1 stands. When every clause is void, the Ledger falls open to Entry 1. The party presents the First Entry and says—any words will do—“We witness you.” Tallis Vend becomes a clerk in a grey suit: mortal, four hundred years old, and very tired. Then the Quill remains, and the signature line.

Background — DM Only

The Final Contract has thirteen clauses (77-B and 1–12), each voided by a Receipt earned across the campaign. A clause with no Receipt requires a DC 25 argument, three Commons Tally witnesses, or a unique exception (Sample Zero’s drop, the Sleeper’s testimony, Ixabeth Vorr’s motion).

Tallis Vend is CR 24. With the Minutes of Removal he has no Legendary Resistance and no directors’ protection. He cannot die while Entry 1 stands: reduced to 0, he rewrites himself (once per clause remaining).

Entry 1 has only one witness. A second witness makes it an ordinary claim—and ends him as an owner.

Running This Mission

  • Gather every Receipt the party holds. Use the strips from @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.finalcontract]{the Final Contract} and burn (or tear) them at the table.
  • Let Vend be genuinely persuasive. His offer is the most dangerous thing in the campaign.
  • Every ally present can testify, including Pip—the real one (Twist).
  • Give the endings room. The epilogue is one short scene per franchise the party touched.

Threads In and Out

  • In: every mission.
  • Out: the world, in whatever form the party leaves it.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

There is no hook. The door is open.

Beyond it is a small grey room: grey walls, a grey carpet, a single window onto nothing. A desk. Two chairs. On the desk, a book bound in grey, open to a blank page, and on the page a document, and beside the document a quill. A teapot steams gently. And in the far chair, hands folded, sits a small, precise man in a grey suit, who rises as you enter and smiles as if you are old friends.

“There you are,” says Tallis Vend. “Tea?”

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Tallis Vend lifts the contract, clears his throat, and begins to read. “Clause seventy-seven B. Signature Authority.” He looks at you over the page. “Do you object?”

DM Description

Run as structured combat. Each round, Vend reads a clause aloud (order: 77-B, then 1–12). On their turn, a character presents the matching Receipt and makes an argument: DC 18 Persuasion, Insight, History, Religion or Investigation, depending on how they make the case. Leverage against the umbrella involved, an allied witness, or a relevant boon grants advantage. Success voids the clause: it burns off the page.

A clause with no Receipt requires DC 25, three Commons Tally witnesses, or a unique exception (Sample Zero’s drop; the Sleeper’s testimony; Ixabeth Vorr’s motion; Weekends grants an extra round).

On a failure, Vend makes a Ledger Entry (see his stat block): he writes a line that becomes true—a character’s weapon was never theirs; an ally “resigned”; a wound “was always there”. Four Compliance Officers act on his turn as his hands.

Clause list and Receipts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.finalcontract]{the Final Contract}. pages.name: Scene 3 — The Chairman Fights
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Tallis Vend stands, and the room stands with him. The walls fall away like the sides of a box. You are in the Counting House—all of it, every floor at once, filing cabinets stacked into towers, ledgers flapping like birds, quills scratching in their millions. Every cabinet is a weapon. Every Compliance Officer is his hand.

“I have been very patient,” says Tallis Vend.

DM Description

Use Tallis Vend’s stat block (CR 24; without Legendary Resistance if the Minutes of Removal were earned). He cannot be killed while Entry 1 stands: reduced to 0 hp, he rewrites himself to full (once per clause remaining).

Keep voiding clauses mid-combat: a character can use their action to present a Receipt and argue (as above). Each voided clause removes one of his rewrites.

The Senior Auditor and Compliance Officers fight for him. Concept boons from S17 (Healing: every creature regains 50 hp; Courage: immunity to fear; Sleep: one Compliance Officer sleeps; Rest: a short rest in a moment) are spent here.

Features of the Area

Filing-cabinet towers
Toppling one: [[/check skill=ath dc=20]] @FWCheck[S24|skill=ath dc=20|Topple a filing-cabinet tower]{Request}, 6d10 bludgeoning in a line—roll [[/r 6d10]].
Flapping ledgers
Each round, roll [[/r 1d6]]: on 1, a storm of pages; [[/save ability=dex dc=18]] @FWSave[S24|ability=dex dc=18|Dodge the page storm]{Request} or blinded until end of turn.
The open floors
Falling between them: 10d6—roll [[/r 10d6]].

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Voiding a clause mid-combat[[/check skill=per dc=18]] @FWCheck[S24|skill=per dc=18|Present a Receipt mid-battle]{Request}One rewrite removed.

Developments

  • When every clause is void, or Vend is at 0 with no clauses left: Entry 1.

Weak: Vend at 400 hp; 2 COs. Strong: all Legendary Resistances intact.

pages.html:

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Counting House folds back into the small grey room. The contract on the desk is a blank page, scorched at the edges. And the Grand Ledger, on its own, falls open to its very first page, where a single line in a small, precise hand reads:

Entry 1. Tallis Vend owns Tallis Vend, in perpetuity. Witnessed by: Tallis Vend.

Tallis Vend sits down in his chair. He looks at you, and for the first time, he looks afraid.

DM Description

The party presents the First Entry (S14) and says—any words will do—“We witness you.” A second witness makes Entry 1 an ordinary claim. Tallis Vend becomes a clerk in a grey suit: mortal, four hundred years old, and very tired.

What happens to him is the party’s choice: imprisonment, a job, mercy, the Clerk of the First Sale’s counter, a bowl of soup at the Tankard & Tallow.

Lines to Steal

Tallis Vend (mortal): “Nobody ever saw me before. I didn’t know it would feel like this.”

Developments

  • The Signature Line.
