pages.name: The Final Contract
pages.html:
The Final Contract

INSTRUMENT OF ACQUISITION No. 1

PROPERTY BEING ACQUIRED: Material Plane and associated subsidiaries. PURCHASE PRICE: Undisclosed. CURRENT OWNER: Disputed. PROPOSED NEW OWNER: Creation & Company. STATUS: Awaiting Signature.

The Final Contract is revealed in full at the Annual General Meeting (S20) and fought in the Signing Room (S24). Its thirteen clauses are listed below with the Receipt that voids each and the spine mission where that Receipt is earned. Photocopy this page, cut the clauses into strips, and burn them one by one at the table (or tear them, if your venue objects to fire).

Voiding a Clause

On their turn in the Clause Debate, a character who holds the matching Receipt presents it and makes an argument: a DC 18 check using Persuasion, Insight, History, Religion or Investigation, depending on how they make the case. Leverage against the umbrella involved, an allied witness, or a relevant boon grants advantage. A clause with no Receipt requires a DC 25 argument, three Commons Tally witnesses, or a unique exception noted in the spine (Sample Zero's drop, the Sleeper's testimony, Ixabeth Vorr's motion). On a failure, Tallis Vend makes a Ledger Entry (see his stat block).

ClauseTextVoided ByEarned In
77-B. Signature Authority The Signatories, having attained five-star public trust, are Representatives of the Commons duly appointed under Contractor Agreement Clause 77-B. Incident Report 77-B (original) S1 (L1)
1. Identity of Purchaser The Purchaser is Creation & Company, a lawful entity with continuous standing since its First Entry, wholly owned by its Chairman. The First Entry S14 (L11)
2. Consideration Full and adequate consideration for the Property has been rendered, in coin or in kind, and receipt thereof is acknowledged. The Wand-Mart Cost Ledger S10 (L8)
3. Free Consent All labour, service and custom provided to the Purchaser and its subsidiaries has been given freely and without coercion. The Loyalty Contracts S4 (L3)
4. Capacity of Signatories The Signatories are of sound mind, awake, and possessed of full capacity to bind the Commons they represent. The Five-Star Testimony S16 (L13)
5. Title to Subsidiaries The Purchaser holds good and unencumbered title to all subsidiaries, premises and franchise territories listed in Schedule A. The Unsigned Deeds S8 (L6)
6. Notarisation This Instrument is sealed under the Notarial Seal of the Company and witnessed by the Golden Tusks at the appointed hour. The Broken Seal S21 (L17)
7. Delivery Acceptance of this Instrument shall be delivered to the Purchaser in good time and in good condition. The Undelivered Order S22 (L18)
8. Collateral All collateral pledged by subsidiaries in security of this acquisition is present, complete and accounted for. Four's Collateral Tag S9 (L7)
9. Non-Infringement The Property does not infringe any mark, name, word or concept held under licence by the Purchaser. The Healing Deed S12 (L9–10)
10. Governing Law This Instrument is governed exclusively by the Company's Articles, and no other jurisdiction—mortal, divine or infernal—shall apply. Infernal Due-Diligence Report S13 (L10)
11. Disclosure All material facts concerning the Purchaser, its officers and its conduct have been disclosed to the Signatories. Gideon Tumble's Notebook S2 (L1–2)
12. Perpetuity The Purchaser, its holdings and this Instrument shall endure in perpetuity, and no part shall be subject to expiry or decay. Sample Zero S18 (L14–15)

pages.html:
DM Tables

Recurring Corporate Contract Types

Whenever the party visits a franchise, generate work from this table. Roll a d12 for the type (reroll a 12 on a d2: 1 Executive Protection, 2 Hostile Acquisition) or choose. The third column is the twist Corporate didn't mention.

#TypeWhat Corporate SaysWhat Corporate Didn't Say
1 Pest Control The pest is never what Corporate originally described. It's a former employee.
2 Delivery The destination is always considerably more dangerous than stated. The recipient doesn't know they ordered it.
3 Loss Prevention Recover stolen goods without discussing why they were stolen. The thief was the rightful owner.
4 Employee Wellness Locate employees who disappeared after raising workplace concerns. They're still working, somewhere.
5 Competitive Research Corporate espionage. The rival shares your client's parent company.
6 Brand Protection Stop embarrassing information becoming public. The information is a Receipt.
7 Procurement Retrieve magical ingredients from somewhere extremely dangerous. The ingredient is sentient and has opinions.
8 Customer Service Deal with customers employees cannot legally kill. The customer is right.
9 Franchise Expansion Clear whatever occupies desirable commercial property. The occupant has a lease older than the city.
10 Product Recall Recover an item before customers discover what it does. Someone already has, and they're organising.
11 Quality Assurance Consume something nobody at Head Office was willing to test. It tests you back.
12 Executive Protection Protect somebody whose decisions caused the current problem. The assassin is a Tally ally.
13 Hostile Acquisition Acquire a rival company. 'Hostile' may be interpreted flexibly. The rival would rather join the Last Independents.

Corporate Euphemisms

d12Corporate SaysIt Means
1 Unscheduled personnel reassignment Someone was eaten.
2 Customer retention event The customers can't leave.
3 Executive continuity initiative The CEO is undead.
4 Accelerated reduction in competitor market presence Murder.
5 Inventory shrinkage Something is eating the stock.
6 Legacy premises A haunted building.
7 Supply continuity alert A planar war.
8 Brand family A cult.
9 Growth opportunity You will probably die.
10 Voluntary overtime Binding infernal clause.
11 Rightsizing A cursed wish.
12 Synergy Two monsters merged.

McGuffin's Happy Quest Toys

Every McGuffin's meal comes with a toy. One in twenty is crucial to somebody's destiny.

d20Toy
1 A small brass key to a door that hasn't been built yet
2 A plastic knight with a real knight's soul inside
3 Half of a treasure map; the other half is in a different kids' meal
4 A spinning top that points at whoever is lying
5 A tin crown stamped 'Rightful Heir'
6 A figurine of a Five Wights brother (collect all five; there is a sixth)
7 A folded paper fortune that is always correct and always useless
8 A bouncy ball that bounces one second into the past
9 A toy briefcase that must not be opened
10 A sticker of the C&C sigil that can't be peeled off anything
11 A tiny rabbit that stamps one star on anything
12 A whistle only dragons can hear
13 A marble with a storm in it
14 A decoder ring that decodes corporate memos into plain speech
15 A wind-up gelatinous cube that absorbs one small object
16 A toy sword that is Chekhov's (it will matter later)
17 A pocket-size copy of the Contractor Agreement
18 A ring that makes you the protagonist for 1 minute
19 A snow globe of Brandmere with a figure in it that moves
20 A coupon for 'One (1) Destiny, Redeemable Once'

Franchise Complications

d20Complication
1 Team Deliverables arrive and claim the job
2 A Compliance Officer is taking notes in the corner
3 The client's parent company is also the villain's parent company
4 Corporate sends a 'motivational' memo mid-fight
5 It's the lunch rush
6 A health inspector (lawful neutral, CR 1) arrives
7 The manager is covering for Head Office
8 The monster has a union rep
9 All payment is in loyalty points
10 Veronique Salt is watching
11 A rival franchise offers double to fail
12 The contract was already completed—by the party—tomorrow
13 A Brandmere Crier reporter wants a quote
14 The only witness is a mascot
15 The job board updates: the pay has been halved
16 A customer loudly asks for the manager (it's the boss monster)
17 Wild magic surge (THAC0 leakage)
18 The building is being rebranded mid-mission
19 Everything on the premises is a mimic
20 Someone mentions the C&C sigil

Final Word

The monsters are dangerous. The dungeons are deadly. But nothing in the multiverse is more terrifying than Corporate.

INCIDENT REPORT 77-B

Location: THAC0 Spell flagship, cellar
Reporting: H. Quench, night manager
Staff member: Dobbs (line cook, nights)

At approx. 2 bells past midnight D. reported hearing a till ringing behind the iron door in the cellar. I told him there is no till down there. He went down. I heard him shout. When I got there the iron door was ajar and warm and D. was inside, laughing. He shouted back "It's still open! They're still serving!" Then the door closed. It has not opened since.

Head Office instructs this be filed as: "Unscheduled lower-kitchen personnel reassignment."

I am filing it as what happened.

C&C SUPPLY   H. Quench

pages.name: Tunnel Vision
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Tunnel Vision

FR-13 · Level 7 · Silver

An infrastructure audit at Krispy Kobold is really a survey of the kobold escape network beneath the franchises.

What Is Really Happening

Hoard Syndicate wants the tunnels mapped and filled. Forty runaway cooks use them as an underground railroad. The party's map can preserve an evacuation route that opens a hidden approach to the Golden Tusks in S21.

Scene 1

Tikka Glaze-Snout supplies a sanctioned map and asks for a complete tunnel plan. A successful DC 14 Investigation or Survival check notices that the supplied plan ends exactly where the warm air, pastry scent, and fresh footprints begin.

Run it as: Scene 1 — The Survey Order.

Scene 2

the party finds a kitchen, sleeping alcoves, and a hand-drawn branch map. The kobolds are frightened, not hostile. The shift foreman asks the party to report a cave-in that never happened. A DC 15 Persuasion check or proof of the escape network earns a guide.

Run it as: Scene 2 — The Living Route.

Scene 3

loyalists arrive with 12 kobolds, 4 winged kobolds, a scale sorcerer, and a guard drake. They fight to seal the route. The party can win them over with evidence that the tunnels are keeping workers alive, or disable the work crew and finish the map.

Run it as: Scene 3 — Fill or Preserve.

Outcomes and Campaign Effects

Payoff: 350 gp less 30%. Preserve the tunnels to gain a secret approach beneath the Brandmere Grand Tusks in S21. Destroy them and the party must enter through Little Caesars Legion lines. Leverage +1 against the Hoard Syndicate. Give the party the annotated map as the receipt.

pages.name: Papa's Back
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Papa's Back

CO-05 · Level 12 · Gold

Papa Morvhal asks the contractors to recover his missing phylactery before a hostile board faction turns his own immortality against him.

What Is Really Happening

The phylactery is hidden in the Charnel Kitchen's frozen soul archive. Papa wants it returned, but the archive also contains names of undead employees whose souls are being used as collateral. The party chooses between returning the lich's security, freeing the workers, or exposing the whole arrangement.

Scene 1

Papa makes the request over a meal he cannot eat. He admits the phylactery was taken after a hostile audit and asks the party not to involve the staff. Insight DC 15 reveals fear, not greed.

Run it as: Scene 1 — Family Meeting.

Scene 2

the mausoleum's cold rooms contain labeled soul jars and a false delivery manifest. Investigation DC 16 finds the phylactery inside a casket marked for disposal. Two wights and a frost-touched wraith patrol the aisles; loud combat risks cracking nearby jars.

Run it as: Scene 2 — Freezer Archive.

Scene 3

an auditor's strike team arrives while the party carries the phylactery. Papa's old family members demand that the workers' jars be opened before he receives his. The party can bargain, fight, or publish the ledger and let the staff decide.

Run it as: Scene 3 — The Return.

Outcomes and Campaign Effects

Payoff: protect Papa and return the phylactery to gain his proxy in S23 and Leverage +1 against the Restaurant Necromancy Group. Free the workers instead and gain Commons allies; Papa may still support the party if they return the phylactery after releasing them. The soul manifest is the receipt.

pages.name: The Reservoir
pages.html:
GM ONLY

The Reservoir

CO-04 · Level 16 · Platinum

Climb the Roastery Spire and shut down the Compliance source in Ulth'Arabica's reservoir.

What Is Really Happening

Every ABI drink contains a trace of Compliance. Thousands of customers will regain their own memories when the reservoir is drained, but the transformation will also expose everyone who signed a loyalty contract. Ulth'Arabica expects a boardroom negotiation and has prepared the tank for a siege.

Scene 1

customer memories return in fragments at the base of the Spire. Collect three signed testimonies or public records to prove the drink's effect; failures bring ABI knights who try to confiscate the evidence.

Run it as: Scene 1 — The Recall.

Scene 2

pass through three occupied floors: barista dormitory, contract archive, and pump station. The party can free ten thralls at a time or keep moving. Releasing workers gives them advantage on the final skill challenge, but raises the alarm.

Run it as: Scene 2 — The Climb.

Scene 3

Ulth'Arabica fights in a flooded reservoir with four chuul and ten thralls. The aboleth uses lair actions and legendary resistance; pumping stations can drain the tank in three successful DC 17 Arcana, Athletics, or tool checks. Destroying the pump keeps the fight underwater.

Run it as: Scene 3 — The Tank.

Outcomes and Campaign Effects

Payoff: freeing the reservoir removes ABI's Board vote in S23. Save the signed contracts to add Leverage +1; burn them to erase thousands of debts but lose the evidence. The vote removal is the reward, and the freed customers become Commons allies.

pages.name: The Showroom
pages.html:
GM ONLY

The Showroom

CO-06 · Level 14 · Platinum

A public launch at IKEA Mimic gives the party one chance to expose ARC's living furniture before it becomes a city-wide product line.

What Is Really Happening

SKÜ's showroom is a floor-by-floor prototype maze. The displays are mimics; their warranty cards are actually control contracts. The public demonstration begins while customers are inside, so a clean victory must protect them as well as destroy the production ledger.

Scene 1

the party gets a showroom map with three impossible room dimensions. DC 15 Perception spots a chair changing position when nobody looks. The salesperson insists this is an immersive customer experience.

Run it as: Scene 1 — Floor Plan.

Scene 2

rescue trapped visitors while navigating mislabeled doors. Each room presents a two-minute puzzle: match a part to its silhouette, follow an instruction sheet that lies once, or identify the one display that is not alive. A failed check costs time and lets the mimic crew reposition.

Run it as: Scene 2 — Assembly.

Scene 3

SKÜ activates a giant assembly mimic, two ropers, and four animated armors to protect the showroom's prototype ledger. The heroes can fight, sabotage the assembly line, or broadcast the original control contract to the crowd.

Run it as: Scene 3 — Product Reveal.

Outcomes and Campaign Effects

Payoff: destroy the production ledger and expose ARC's living furniture to remove its Board vote in S23. Capture the warranty contract to gain Leverage +1 against the Adventure Retail Consortium. Any civilians evacuated become Commons allies.

pages.name: Delivery Territory
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Delivery Territory

FR-45 · Level 7 · Silver

Negotiate with a young brass dragon courier and obtain proof that the Hoard Syndicate's delivery territory clauses bind more dragons than they admit.

What Is Really Happening

Pyrrhax wants to be free of his grandmother's contract and will trade a copy for safe passage. His local agent, a young brass dragon accountant, has the original in a route ledger. Auntie Vermillia's kobold staff can be persuaded that the contract is unenforceable.

Scene 1

Matteo Scorch sends the party to a hillside oven where the dragon courier makes deliveries. A DC 14 Persuasion or Deception check gets a private meeting; failure starts a chase across the roofline.

Run it as: Scene 1 — The Route.

Scene 2

the brass dragon's audit nest is protected by six kobolds. Their supervisor can be bought with a 100 gp “late delivery” fee or convinced that the contract makes them personally liable. The original route ledger lists every bound dragon.

Run it as: Scene 2 — The Ledger.

Scene 3

Pyrrhax meets the party at a roadside milestone. Give him the full contract, a copy, or use it to bargain for a public release clause. If the party refuses, he attempts to steal the ledger and flee.

Run it as: Scene 3 — The Choice.

Outcomes and Campaign Effects

Payoff: 700 gp less 30%. A copy of the contract gives Leverage +1 against the Hoard and advantage when inviting dragons in S19. If Pyrrhax is freed, he votes with the party and can carry them to S21.

pages.name: The Hutt Below
pages.html:
GM ONLY

The Hutt Below

FR-44 · Level 7 · Silver

Explore the reserve anchor tunnels beneath Pizza the Hutt before the party chooses whether the route is kept, sealed, or surrendered.

What Is Really Happening

The Hutt's basement is a buried palace-restaurant built around a fourth golden anchor. Grubbo knows that it is not a restaurant foundation; it is a load-bearing piece of Creation & Company's claim on the Material Plane. If the anchor is kept, it stabilizes the final seal. If it is removed, the seal cracks but the Hutt's land becomes free.

Scene 1

Grubbo offers access in exchange for a guarantee that the party will not put him back in the kitchen. His staff provide a grease-stained plan; a DC 15 Investigation check finds a hidden stair marked “reserve inventory.”

Run it as: Scene 1 — The Basement Door.

Scene 2

a flooded ballroom contains a gelatinous-cube grease trap, two animated statues, and a wall of old franchise deeds. The deeds show the reserve anchor was never part of the Hutt's contract.

Run it as: Scene 2 — The Buried Dining Room.

Scene 3

a golden iron golem wakes when anyone touches the tusk. The party can defeat it, decommission it with three DC 16 Arcana checks while a companion distracts it, or negotiate with Grubbo to surrender the land and leave the anchor intact.

Run it as: Scene 3 — The Anchor.

Outcomes and Campaign Effects

Payoff: preserving the anchor gives one extra stabilizing point in S24; removing it gives the Commons an independent route into the Counting House but reduces the final seal's stability. A signed deed returning the land to Grubbo adds a Commons ally. The sealed deed is the receipt.

pages.name: Late Checkout
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Late Checkout

FR-61 · Level 11 · Gold

The sleepers at Plane Inn's Room 13 have never checked out. The party must find the contract that keeps their dreams on the property ledger.

What Is Really Happening

The hotel uses a time-stop field to keep guests suspended. Healing, if freed in S12, knows the hidden exit into Room 13. A guest's dream is being used as collateral for a reservation that was renewed in perpetuity.

Scene 1

the party arrives at midnight and finds the lobby clock moving backward. The clerk will not admit Room 13 exists. A forged key, an old guest receipt, or a DC 16 Persuasion check gets the ledger from the night desk.

Run it as: Scene 1 — The Desk.

Scene 2

every door returns to the lobby unless the party speaks a guest's real name. The names can be found on forgotten luggage tags. A minute in the hall costs a day outside; failed checks add one fatigue complication, not a combat penalty.

Run it as: Scene 2 — The Hallway.

Scene 3

the Sleeper is a dream-fed guardian and two nightmare hounds. Break the contract seal with the guest receipt, a successful DC 17 Arcana check, or a clear statement that the guests revoke consent. If the party attacks first, the Sleeper fights to preserve the dream.

Run it as: Scene 3 — Room 13.

Outcomes and Campaign Effects

Payoff: release the guests and add Leverage +1 against Planar Hospitality; they become Commons allies and provide a route to the Counting House. Keep the contract for evidence and return later to the hotel. The original room ledger is the receipt.

pages.name: Authenticity Guaranteed
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Authenticity Guaranteed

FR-52 · Level 3 · Copper

A public song contest at Hard Bard Café has been stopped by a negative review and an injunction from Nine Circles counsel.

What Is Really Happening

The café's founder, Cadwyn, is the only person who can open a time-stopped door beneath Creation & Company. Nine Circles wants the song declared counterfeit so that the door stays sealed. The party can restore Cadwyn's reputation by proving the review was purchased or by performing the original song.

Scene 1

interview the critic, Cadwyn, and the café staff. A DC 13 Investigation check reveals the review was posted before the performance. The critic's invoice bears Counsel Ixabeth Vorr's seal.

Run it as: Scene 1 — The Review.

Scene 2

Cadwyn refuses to sing while the injunction remains. Persuasion DC 13, proof of payment, or an honest performance by a PC gets him on stage. The crowd becomes an ally if the party treats the song as a shared work rather than a product.

Run it as: Scene 2 — The Open Mic.

Scene 3

the original song opens the time-stop field for one minute. A summoned contract devil tries to seize the score. The party can protect Cadwyn, copy the song, or let him choose what to do with his own work.

Run it as: Scene 3 — The Door.

Outcomes and Campaign Effects

Payoff: Cadwyn's song can open the sealed room in S24; expose the fake review to gain Leverage +1 against Nine Circles. The purchased review and the signed performance ledger are receipts.
